articleTitle: Research on contact electrical life model based on action parameters and electromagnetic relay reliability prediction
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: Recent advancements have focused on extending the life expectancy and enhancing the reliability of electromagnetic relays. However, the existing electrical life models are specifically designed for certain relay types, limiting their applicability across models with similar structures and thus restricting their universality. This study proposes a new model, the equilibrium forc e-type electromagnetic relay electrical life model, which incorporates contact breaking speed as a critical input parameter, allowing it to theoretically adapt to various types of equilibrium force-type electromagnetic relays. The model development begins with an electrical life test to measure parameters such as contact breaking speed, number of electrical lif etimes, single arcing charge, and cumulative arcing charge. These parameters serve to establish a contact electrical life model. The study further involves generating batch virtual samples based on the initial distribution of product parameters, facilitati ng the input and output modeling through a virtual prototype. The integration of the virtual sample data with the contact electrical life model permits the estimation of product reliability. This research, by focusing on batches of different types of equilibrium force-type electromagnetic relays with identical structures, establishes and validates the model's efficacy within a specified stress range, thereby contributing to the broader application and understanding of relay reliability modeling.

articleTitle: Research on the degradation process and failure mechanism of high voltage DC contactor in electrical endurance experiment
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: The longer electrical lifespan and higher reliability of high voltage DC (HVDC) contactors have always been the requirements of the power distribution system. This paper carries out an electrical endurance experiment of a typical HVDC contactor under resistive load. Firstly, the typical waveforms of the contact voltage and coil current during the operation process are tested and presented. Then, the degradation trends of featured parameters such as pick-up time, release time, arcing time and contact resistance are extracted and analyzed. It is determined that the pick-up time and release time are the sensitive featured parameters for characterizing the degradation process of the contactor. The relationship between release time and arcing time are investigated. Furthermore, based on the variation trends of the pick-up voltage and the release voltage, it is discovered that the degradation of the opposing force is the root cause for the decrease in pick-up time and the increase in release time. Finally, the possible degradation and failure mechanisms of HVDC contactors are analyzed.

articleTitle: APF guided reinforcement learning for ship collision avoidance
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: With the accelerated melting of Arctic Sea ice, the research and application of Arctic shipping routes have also accelerated. Maritime transportation serves as the primary mode of transportation; however, transportation risks are substantial. The extreme weather conditions in the Arctic region elevate the likelihood of maritime accidents. To mitigate the risks associated with ships navigating through Arctic ice regions and to prevent collisions between ships and ice, this article proposes an APF-PPO algorithm for collision avoidance utilizing Artificial Potential Field (APF) guided reinforcement learning algorithms. The APF-PPO algorithm offers dual guidance in decision-making and reward. Specifically, during decision-making, APF guidance supplants random decision-making, and an APF reward function is devised to significantly reduce ineffective exploration in the early stages of reinforcement learning, thereby enhancing the convergence speed of the reward function. Based on the results of simulation experiments, the APF-PPO algorithm demonstrates the capability to empower intelligent ships to evade obstacles and navigate securely within intricate ice environments.

articleTitle: Cost-based importance genetic algorithm for system reliability optimization
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: As the counterpart to conventional reliability optimization problems (ROP), the cost minimization reliability optimization problem (CMROP) plays a critical role within the domain of ROPs. Given the escalating demands for product reliability, CMROP has emerged as a focal point in reliability optimization research. This area of study concentrates on enhancing system reliability efficiently while minimizing costs to meet specific requirements. This paper introduces a cost-importance-based genetic algorithm (CIGA) designed to enhance the efficiency of the cost-minimization reliability optimization model. The algorithm integrates a cost-based importance measure with a local search rule and a genetic algorithm. The validity of this algorithm is corroborated through its application to several typical system structures. Extensive numerical experiments are conducted to evaluate the performance of CIGA in comparison to traditional genetic algorithms (GA) and BIGA across five aspects of the solutions. The results demonstrate the superiority of the proposed algorithm in addressing cost minimization reliability optimization problems, showcasing its enhanced efficacy over the competing algorithms.

articleTitle: Remaining useful life prediction of rolling bearings based on TCN-LSTM
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: Rolling bearings are crucial components in mechanical systems, and accurately predicting their remaining service life holds significant practical importance. To tackle the shortcomings of conventional deep learning methods for predicting remaining useful life (RUL), which suffer from insufficient feature extraction and low prediction accuracy, especially regarding single short-term and single long-term dependent features. This paper introduces a residual remaining useful life prediction method for bearings, named TCN-LSTM-attention, which leverages CBAM attention alongside parallel Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) components. The method employs parallel TCN and LSTM network architectures for feature extraction, concurrently integrating the CBAM attention mechanism to weigh features across various dimensions. This approach not only captures a more comprehensive distribution of features but also amplifies the representation of critic al features, thereby significantly enhancing RUL prediction accuracy. Finally, to assess the efficacy of the proposed method, we conducted experiments using the PHM2012 rolling bearing datasets. The results demonstrate the method's robustness and generalization capabilities.

articleTitle: Simulation research of multi-physics field bidirectional interactive coupling of HSERS
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: The operational state of Hermetically Sealed Electromagnetic Relays (HSER) in the aerospace sector involves multiple physical processes, including mechanical, electrical, and magnetic phenomena. The efficiency and accuracy of traditional dynamic characterization methods, which rely on static data tables, are inadequate for meeting the demands of reliability analysis. T his paper introduces a meshless node flexible body model as the foundation of a multibody dynamics model. It establishes a real-time interaction channel between transient mechanical torque, electromagnetic force, and the shape and position parameters. Furthermore, the paper incorporates an implicit integration algorithm to address nonlinear contact and collision issues within the rigid-flexible coupling model, as well as a finite element numerical solution for the electromagnetic field derived from Maxwell's equations. A bidirectional interactive coupling computational model combining multibody dynamics and electromagnetic finite element analysis is developed. This model facilitates real-time coupling calculations and analyses of the dynamic characteristics of HSER in terms of mechanics, electricity, and magnetism. Additionally, a testing system for HSER’s electrical, temporal, and force parameters is constructed, and the test data from the principle prototype are compared with the analytical and computational results. The relative errors of the three types of parameters fall within the specified error range, confirming the validity of the method.

articleTitle: Research on the concept and parameter system of equipment support effectiveness
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: This article investigates the current state of support effectiveness both domestically and internationally, analyzing the gaps and deficiencies prevalent in domestic contexts. Building on this analysis, it introduces the concept and nuances of equipment support effectiveness. The key factors influencing equipment support effectiveness are delineated, alongside an exploration of the interrelationships and characteristics of each parameter. A hierarchical parameter system for equipment support effectiveness, comprising three layers and 22 parameters, is constructed. Additionally, three comprehensive parameters are thoroughly analyzed. This study serves as a valuable reference for further research into equipment support effectiveness.

articleTitle: Optimization of dense modal identification for aerospace components based on VMD
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: This paper focuses on aerospace engine parts, specifically addressing the challenge of recognizing structure-intensive modal frequencies, and proposes a novel method for extracting these frequencies. The research primarily investigates a signalf 2/f 1> 0.5 delay processing approach using a BP neural network. To mitigate the endpoint effect associated with the Variational Mode Decomposition (VMD) method, two signal extension strategies were evaluated: extreme point extension and BP neural network prediction extension. Simulation tests on various signal types demonstrated that the BP neural network prediction extension method provides the most effective suppression of the endpoint effect. Consequently, this method was applied to pre-process the delay of simulated signals, which were subsequently decomposed using the VMD algorithm. Experimental validation confirmed that this combined BP-VMD approach effectively extracts frequency information from signals, thereby enhancing the decomposition accuracy of the VMD algorithm.

articleTitle: Failure mechanism analysis and experimental study of tubular fuses for nuclear power plants
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: As a pivotal component within the instrumentation and control (I&C) system and the electrical infrastructure of nuclear power plants (NPPs), the fuse plays a crucial role in ensuring the safe and stable operation of NPPs. Consequently, a thorough analysis and exploration of the failure mechanisms underlying the tube fuses employed in NPPs were conducted in this study. This involved identifying sensitive stresses and performing reliability enhancement tests, including damp heat and steady-state unsaturated pressurized vapor tests, on the fuses. Through a combination of failure analysis and testing, the failure mechanisms of the selected fuses were verified. This research holds immense value for the operational maintenance of fuses in NPPs and for enhancing their inherent reliability.

articleTitle: A Chebyshev interval iteration-based multidisciplinary interval reliability optimization
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: The inherent uncertainty of parameters poses a significant challenge to multidisciplinary design optimization (MDO), especially when sample availability is limited and computational costs are high. This paper introduces a n ovel iteration-based methodology to address the multidisciplinary interval reliability optimization problem utilizing the Chebyshev interval method. Initially, Chebyshev polynomials are utilized to quantify interval uncertainty, followed by an analysis of the intervals of coupling variables in multidisciplinary systems using an iterative approach. Subsequently, an interval reliability index is introduced, based on the constraint interval, with a detailed description of the calculation process provided. Furthermore, interval order relations are employed to streamline the uncertainty optimization problems, allowing for the adjustment of the optimization objective according to the interval characteristics. Two numerical examples are presented to demonstrate the accuracy and practicality of the proposed method, which effectively enhances the reliability within a precisely defined constraint interval in multidisciplinary optimization under interval uncertainties.

articleTitle: Reliability modeling and analysis of k-out-of-n: F systems with self-healing components
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: For complex multi-component systems, which typically consist of multiple interconnected subsystems or components, reliability is crucial due to the significant losses that can result from failures. Multi-component redundant systems with self-healing properties are particularly valuable as they can utilize their inherent capabilities to mitigate or buffer impacts, thereby enhancing operational reliability. This paper draws upon mathematical reliability theory to examine a k-out-of-n system endowed with self-healing features. A reliability model that accommodates external impact environments is developed to explore its self-healing characteristics, complemented by a simulation algorithm for assessing system reliability indicators. Numerical examples are simulated and analysed using this algorithm, and a sensitivity analysis is conducted on select parameters to gauge their influence on system reliability.

articleTitle: Research on safety risk assessment of non-stop construction in civil aviation airport
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: Non-stop construction at airports encompasses numerous uncertain factors that can lead to various unsafe incidents. To scientifically assess the risks associated with non-stop construction activities, this study has conducted a comprehensive identification of risk factors through literature research, event analysis, and case studies. A risk assessment index system for continuous construction has been developed, encompassing four dimensions: human factors, machinery, environment, and management practices. The proposed risk assessment model aims to systematically evaluate the risks associated with uninterrupted construction

articleTitle: A multi-channel fault information bearing fault diagnosis method based on improved vision transformer
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: Bearings are crucial components of modern mechanical equipment and their failure can lead to equipment downtime, economic losses, and potential threats personal safety. Therefore, it is essential to carry out fault diagnosis of bearings. In this paper, Multichannel Signal Transformer (MST) model is employed for diagnosing bearing faults. Initially, a single vibration signal and two motor current signals are collected and combined into a multichannel signal. This multichannel signal is then used to train and test the MST model. The performance of the MST model is subsequently compared with that of an established one-dimensional CNN. The feasibility of the method is verified by comparing the accuracy and loss function values of the two models in fault diagnosis. Finally, the confusion matrix of the MST model for fault classification is analyzed, and the t-SNE visualization is performed on the features of the fully-connected layer. The results demonstrate that the MST model has a higher accuracy in fault diagnosis.

articleTitle: Failure data analysis for tracked vehicles under different environments using principal component analysis
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: Enhancing vehicle reliability is of paramount importance during the research and development phase, with reliability growth testing playing a crucial role in this process. Traditional reliability growth testing often treats vehicle failures under varying environmental conditions with uniform significance, overlooking the specific impacts these conditions may have on failure occurrence. This paper aims to illuminate the influence of environmental factors on vehicle failures. To explore the relationship between vehicle failures and the contexts in which they occur, Principal Component Analysis (PCA) was employed. The findings indicate that a diversified testing approach, which assigns different levels of importance to various testing scenar ios, is recommended. This approach is likely to yield a more nuanced understanding of vehicle performance and foster a more effective strategy for enhancing reliability.

articleTitle: Simulation and experimental research on transient temperature field of IGBT modules PWM inverter
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: Significant heat generation occurs during the operation of Insulated Gate Bipolar Transistors (IGBTs). This issue becomes more pronounced as IGBT modules advance to higher voltage and current levels, making thermal management increasingly challenging. This paper discusses the estimation of power losses in PWM inverters with IGBT modules, focusing on losses due to switching and conduction based on their control rules. A thermal management method using forced air cooling was designed and simulated. The results of the transient temperature field simulation demonstrated that the method could maintain the IGBT modules' working temperature within acceptable limits across all operating stages. A PWM inverter prototype with six IGBT modules was constructed and tested. The experimental results showed the good agreement with the simulation results. This investigation confirms that the electro-thermal model built according to SPICE is accurate and that the thermal management system, based on the IGBT modules' control rules, is suitable and effective.

articleTitle: Analysis of the outsourcing risk management mechanism adapted to the characteristics of scientific research according to the quality management system
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: Most universities have established a quality management system to meet the access requirements for scientific research projects and strengthen research quality management. Practical exploration in developing a quality management system tailored to university research has yielded some results. However, investigation and communication reveal shortcomings in using these systems to establish an effective outsourcing risk management mechanism suited to the unique characteristics of university research. There is a notable lack of effective monitoring of two significant risks: the illegal acquisition of res earch funds and the substandard quality of outsourced products. Addressing these issues necessitates leveraging the management methods inherent in quality management systems while considering the specific research characteristics of academic institutions.

articleTitle: An integrated multi-objective production scheduling approach considering mission reliability
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: In production transportation systems, such as mine production systems, the transportation component is a critical part of the production process, and its operational reliability significantly impacts the overall health of the production system. Tradit ional scheduling plans for these systems typically focus solely on transportation costs and total transportation volume, neglecting the influence of various factors in the transportation process. This oversight can affect the reliability of the final production task. Therefore, this paper incorporates the mission reliability of the production and transportation system into the scheduling decision-making process to propose a more reasonable production scheduling scheme. Firstly, the paper introduces the basis for production scheduling that considers mission reliability from the perspective of the material flow network. Secondly, it proposes a multi-objective integrated production scheduling method that incorporates mission reliability, using a hybrid simulated annealing-genetic algorithm. The effectiveness of this approach is verified through the scheduling of mine vehicles on a mine production line.

articleTitle: Joint optimization of serial system based on deep reinforcement learning
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: While the serial manufacturing system is a productive mode of production, rework and maintenance are inevitable aspects of real-world operations, and their promptness and effectiveness are crucial for both production effic iency and product quality. This study begins by analyzing the manufacturing system to understand the impact of unqualified work-in-progress (WIP) on the overall system. Maintenance tasks can enhance machine processing quality and reduce the production of u nqualified WIP items; however, they also increase maintenance costs, consume system resources, and decrease production output. Conversely, rework can lower manufacturing costs by converting unqualified WIPs into qualified ones, but processing unqualified W IPs can negatively impact machine quality, leading to further unqualified WIP production. To simulate and optimize the rework and maintenance process, thereby maximizing system production efficiency and product quality, this study proposes a combined optimization model based on the Double Deep Q-Network (DDQN) algorithm. Experimental findings demonstrate that the proposed DDQN algorithm offers significant practical value and a broad range of application prospects. It effectively optimizes rework and maintenance decisions, reduces the number of unqualified WIPs, lowers production costs, and enhances production efficiency.

articleTitle: Resilience evaluation of production system recovery strategy based on improved node importance
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: The problem of troubleshooting and repairing the production system is a key issue in restoring the productivity of the system as soon as possible after the system receives an external disruption. Based on such problem background, this paper focuses on the resilience assessment of recovery strategies for production systems and the determination of recovery sequences for failed machines. In this paper, a resilient recovery strategy for production systems based on improved node importance is used, where the node importance is determined by the minimum eigenvalue of the Laplace matrix corresponding to the deletion matrix. Then with the help of production line completion (Crp) to determine the priority of machine restoration on the repair branch line and thus obtain the maintenance decision indicator (Mdi), and according to the size of this indicator to determine the maintenance order of the damaged nodes, and finally apply the resilience triangle metric to evaluate the repair strategy. Through software simulation of different recovery strategies, comparative analysis shows that the recovery strategy based on improved node importance is more effective. This paper provides the theory in the field of recovery strategies after distribution and gives an idea for determining the order of repair of a faulty machine.

articleTitle: Methods of designing accelerated reliability verification tests for electrical energy meters based on Lomax distribution
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: Long test times and large sample sizes make it unaffordable for industries to conduct reliability verification tests on high-reliability and long-life products. Accelerated reliability verification tests have therefore attracted extensive attention worldwide and present significant challenges for the electrical energy meters industry. In this study, the failure rate of parameters of the exponential distribution is considered to obey a gamma distribution, which updates the Lomax distribution using conditional probability and applies it to describe the life of electrical energy meters. The reliability data from similar or historical electrical energy meters are synthesized to address the small sample problems encountered in reliability verificat ion tests. Based on the Lomax distribution, the operating characteristic functions for three indices, reliable life, failure rate, and average life, of the electrical energy meter are constructed. By introducing an acceleration factor, an acceleration equation for the electrical energy meter is developed based on the Lomax distribution. Accelerated reliability verification tests for the electrical energy meter are provided, taking into account the varying risk levels of different consumers. Validation research is conducted using examples, offering a novel approach for accelerated reliability verification tests of small samples, high-reliability, and long-life products. This study provides new insights for the accelerated reliability verification tests of small samples, high-reliability, and long-life products.

articleTitle: Probabilistic fatigue modeling using the strain energy concept
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: In the realm of structural integrity design, Notch fatigue analysis holds paramount importance. Despite its criticality, however, efficient fatigue models that seamlessly integrate notch and size effects remain elusive, making their development a highly sought-after pursuit, particularly in the design of vital components. Responding to this need, the current study presents a novel probabilistic fatigue model for lifespan evaluation. This model masterfully intertwines the weakest link theory with the strain energy (SE) concept, creating a harmonious union. To be precise, we introduce an innovative SE concept that seamlessly connects the experimental data pertaining to smooth specimens with the SE density of notched components, particularly within their critical damage zone. For the purpose of validation and an in-depth comparative analysis, we exploit experimental data from various alloys, each exhibiting unique geometrical configurations. The outcomes garnered from this rigorous examination indicate that our proposed model triumphs over the other two models, exhibiting remarkable accuracy. Additionally, the probabilistic curves provide an insightful and efficient depiction of the variance and scattering present in the experimental data, further strengthening the credibility of our findings.

articleTitle: A deep learning model-based framework for abnormal state monitoring of blast furnace heat loads
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: Heat load is a pivotal metric for ensuring the safety of blast furnace equipment in the iron and steel smelting industry, crucial for monitoring the heat exchange process of blast furnace cooling walls and evaluating the erosion of furnace bodies. The variability of blast furnace heat load, influenced by factors such as feed and oxygen supply, often results in abnormal internal furnace temperatures and drastic heat load fluctuations, hindering effective preventive maintenance. This study introduces a deep-learning-based framework for monitoring the abnormal state of blast furnace heat load. Initially, a two-stage data preprocessing method for monitoring ironmaking parameters is proposed: the first stage eliminates missing and abnormal values from the monitoring parameters, while the second stage employs a feature selection model to identify key influencing parameters. Subsequently, a real-time prediction model of blast furnace heat load is designed, integrating one-dimensional convolutional neural networks (1DCNN) with bidirectional long short-term memory (BiLSTM) networks. This model uses a two-layer 1DCNN for automatic feature extraction from time series data, complemented by a single-layer BiLSTM network to accurately predict anomalous trends in heat load. This deep learning framework has demonstrated superior performance in prediction accuracy and abnormal trend identification compared to alternative models.

articleTitle: Research on metro platform width calculation considering the effective length of the boarding area
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: Addressing the limitations in the platform width calculation formula specified in the Code for Design of Metro (GB 50157-2013), this study proposes a refined method that incorporates the effective length of the boarding area and accounts for the movement patterns of passengers across various functional zones and the characteristics of passenger flow distribution. This approach charts the fluctuations in passenger flow associated with the arrival and departure of trains, producing diagrams that delineate the evolving dynamics of passenger density in the waiting and distribution areas at different intervals. By calcula ting the maximum number of pedestrians at each stage and considering the effective length, the method determines the required widths for the boarding area, the disembarking passenger's walking area, and the distribution area. An application of this modified method at a transfer station in Chengdu Metro demonstrates a reduction in maximum passenger flow density by 26.5%, 23.5%, and 3.8% in the upward waiting area, downward waiting area, and distribution area, respectively, compared to the original formula. Notably, even though the width of the distribution area remains unchanged, the modified approach still yields a lower maximum passenger flow density, indicating that congestion in the waiting area influences the distribution area. This observation underscores that, in practical applications, when the width of the waiting area cannot accommodate the queue length, the queue may extend into the distribution area, suggesting that congestion in the waiting area can propagate to the distribution area. Consequently, while the two areas are physically distinct, they are not functionally independent.

articleTitle: Multi-objective optimization of maintenance policy considering the impact of degradation of spare parts on the system
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: Wind power has emerged as a prominent method of new energy generation in recent years. As the efficiency of generator operation becomes increasingly critical, the maintenance of these generators has come into focus. Wind turbines are often located in areas with high wind availability, and establishing warehouses for spare parts storage at these sites can substantially decrease both maintenance time and costs. However, the longevity of these spare parts can be compromised by soft failures, such as corrosion, which diminish their service life. This paper explores a novel inventory management strategy designed to mitigate the effects of soft failures on spare parts and reduce overall system maintenance costs. It is noted that the degradation process of components during storage and usage follows different distributions of soft failures. Moreover, the transition probabilities between different system states are modeled using a semi-Markov decision process. The study aims to optimize the system’s inspection intervals and preventive replacement thresholds to minimize the average cost rate of the system.

articleTitle: Research on quantitative analysis and evaluation method of complex safety mission for spacecrafts
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: The safety of spacecraft and astronauts is critically compromised by the complexities of aerospace missions, which include multiple products (fault) interactions, human-machine couplings, and temporal couplings among other hazardous events. Traditional safety analysis and evaluation methods for aerospace products have proven inadequate in addressing these complex mission requirements. Utilizing the probability risk evaluation method, this paper develops a dynamic safety analysis model based on the flight event chain, and it establishes a quantitative analysis and evaluation approach for complex safety missions. This method is applied to the fire response mission at the China Space Station as a case study. The application results demonstrate that the dynamic safety quantitative analysis and evaluation method can effectively quantify the probability of hazardous events, dynamically reflect the state of the aircraft system, accurately identify vulnerabilities, and contribute to ensuring the development of quality and safety standards of aerospace models.

articleTitle: Method for determining reliability requirements of airborne structural health monitoring system
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: The airborne structural health monitoring system is a critical component of civil aircraft, primarily used to monitor the sta tus of aircraft structures. Establishing reasonable reliability requirements is essential for ensuring the smooth execution of tasks while significantly reducing usage, maintenance, and support costs, all within the framework of meeting the system's efficiency requirements. In this paper, based on the characteristics of the system, a procedure for demonstrating reliability requirements is presented. The reliability index at the system level is demonstrated using the Monte Carlo modeling and simulation method. The reliability index of the optical fiber demodulation instrument is demonstrated considering the constraints of safety and economy, which is significant for determining the reliability requirements of the airborne structural health monitoring system.

articleTitle: The effect of the blade damage on the dynamic characteristics of a centrifugal pump fluid
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: Due to prolonged operation, centrifugal pumps often experience wear and erosion on their blades caused by impurities and debr is impacting at high rotational speeds. To investigate the effects of blade damage on the dynamic characteristics of centrifugal pumps, a numerical simulation model based on the fluid dynamics of a centrifugal pump has been developed. The SST k−ω turbulence model is employed to characterize the flow field within the pump. The results indicate that damage to the blades leads to increased inhomogeneity and instability in the pressure and velocity fields within the flow field, particularly pronounced at the volute and outlet. Such conditions can diminish the pump head and overall efficiency. This study provides valuable numerical insights for fault diagnosis of centrifugal pump blades, as well as for their optimal design.

articleTitle: Research on real-time adaptive adjustment method for HSER stable manufacture and consistent quality
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: Hermetically sealed electromagnetic relays (HSER) are critical components within aerospace applications, particularly in power supply and communication systems, and thus have stringent reliability requirements. To enhance the quality consistency across different batches, there is a significant need for a production line that is capable of real-time adaptive adjustments. This paper analyzes the manufacturing process of a typical HSER model, identifying the initial pressure of the contact system as the primary control target using single-factor analysis. A dynamic model of the contact system is developed through virtual prototype simulation, and the Taguchi method is utilized to simulate the large-deviation data of the key process. Subsequently, a rapid calculation model is constructed using the Kriging method. A key parameter collection platform for the contact system is also established to enable the real-time acquisition of critical process data. Real-time adjustment strategies based on parameter design and tolerance design methods are provided to address three potential types of deviations in real-time Cpk. These strategies are implemented to analyze and adjust the production line, restoring the Cpk of the initial pressure from 0.60 under extreme conditions back to 1.33, thereby achieving quality stability. The effectiveness of these adjustment methods is thus validated.

articleTitle: Boiler pipe life analysis method based on mate-rial fatigue analysis and operating parameter correction
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: The fatigue stress of metallic materials is the most direct and precise metric for quantifying material degradation and pipeline integrity. However, in practical industry, obtaining continuous, extensive, and timely technical supervision of metals presents a significant challenge. Consequently, meeting the accuracy requirements for pipeline life prediction is difficult. This article proposes a boiler pipeline life analysis method based on material fatigue analysis and running parameter model correction. Firstly, a stress life analysis model is constructed using experimental data on pipeline metal materials, geometric parameters, strain parameters, and fatigue process physical quantities. Subsequently, the information parameter method is employed, utilizing data such as operating status parameters, including temperature and pressure, to refine the model. Finally, four experiments are conducted using technical supervision data and operating data from boiler pipelines and bending tube weld metals. The analysis results closely align with actual outcomes, demonstrating that the life analysis method proposed in this article is viable and can serve as a reference for future studies.

articleTitle: A novel adaptive coevolution based multi-objective robust optimization strategy
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: Multi-objective optimization addresses engineering design problems with multiple objectives, often encountered in practical engineering, which typically involves various sources of uncertainty that can significantly impact design performance. To account for these uncertainties, robust design methodologies have been developed to achieve solutions that are both optimal and resilient to uncertainty. However, performing robustness analysis in the context of robust design, particularly when consider ing interval uncertainties, can be extremely time-consuming. To address this issue, a new algorithm is proposed in this paper, which is named Adaptive Coevolution-Based Multi-Objective Robust Optimization (AC-MORO). This method employs an adaptive approach to determine the neighborhoods between the robustness analysis problems associated with candidate solutions. In contrast to the conventional approach of analyzing the robustness of a single candidate solution at a time, the proposed meth od performs a simultaneous robustness analysis of multiple candidate solutions, utilizing the information obtained from their respective neighborhoods. To demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed algorithm, a series of tests and evaluations were conducted on six benchmark problems.

articleTitle: The study on optimization of overspeed test of steam-driven auxiliary water supply pump in nuclear power plant
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: The steam-driven auxiliary water supply pump, utilized within the Auxiliary Water Supply System (ASG) of nuclear power plants, is classified as nuclear safety level-3 and RCCM-2, marking it as a critical sensitive component and a specialized safety facility. This pump is pivotal, particularly when the main feedwater system fails, as it is designed to activate promptly and dissipate the residual heat from the reactor core, thereby directly influencing the safety of the unit. Periodic testing of this pump is crucial and significantly impacts the duration of the unit’s overhaul. Currently, a mechanical overspeed test is conduc ted in each fuel cycle to verify the pump’s overspeed protection function. The success rate of this test directly affects the overha ul period of the nuclear power plant. To enhance the reliability of the steam pump and minimize its impact on the safe operation of the unit, this paper explores the optimization of the mechanical overspeed test for the steam-driven auxiliary water supply pump.

articleTitle: A modified model for fatigue life prediction with stress gradient
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: Mechanical components are subjected to variable amplitude loads under operational conditions, leading to a stress concentration phenomenon that can create a high-stress gradient in the critical regions of these components. This high-stress gradient significantly influences the lifespan of mechanical components. In this research, considering the effect of the stress gradient, a stress gradient factor is proposed and subsequently incorporated into the SWT (Smith-Watson-Topper) parameter model. The modified model's efficiency and accuracy were validated using three categories of experimental data from notched components made of 7075-T651, 1Cr11Ni2W2MoV, and GH901 materials. It shows that the modified model provides superior life prediction outcomes.

articleTitle: Yet another least squares estimation in NHPP-based software reliability models with grouped data
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: The present paper concerns yet another least squares estimation in nonhomogeneous Poisson process (NHPP)-based software reliability models. As Ishii et al. (2012) pointed out in the analysis of software fault-count time-domain data, since the ordinary least squares (OLS) estimation is irrelevant to the probability law of the underlying NHPP, its applicability to estimate the model parameters as well as the quantitative software reliability is rather questionable. We consider similar but somewhat different least squares estimation methods for the software fault-count time-interval data, called the group data, and compare their predictive performances with the OLS estimation and the common maximum likelihood (ML) estimation. In numerical illustrations with eleven parametric NHPP-based software reliability models, it is shown that both the OLS estimation and the ML estimation could not always provide the best predictors.

articleTitle: Area segmentation based on UAV performance differences
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: Collaborative search is pivotal in obtaining battlefield environment information in future combat scenarios and has emerged a s a focal area of research in the domain of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) task planning. The Entropy weight-TOPSIS algorithm is initially utilized to effectively address the UAV performance evaluation challenge. This paper introduces a Non-Equal Area Segmentation Algorithm based on Moving Feedback (NEASA-MF), which incrementally approximates the expected area and delineates precise segmentation lines. This algorithm allows for the search area to be partitioned into multiple sub-areas of varying sizes based on the comprehensive performance of the UAVs. Consequently, UAVs exhibiting superior performance can alleviate the search burden of those with lesser capabilities. Simulation results affirm the efficacy of the NEASA-MF algorithm in segmenting areas for both convex and concave polygons, validating its utility in strategic UAV deployment.

articleTitle: Outlier anomaly assessment method based on the attention-enhanced LOF algorithm: a case study of loose particle detection signals in aerospace relays
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: Quality and reliability are essential in aerospace systems. Aerospace relays, as critical components, must pass stringent loose particle detection tests before factory dispatch. This paper introduces the Attention-Enhanced Local Outlier Factor (AE-LOF) algorithm, an advancement of the Local Outlier Factor (LOF) algorithm, specifically designed to improve the detection of anomalies in loose particle detection signals from aerospace relays. This novel algorithm incorporates an attention mechanism to enhance the outlier sensitivity traditionally hindered by the LOF algorithm's dependence on the k-value, which often results in underestimation of anomaly degrees. The AE-LOF algorithm refines the LOF calculation method by integrating outlier evaluation metrics, thus broadening the detection range and capturing more significant outliers. Experimental results demonstrate that AE-LOF exhibits greater sensitivity in detecting outliers, effectively enhancing the detection and recognition of loose particles within aerospace relays. This method proves to be of substantial practical value in the field of aerospace loose particle detection.

articleTitle: Research on the development and application of fire real-time risk model for nuclear power plants
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: Nuclear safety is the lifeline of nuclear power development, and Risk Monitor (RM) is a crucial tool for the safety analysis of nuclear power plants. RM has been extensively researched and applied by various research institutes and nuclear power plants. Currently, mainstream research and applications primarily focus on the development and use of internal event probabilistic safety analysis (PSA) within RM. However, there has been limited research on developing fire PSA models to reflect the real-time impact of changes in plant configuration on fire model logic and risk. The fire protection design and operation of a nuclear power plant must meet the overall risk objectives of the plant, making fire risk management an essential aspect of plant risk management. Therefore, developing a real-time risk modeling approach for fire is necessary for a more comprehensive and in-depth application of risk guidelines. This paper focuses on the M310 unit and studies the fire PSA model based on the benchmark fire PSA model. It also examines the fire PSA technical elements within the RM development method, addressing key elements such as initiating events, operation/standby trains, ignition frequency, and other modeling components. Furthermore, an example is provided to illustrate the importance of considering real-time fire risk comprehensively when performing real-time risk configuration and management in a power plant. This research lays the foundation for achieving plant-wide risk monitoring.

articleTitle: Bayesian updating for thermal model of laser powder-bed fusion additive manufacturing
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: This study aims to enhance the accuracy of thermal models for laser powder bed fusion in metal additive manufacturing (AM) by addressing uncertainties related to stochastic model parameters and inherent biases. Given the limited availability of experimental data due to resource constraints, a rigorous quantification of cognitive uncertainties is essential. The proposed methodology employs Bayesian model updating theory to calibrate an existing thermal model, incorporating an efficient algorithm known as Bayesian Updating with Structural Reliability Method (BUS) to execute the calibration task. Additionally, a Gaussian process regression surrogate is integrated to further mitigate the computational burden. This comprehensive approach facilitates robust uncertainty quantification, particularly concerning the thermal pool w idth and depth. Despite the complexity of physical mechanisms and high computational costs, this research seeks to improve the predictive capabilities of simulation models, thereby advancing the understanding of the "process-structure-property" relationship in selective laser melting technology.

articleTitle: Reliability simulation analysis technology for electronic products based on failure physics and failure propagate models
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: This article addresses the significant gap in engineering performance and reliability modeling and simulation for complex electronic products such as antennas. The current shortfall in technology hinders the ability to analyze how actual working environments impact these products and precludes mechanism-level evaluation of their reliability indicators. In response to the distinctive needs of complex electronic products, this study delves into reliability simulation analysis technology based on the physics of failure and models of failure propagation. It introduces a novel approach to constructing reliability models that integrates both failure physics and propagation frameworks, offering a comprehensive reliability simulation analysis process and methodology for electronic products grounded in these models. Utilizing antennas as a case study, this research assesses the impact of unit reliability on overall product performance and establishes an analytical model for antenna failure time derived from simulation data. A case study on a typical antenna is conducted to demonstrate the effectiveness and credibility of the proposed technical approach, validating its applicability in enhancing the reliability assessment of complex electronic systems.

articleTitle: Enhanced intrusion strategy learning for security systems using an optimized PPO algorithm
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: In response to the limitations observed in critical infrastructure protection systems, particularly their lack of adaptabilit y in dynamic and complex environments, this paper introduces an intrusion behavior strategy analysis method utilizing an enhanced Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) algorithm. This method accounts for the decision-making behavior of attackers who have access to partial information, enabling it to effectively simulate authentic intrusion strategies. By leveraging feedback fro m environmental interactions as a learning mechanism, the approach facilitates agent strategy learning to accurately simulate optimal intrusion strategies. This advancement aids in the strategic deployment and enhancement of defenses at critical infrastructure vulnerabilities. Test results demonstrate that the improved deep reinforcement learning algorithm exhibits rapid convergence and stable computational outcomes. The proposed intrusion behavior strategy analysis model displays robust learning capabilities and strong generalizability, offering a novel framework for analyzing attack and defense strategies and advancing security defenses in physical protection systems against novel intrusion challenges.

articleTitle: Reliability study of multiple state system based on competitive failure
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: Considering the competing failure processes and multi-state characteristics of complex systems, the semi-Markov model is used to simulate degradation process, delineating transitions between different system state performances. Additionally, the probability level of the system's instantaneous resident state is specified. Leveraging the general generating function, a multi-state reliability analysis model is established. It postulates that random shocks influence the probability of a state transition occurring, with the magnitude of damage depended on the shockproofness and the probability of system aging. Consequently, system failure due to cracking, Thus, this process causes competition failure. Here, take a turbine electrical power generating system for example, and its reliability is analyzed, the results of analysis demonstrate that the feasibility of the proposed method and highlighting the necessity of accounting for competitive failure processes in reliability assessments.

articleTitle: Research on the degradation state division of DC contactors based on LSTM and Pelt algorithm
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: Achieving self-awareness of the state of DC contactors is of great significance for improving the intelligence and reliability of the systems in which they operate. This paper explores the phased division of the degradation states of DC contactors, considering their multiple features and time-dependent data characteristics. Based on the current signals collected over the full life cycle of DC contactors, we first established a life model of DC contactors using the Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) neural network. On this basis, considering the volatility and signal interference in the original data, the Pelt algorithm was used to segment the degradation state time series output by the life model into different phases. Analyzing the life test results of multiple experimental contactors using this method revealed that the degradation process of DC contactors exhibits distinct three-stage characteristics: the aging stage, the stable stage, and the failure stage. This makes the proposed method superior to common life prediction methods in reflecting the current working state of the contactor, which has practical significance for the maintenance and early warning of switching devices and lays a theoretical foundation for degradation state assessment.

articleTitle: Enhancing emotion recognition with attention-augmented EEG models
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: The analysis of human reliability in the context of nuclear power is profoundly influenced by the role of emotions. In this paper, we utilize electroencephalogram (EEG) signals for emotion recognition, employing the SJTU Emotion EEG Dataset (SEED) alongside a Graph-based Multi-task Self-Supervised Learning model (GMSS) enhanced with attention-activated convolutional networks. Experimental validation revealed that the accuracy of the model improved fro m 91.49% before the introduction of the networks to 92.51% afterward, marking an increase of 1.02%. These results demonstrate that the enhanced framework proposed in this paper is capable of effectively recognizing emotions, and the incorporation of attent ion-augmented convolutional networks has the potential to further enhance the model's recognition efficacy.

articleTitle: Research on fault symptom monitoring and early on fault symptom monitoring and early warning method of typical transport system
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: To enhance the reliability and safety of aircraft flight testing, this study introduces an interpretable multi-parameter fusion methodology designed for monitoring and early warning of fault symptoms in typical transportation systems. This methodology comprehensively integrates historical flight parameters, onboard test data, and fault or maintenance records, combining system functional modeling with advanced data-driven techniques. The approach begins with a detailed analysis of historical data to identify critical systems and predominant fault modes, followed by the development of a functional model and the establishment of a custom parameter spectrum. A Euclidean norm-based technique is then employed to systematically select representative samples of system health, facilitating the creation of a precise health assessment model. This model calculates a health index using the Mahalanobis distance metric. To increase the accuracy of fault detection, a health-fault standardization analysis is implemented, and the early warning threshold is determined by identifying the minimum discrepancy in the health index. The standardized health index is then directly correlated to this threshold, providing an interpretable solution for fault monitoring and warning. The effectiveness of the proposed method is validated through its application to data from civil aircraft air conditioning systems, where it successfully detects faults and issues timely warnings. This study provides a critical technical basis for leveraging historical data-driven fault symptom monitoring, proactive risk early warning, and the enhancement of safety in flight tests.

articleTitle: A bi-level heuristic maintenance scheduling framework for an aircraft fleet under uncertain mission scenarios
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: The aircraft fleet is typically required to perform a series of missions with finite breaks between two adjacent missions. Fleet performance can be significantly improved by having multiple teams perform timely maintenance activities on damaged aircraft during each break. However, maintenance scheduling optimization in this case is inherently constrained by the limited resources, coupled with the wide variety of ways to allocate aircraft among teams. In this paper, we develop a new maintenance scheduling framework that aims to maximize the expected readiness rate of the fleet. Additionally, we consider the uncertainty in the start time and demand of the next mission and develop a bi-level heuristic algorithm to efficiently solve the resulting optimization problem. The effectiveness of the proposed method is also tested with an example of twelve aircraft in two teams.

articleTitle: Research on incipient fault diagnosis method for pneumatic solenoid valve in nuclear power plant
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: Pneumatic solenoid valves are extensively utilized in nuclear power plants, where their failure can lead to substantial econo mic losses and pose significant safety risks. In this study, pneumatic solenoid valves are selected as the research focus. A model is constructed in DABLib using the DAMADICS data simulation platform to simulate and generate fault-type data. XGBoost regression prediction and XGBoost multi-dimensional time series prediction algorithms are then employed to diagnose incipient faults in pneumatic solenoid valves.

articleTitle: Reliability modelling of a dependent system using mic and pair-copula
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: For the reliability modelling of a multi-components system, the dependence between components should not be overlooked. However, the embedded nonlinearity and increasing complexity hinder the application of existing system reliabili ty methods like FMEA and FTA. To fill this gap, this work proposes a novel approach for the reliability modelling of dependent systems, where the Maximal Information Coefficient (MIC) method is used to simplify the dependence modelling, followed by the development of a new dependence model called MIC-PCC using Pair-Copula. The effectiveness and generality of this method are validated through numerical examples.

articleTitle: A reliability assessment method for complex electronic systems based on Vine copula and Inverse Gaussian process
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: Complex electronic systems are integral to signal transformation and information transmission. Therefore, it is crucial to assess and predict their reliability to ensure safe operation and enhance economic efficiency. These systems are characterized by high reliability, long lifespans, multiple performance parameters, and complex, multi-source failure mechanisms, which often manifest as the simultaneous degradation of multiple performance parameters. Due to the intricate internal structure and manufacturing processes, the degradation processes are often correlated. Thus, accurately assessing the reliability of complex electronic systems is particularly important. This paper proposes using the Inverse Gaussian (IG) process to describe the degradation process of a single performance characterization parameter in complex electronic systems. Additionally, the correlation of multiple performance characterization parameters is modeled using the Vine copula. Finally, the proposed theory is illustrated with a practical example of a specific type of electronic system.

articleTitle: Deep learning based key parameters prediction in nuclear power plants
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: Accurately obtaining key parameters under accident conditions in nuclear power plants (NPPs) is essential for safety analysis and is critically important for operational decision making. To enable rapid and precise forecasting of parameter trends in NPPs, we introduce an enhanced Non-stationary Transformer (NS Transformer) model. This model enhances the attention mechanism by incorporating a sparse attention mechanism. The sparse attention mechanism, which selectively focuses on key locations in the sequence, thereby significantly reducing computational complexity and memory use. In this paper, we detail the model structure and validate its effectiveness through experiments predicting key parameters in nuclear power plants. The results demonstrate that the improved prediction model can accurately forecast long-term parameter trends. This study enhances the accuracy of critical parameter predictions in NPPs during failure conditions, thereby improving the emergency response capabilities of NPPs in the event of failures and accidents.

articleTitle: Reliability prediction of power electronic converters based on surrogate models
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: Power electronic converters (PEC) are integral to various sectors, including power systems, transportation, and industrial production, where their reliability significantly influences overall system performance. Despite its importance, current research has not thoroughly addressed the simultaneous impact of component performance degradation and functional failures on electronic system performance. This paper introduces a reliability prediction method for PEC that considers both component performance degradation and functional failure. Initially, digital prototype models of PEC are developed to accurately represent the operational processes and simulate performance under each critical fault mode. To minimize simulation costs, two surrogate models based on neural networks are then established for PEC. Subsequently, through iterative calculations that utilize models of performance degradation and functional failures of components, an analysis of both PEC performance degradation and functional failure states is conducted, facilitating the completion of PEC reliability prediction. This proposed framework for reliability prediction may also be applicable to other electronic systems.

articleTitle: Research on reliability simulation based on electronic product digital mock-up
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: This paper discusses a reliability simulation methodology that integrates thermal simulation, vibration simulation, and fault physical modeling to develop CAD, CFD, and FEA digital prototypes of products. By subjecting these digital prototypes to environmental stresses such as temperature and vibration, stress analysis and damage assessment are performed. This process identifies potential weak points within the product, allowing for design enhancements that improve product reliability. Additionally, this method enables the prediction of the average time to first failure, providing a foundation for virtual verification of product reliability. It also supports the parallel collaborative design of product functionality and reliability. An application example of this reliability simulation method is provided to illustrate its practical implications.

articleTitle: Study on vibration fatigue life prediction and reliability evaluation method of turbo-pump considering structural characteristics
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: The structural characteristics of the turbo-pump impeller in a liquid rocket engine are integrated into a vibration fatigue life model. Based on this model, a dual-layer evaluation model for the vibration fatigue life reliability of the turbo-pump structure is developed, accounting for parameter dispersion. This model advances a more universal and quantifiable prediction approach for structural vibration fatigue life, incorporating a high-reliability material S-N characteristic identification method that considers structural nuances. The efficacy of this model and the associated reliability evaluation method is demonstrated through tests on two types of turbo-pump impeller products, confirming their capability to accurately identify the S-N characteristics and their parameter dispersion. Furthermore, the life distribution law under varying levels of reliability is determined. The results underscore the significant application value of this method in predicting and evaluating the fatigue life of typical structures within rocket engines.

articleTitle: Reliable life optimization of a dual magnet differential polarisation relay based on digital model
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: In this paper, a three-dimensional assembly prototype model of a relay was developed using the 3D modeling software UG. The static suction and reaction characteristics of the relay were subsequently calculated using ANSYS and ADAMS. Utilizing the static suction data obtained from the static feature simulation, the relay's dynamic feature results were derived in the MATLAB/Simulink module. A virtual prototype platform was then constructed to serve as a simulation analysis tool for optimal design. To enhance the instantaneous speed at the moment of contact separation, a novel structure for the contact system was proposed. The feasibility of this proposed scheme, aimed at improving product lifespan, was rigorously verified through simulation analysis on the virtual prototype platform and empirical testing of the prototype product.

articleTitle: Rare reliability analysis by beta-surfaces and Kriging model
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: Conducting reliability analysis for rare events poses a significant challenge in structural safety assessment and reliability-based design optimization. This paper introduces the Stratified Beta-Spheres (SBS) method to address these challenges. The approach starts by partitioning the entire support space of random input variables into sub-domains using multiple Beta-spheres, specified by the user. Truncated samples are then generated within these sub-domains both explicitly and efficiently. Using these truncated samples, the original failure probability can be estimated by summing the failure probabilities of the sub-domains. The paper also discusses and demonstrates the unbiasedness of the failure probability estimator in the proposed method. The SBS method inherits the advantages of Monte Carlo simulation (MCS) applicable to rare events and problems with multiple failure domains while maintaining ease of implementation. Additionally, the method is integrated with adaptive Gaussian process regression to perform reliability analysis for complex structures. The superiority of the proposed SBS method is validated through both numerical and engineering examples.

articleTitle: Research on complex product quality prediction method based on FA-lightGBM
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: The data generated during the manufacturing of complex products exhibits high dimensionality, strong inter-feature correlations, and data imbalance. These characteristics pose significant challenges to the accurate prediction of product qua lity. To address this issue, a complex product quality prediction model employing Factor Analysis and Light Gradient Boosting Machine (FA-lightGBM) was proposed. Initially, the mutual information method was utilized to select the optimal feature subset. Subsequently, a concise set of factor features encompassing all quality information was constructed through factor analysis. Building on this, a quality prediction model was developed using lightGBM, establishing a mapping relationship between manufacturing data features and quality characteristic values. Experimental validation confirmed that the proposed quality prediction model exhibited higher prediction accuracy compared to Lasso regression and eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) models.

Index Terms: Least Absolute Shrinkage And Selection Operator

articleTitle: Failure analysis and degradation-based reliability assessment of a fiber optic gyroscope
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: Fiber optic gyroscope (FOG) is an essential component of the photoelectric equipment servo system, and its performance degradation during operation can result in the failure of overall equipment causing undesired safety concerns. Therefore, the failure mode, effects, and criticality analysis (FMECA) approach is used in this paper to conduct the degradation-based reliability modeling and assessment of the device and to identify its weakest link. The applied approach for the FOG device indicates its high reliability within 7000 hours of operation being consistent with the actual engineering. The proposed method and analysis result presented in this research can provide a reference for investigations on the reliability of FOG.

articleTitle: Failure analysis and reliability assessment of infrared thermal imager
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: In this paper, FMECA is used to analyze the equipment system of infrared thermal imager given the characteristics of refrigeration temperature fluctuation and limited infrared video acquisition in long-term service. The results show that the imaging circuit component failure is the major fault mode in the infrared thermal imager equipment system, and the influence of the fault is mostly the abnormal refrigeration temperature. The degradation models of vacuum dewar performance index, refrigerator performance index, and Blind pixel rate index were established respectively. Copula function is used to analyze the influence of correlation degree between multiple performance indicators on reliability assessment. The DIC criterion is used to compare the ratio of three Copula models and select the most appropriate correlation degradation model. The variation rule of reliability difference between the independent model and related model is obtained, which guides equipment maintenance at different stages.

articleTitle: A bearing fault diagnosis method based on VGG SENet-BiGRU global attention
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: Rolling bearings are the core devices in the industrial field, widely used in machinery production and automation industry. Therefore, it is necessary to detect the fault of rolling bearing. In this paper, an improved VGG model based on Channel Attention mechanism (SENet) is proposed to extract the spatial features of multi-scale features after fault signal preprocessing. The BiGRU network model based on Global Attention optimization is proposed to extract the time domain features of multi-scale features after fault signal pretreatment. Excellent results are obtained by parallel fusion for fault detection.

articleTitle: Design of anti-freezing device using for oil storage tanks breathing valves system
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: The breathing valve and the flame arrester are crucial safety components of oil storage tanks. In regions where winter temperatures plummet, these devices can freeze, posing a risk to the safety of the tanks. To prevent the freezing blockage, a kind of device is designed, which is consisted of a cylinder body, a copper tube heat exchange component, a spoiler plate, a helical spoiler structure, and an airflow inlets and outlets. By leveraging heat exchanger principles, the design facilitates heat transfer between internal worm oil gas and external cold air. Therefore, excessive water vapor in the oil and gas may be pre-liquefied and refluxed to the oil storage tank before it reaches the flame arrester, avoiding freezing and blockage of the flame arrester and breathing valve. Fluent simulation was also carried out, and the results showed that the average temperature of the oil and gas at the outlet of the device could be reduced to −6.15 ℃, which is beneficial for solving the freezing and blockage of the breathing valve.

articleTitle: A deep learning based short-term wind power prediction model with Fourier self-attention mechanism
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: Traditional wind power forecasting methods typically focus on predictions at a single scale. However, changes in wind power generation are influenced by both long-term trends and cyclical fluctuations. This study employs an improved wavelet decomposition method for the multi-scale decomposition of wind power generation series, independently revealing its trend and frequency components. For the trend component, we combine convolutional neural networks (CNN) and Fourier transforms for prediction. Convolutional neural networks excel at capturing local features of wind power data, while Fourier transforms provide insights into the global fluctuation patterns of the data. For the frequency component, we design a Fourier self-attention mechanism, which combines the powerful frequency-domain analysis capability of the Fourier transform with the context-capturing properties of the self-attention model to achieve accurate prediction of frequency fluctuations. Experimental results demonstrate that our proposed prediction method outperforms traditional methods.

articleTitle: Reliability analysis of ship time domain motion response based on fractional order moment maximum entropy method
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: Addressing the ship motion response under stochastic irregular waves and accounting for the uncertainty of these waves, a time-domain numerical simulation was conducted on the S175 container ship utilizing the three-dimensional time-domain potential flow theory to develop a model of ship motion response. The extremum method was applied to convert the time-varying problem of motion response into a time-invariant problem, thereby establishing a reliability analysis model for ship motion response under irregular wave conditions. Subsequently, the extremal distribution of the motion response was calculated using the fractional moment maximum entropy method to derive the probability density function. By assessing the extremal distribution of motion response under specific sea state conditions, a new method for analysing ship motion response was proposed.
