This approach can provide a relatively accurate estimation of the probability of danger associated with ship motion response.

articleTitle: A safety barrier-based risk control method of blowouts in arctic drilling operations
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: With the melting glaciers in recent years, the Arctic area has received increasing attention from academia and industry due to its huge resources. Increasing oil and gas drilling activities can be observed in Arctic areas. One of the most critical accidents associated with these operations is the blowout. Consequently, effective risk management of blowouts in Arctic drilling operations is imperative. This paper presents a safety barrier-oriented approach for managing blowout risks during Arctic drilling operations. The approach begins by identifying the unique characteristics of Arctic drilling blowouts and analyzing specific risk factors that augment those typically associated with conventional offshore blowouts. Subsequently, a safety barrier-based risk control method is developed, which utilizes a bow-tie model integrating both fault tree and event tree methodologies. The effectiveness of this method is partially validated through the analysis of a hypothetical blowout scenari o in the Arctic, where key risk-influencing factors are identified. The results indicate that the proposed safety barrier-based risk control method effectively identifies and mitigates blowout risks in Arctic regions. Moreover, this method shows potential fo r application in other offshore and maritime operations.

articleTitle: Reliability analysis of suction anchor under the limited geological prospecting data
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: This study develops a parametric model to evaluate the anti-pulling force of the LS-FA-211001 suction anchor using geological survey data. The anti-pulling force at various exploration points is calculated, and a normal distribution is employed to model the limit anti-pulling force data, allowing for the extraction of mean and variance values. Additionally, the stress-strength interference model is utilized to assess the reliability of the suction anchor. The study conducts a comparative analysis of the distribution and reliability results of the anti-pulling force across different exploration points based on limited data. The findings reveal variations in the anti-pulling force among the exploration points, yet confirm that each maintains a high level of reliability.

articleTitle: The research and application of risk-managed technical specifications for typical nuclear power plant
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: Risk-managed technical specification (RMTS) is a plant-specific technical specification based on plant configuration to determine the completion times (CT) of components in real time by evaluating the risk. With the technological advancement of the domestic risk-informed application and the release of the "Technical Policy on Configuration Risk Management of Nuclear Power Plants”, it creates a convenient condition for the implementation of RMTS for the nuclear power plants, and the implementation of RMTS can improve operational flexibility and extend the CT of safety systems under the premise of guaranteeing the safety of the unit. This paper gives the principles and prerequisites for implementing RMTS, and takes typical safety systems of a typical VVER unit as the research object to carry out the optimization analysis of implementing RMTS. In the meantime, this paper evaluates the impact of external events on the implementation of RMTS by taking an internal fire as an example, which provides guidance and suggestions for the subsequent in-depth research and engineering application.

articleTitle: Fault classification methods for fuel cell vehicles under poor data conditions
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: Fuel cell vehicles (FCVs) represent a significant direction for the sustainable development of the automotive industry. However, current testing and evaluation standards for FCVs have not thoroughly explored fault types and classifications, leading to the absence of a unified fault grading classification scheme. To address this gap, this paper proposes a comprehensive set of grading classification evaluation indicators for FCV faults to standardize fault levels. Utilizing factor analysis and fuzzy set theory, a fault mode classification evaluation method for FCVs under conditions of data scarcity is developed, thereby guiding the classification of FCV fault levels.

articleTitle: Mixed uncertainties quantification of rolling bearings based on active Kriging model
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: Rolling bearings are critical components widely utilized in industries such as high-speed railways, aviation, and maritime sectors, where they significantly impact the stability and safety of equipment. However, the complex failure dynamics of rolling bearings pose challenges in analytically representing the limit state function, often necessitating finite element simulations for accurate establishment. Methods based on numerical simulations are computationally intensive and insufficient when describing the operational state of rolling bearings solely through static random uncertainty. Incorporating interval and time-dependent correlations is essential. Consequently, these methods require extensive sampling, further increasing computational demands. To enhance the efficiency of bearing reliability analysis, this study introduces a method for assessing time-dependent failure probability and predicting Mean Time to Failure (MTTF) using active learning Kriging models. The proposed method, suitable for mixed uncertainties, is initially validated through a numerical example. It is then applied to quantify the mixed uncertainties of a double-row cylindrical roller bearing.

articleTitle: The application of failure analysis technology in the development of new quality productive forces in high-density chip level packaging industry
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: To highlight the role of new quality productive forces in the development of the integrated circuit industry, this paper introduces a business cooperation model that incorporates fault analysis technology to assist in process validation during the product development stage. Through systematic research and analysis of phosphorus content in the plating process of integrated circuit packaging substrates, the process control window for phosphorus content is defined for customers. This approach effectively mitigates potential failure hazards that may occur in the plating process, creating value for customers by reducing R&D costs and shortening development time. The innovation and enhancement of this business cooperation model have promoted the optimization of the integrated circuit production process and improved the overall quality of integrated circuits.

articleTitle: Optimizing the scale of off-site emergency decontamination infrastructure for nuclear power plants: a case study
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: Nuclear energy is renowned for its high efficiency and low carbon emissions; however, it also presents significant safety hazards. Ensuring the safety of nuclear power plants (NPPs) is essential for achieving sustainable development. As the utilization of nuclear energy expands, the necessity for robust off-site emergency response mechanisms at NPPs has become paramount to mitigate radioactive hazards and manage potential accidents effectively. Specifically, nuclear emergency decontamination (NED) facilities play a crucial role in minimizing radiation exposure, with fixed facilities being the most prevalent type. The construction scale of these facilities should correspond to the population within the off-site plume emergency planning zone (EPZ) of the NPP. Currently, existing NED stations are insufficient due to the rising population within these zones. This study aims to ascertain the appropriate scale for off-site emergency decontamination stations by examining population data surrounding the NPP and analyzing pertinent population statistics. The research involves estimating the temporal and spatial boundaries required for public decontamination, calculating the population necessitating decontamination through satellite thermal imagery, and determining the essential equipment for effective decontamination within a specified timeframe. This study provides a comprehensive methodology for assessing the capabilities of decontamination facilities and contributes to the development of strategies aimed at enhancing nuclear safety and managing the risks associated with nuclear energy.

articleTitle: A novel remaining useful life prediction combining IWOA-BiLSTM and PCA for aircraft engine
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: Remaining useful life (RUL) Prediction is crucial for the predictive maintenance of industrial manufacturing systems. The challenges encountered in the prediction of RUL include identifying a pertinent health indicator (HI), effectively modeling t he degradation pattern across diverse features, and selecting optimal methodologies to enhance prediction accuracy. This paper establishes the construction of the HI using PCA, utilizing data from aircraft engines. Bi-LSTM with optimization algorithm is investigated for RUL evaluation and prediction of aircraft engines. Subsequent experiments are performed on simulation data from a commercial modular aero propulsion system using the proposed method, demonstrating its superiority over traditional approaches.

articleTitle: Research on quantitative evaluation of customer satisfaction
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: This paper conducts a critical analysis of the prevalent issues in the evaluation of customer satisfaction. It introduces a comprehensive model for the quantitative evaluation of customer satisfaction and proposes four distinct types of customer satisfaction evaluation models. Furthermore, this study delves into the refinement of evaluation criteria including the satisfaction coefficient, satisfaction evaluation tables, and methods for calculating satisfaction. This paper aims to serve as a valuable reference for the assessment of customer satisfaction in various sectors.

articleTitle: Failure physics modeling and reliability prediction of electromagnetic relay based on permanent magnet degradation
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: The degradation of the magnetic properties of permanent magnets, a critical component of electromagnetic relays, significantl y impacts the electromagnetic suction characteristics of these relays. However, due to the complex structure of relays and the nonlinearity between input and output, existing degradation models for individual permanent magnets cannot be effectively applied to the overall performance degradation of electromagnetic relays. Therefore, this paper proposes a method for failure physical modeling and reliability prediction of electromagnetic relays based on permanent magnet degradation. Initially, a high-temperature accelerated degradation test is designed and used to establish the failure physics model of the permanent magnet and the migration matrix of a typical structure. Subsequently, product batch virtual samples are created using the Monte Carlo method, and the reliability of the product is predicted using the virtual prototype model. The feasibility of thi s modeling method is verified using Alnico, a commonly used permanent magnet material, and the typical structure of electromagnetic relays as examples.

articleTitle: Remaining useful life prediction of induction motor based on hybrid temporal convolution neural network
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: To ensure safety across various industries including manufacturing, construction, defense, science, and medical care, the hea lth of induction motors is critical. However, existing research on motor health monitoring is not comprehensive. Moreover, commonly used deep learning techniques such as convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and recurrent neural networks face challenges in making accurate long-term predictions. To overcome these limitations, this study proposes a hybrid temporal convolutional neural network (HTCN) aimed at predicting the remaining useful life (RUL) of induction motors. The HTCN architecture consists of two parallel branches: one integrates a temporal convolutional network (TCN) with a self-attention mechanism, while the other integrates a 1D CNN module enhanced with a convolutional block attention module (CBAM). The TCN branch utilizes different features from multi-sensory signals, while the raw signals are directly fed into the 1D CNN branch with CBAM. The extracted features from both branches are concatenated to predict RUL. This integrative approach enriches the model's understanding of the input data and aims to improve the accuracy of RUL predictions. The effectiveness of the proposed model is validated using datasets derived from an accelerated aging experiment on an electric motor.

articleTitle: Bearing fault diagnosis based on capsule network and transfer learning
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: Bearings are widely used in many machines and equipment and often fail when they are used for long periods under different conditions of varying frequencies and loads. As a result, the detection of defects in bearings in various working states is crucial. However, the conventional neural networks are associated with severe feature extraction problems and relatively low detection rates due to data loss in the pooling layers. This study uses capsule neural networks to overcome the above - mentioned limitations in bearing fault diagnosis. This paper also solves the problem of traditional diagnostic methods that do not easily adapt to different conditions by using transfer learning with the capsule network. The experimental results are compared with the Case Western Reserve University’s dataset to check the efficiency of the proposed methodology for cross-condition bearing fault diagnosis. It is evidenced by the findings that this method is accurate, and that the algorithm introduced in this work is quite complex.

articleTitle: Spring life prediction model based on stress relaxation theory
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: Stress relaxation is a significant failure mode observed in springs, and constructing a life prediction model based on stress relaxation is an effective approach. However, recent research has primarily focused on expensive experimental methods to quantify stress relaxation values. In this study, finite element simulation experiments on spring stress relaxation were conducted using a creep constitutive model and stress relaxation theory. The findings indicate that the results from these fi nite element simulations align well with theoretical expectations, suggesting that such simulations can partially substitute costly physical experiments. Furthermore, by leveraging data from finite element simulations, a stress relaxation model was integrated, and parameter fitting was performed to enhance the accuracy of the stress relaxation model and improve life prediction capabilities.

articleTitle: Accumulation characteristics of contact surfaces based arc energy of HSER
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: Under rated load and overload conditions, an arc may form between the contacts of a relay during its release or operation state, with the trajectory of the arc being random. The variability in ignition times and positions results in differing amounts of energy being released by the arc, leading to uncertainty in the ablation of the contact surface. Generally, as the number of operations increases, the roughness of the relay contact surface gradually increases, which in turn raises the contact resistance and exacerbates contact heating. This paper summarizes the accumulated characteristics of the contact surface in the released state of a Hermetically Sealed Electromagnetic Relay (HSER). A dual-angle arc photography platform was constructed to capture the two-dimensional trajectory of the arc. By analyzing scatter plots of the arc center and the trajectory of the arc center, the distribution patterns of the arc center and its trajectory are established. Consequently, the accumulation characteristics of the contact surface are thoroughly analyzed.

articleTitle: Analysis of sealing reliability and unsealing safety of K361 packer
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: Current research on the sealing reliability and unsealing safety evaluation of the all-metal sealed K361 thermal recovery packer remains largely unexplored. This paper addresses this gap by establishing a mathematical model for mechanical analysis that incorporates the shadow response during the expansion contact process, based on an analysis of the K361 packer's sealing structure characteristics. Utilizing ANSYS software, this study simulates and analyzes the contact stress, deformation, and residual deformation under variations in the effective length, inner diameter, and wall thickness of the sealing sleeve. Additionally, the established setting factor and unsealing factor are evaluated, and the influence of these three parameters on setting and unsealing is determined. The findings of this analysis provide guidance for the design and optimization of the K361 thermal recovery packer, thereby enhancing the reliability of tools and the efficacy of heavy oil stratified recovery.

articleTitle: Structural vibration analysis and modal analysis based on EEMD
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: Modal parameters play an important role in the reliability and stability of various structures Specifically, modal analysis is an engineering method used in structural dynamics to obtain key modal parameters, including modal frequencies and modes. This provides researchers with a reliable basis for examining structural stability, identifying design flaws, and other aspects. In this paper, we propose an improved algorithm based on Ensemble Empirical Mode Decomposition (EEMD), referred to as the PSO-EEMD algorithm, and verify its effectiveness through simulation. The results indicate that the improved algorithm can significantly enhance the accuracy of decomposition, reduce errors, and provide more accurate modal analysis results.

articleTitle: Reliability analysis for new LNG hose bunkering system
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: To enhance the safety of liquefied natural gas (LNG) bunkering operations, this study designs an LNG hose bunkering system. The system integrates both hardware and software components to implement an emergency release mechanism for leaks. The software system collects and transmits environmental and operational data, while the hardware system executes the necessary functions. Three emergency release mechanisms are designed to ensure the safety of bunkering operations: component-activated, physical-activated, and system-activated. A failure rate analysis of the LNG bunkering system was conducted to validate the reliability of the proposed system. The results indicate that although the Programmable Logic Controller (PLC) is identified as the most critical component, its failure rate remains within acceptable safety criteria.

articleTitle: Positioning accuracy analysis for an electromechanical coupled robotic joint module under uncertainties
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: The robotic joint module is a typical mechatronic system that inevitably faces uncertainties from various fields. These uncertainties significantly influence its positioning accuracy. In this article, we develop a positioning accuracy analysis o f a robotic joint module under such uncertainties. First, a comprehensive electromechanical coupling model is constructed by considering the information exchange rules between mechanical and electronic components. Subsequently, a positioning accuracy analysis is performed, taking into account uncertainties from different fields. A variance-based sensitivity analysis method is employed to represent the contribution of these uncertainties. Finally, simulations are carried out to evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Study on risk-informed surveillance test interval optimization for emergency diesel generators in nuclear power plants
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: After years of development and practice of probabilistic safety assessment (PSA) technology, the application of risk-informed technology based on PSA in nuclear power plants has been widely recognized. Combined with the practical experience and actual needs of the nuclear power plant, this paper adopts the risk-informed method to analyze the optimization (extension) of the surveillance test interval of the emergency diesel generator of the nuclear power plant. The analysis results show that the operating experience feedback of emergency diesel generator is good since the commercial operation, and the surveillance test interval has base for optimization. According to traditional engineering analysis, the optimization of surveillance test interval satisfies the principle of defense in depth of nuclear power plant, and does not affect the safety margin of nuclear power pl ant. According to the probabilistic safety assessment, the increase of core damage frequency and large early release frequency after the optimization of the surveillance test interval is a small change with acceptable risk, and nuclear power plants can carry out the optimization of the surveillance test interval of emergency diesel generators.

articleTitle: Contact characteristics and reliability assessment for high-speed electrical connector based on artificial neural network surrogate modeling
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: Electrical connector is an important key component in the electronic information industry, its performance and rel iability have an important effect on the performance of the entire system. In this paper, considering the influence of uncertainties from structural parameters and working load, a reliability estimation method is proposed based on physical of failure modelling and Monte Carlo simulation (MCS) method. Firstly, considering the randomness of the structural parameters and temperature, the mechanical properties of the electrical connector are studied by finite element analysis method. Further, the contact resistance is calculated by empirical theoretical model. Then, the failure modes of the electrical connector are analysed, and physical model of failure is formulated based on backpropagation neural network (BPNN). On this basis, the reliability of electrical connector is analysed by combining surrogate model and MCS method. Reliability analysis of a high-speed electrical connector is presented to validate the proposed method. The reliability evaluation results show that this type of electrical connector meets the reliability requirements.

articleTitle: Optimization of startup signal for residual heat removal system of secondary side
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: Due to the component interaction behavior in the control process, the startup signal of the residual heat removal system of the secondary side (PRS), and the fault tree analysis method may have incomplete identification of the failure model. Therefore, this paper enhances the fault tree analysis method by introducing the System Theory Process Analysis (STPA) method as a supplement. The STPA method is used for qualitative analysis of the startup signal of the PRS, identifying a more comprehensive set of potential failure factors. Subsequently, quantitative analysis is performed by building a fault tree mod el to identify the weaknesses of the PRS startup signal. An improvement scheme for the PRS startup signal is then proposed. Evaluation and analysis of the improved scheme indicate that the optimization strategy is both reasonable and feasible. Furthermore, the proposed enhanced fault tree analysis method can be effectively applied to system desig n improvement and optimization in the development process of similar power plants and new reactors.

articleTitle: Study on risk-informed safety classification in VVER nuclear power plant
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: With the development of probability safety assessment (PSA) and the application of risk-informed technology, a risk-informed safety classification method of Structures, Systems and Components for nuclear power plants has been developed. The risk-informed safety classification does not replace the existing safety classification, but further subdivides the two levels of "safety related" and "non-safety related" in the existing safety classification according to the safety significant of components to the risk. The SSCs is subdivided into high safety significant (HSS) and low safety significant (LSS) according to the safety significant of components to the risk. This paper focuses on the methods of risk-informed safety classification. In the analysis, the typical system of nuclear power plant is studied as a risk-informed safety classification, and according to the analysis results, the optimization of special treatment requirements for RISC-3 components is proposed. The analysis results show that among the components classified as safety related by traditional deterministic analysis method, a relatively high proportion of the components can be classified as safety related components with low safety significant through analysis. Exempting or reducing the special treatment requirements for these components can effectively improve the economy of nuclear power plant under the premise of ensuring safety.

articleTitle: Assessment of UAV combat effectiveness based on ADCBU methodology
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: With the rapid advancement of UAV technology, the deployment of UAVs in actual combat has increased, necessitating an urgent need for accurate combat effectiveness assessment. Traditional ADC assessment methods are insufficient for contemporary combat scenarios. This paper introduces an improved ADC assessment model. By constructing a comprehensive UAV combat effectiveness index system, it integrates factors such as personnel training, skill levels, and battlefield environment, supplemented by expert evaluations. The improved ADC model is demonstrated to be more pertinent to real-world combat situations through detailed calculation examples.

articleTitle: Study on key dynamic parameters of station blackout accident based on RISMC method
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: The Risk Informed Safety Margin Characterization (RISMC) methodology is based on the coupling of deterministic safety analysis theory and probabilistic safety analysis theory. The accident which may lead to core damage will be researched realistically. The evolution law of the accident, the possibility of occurrence and the consequences are studied. The method aims at studying the influence of thermal parameters and model uncertainty, random failure uncertainty on the accident process of nuclear power plants under different accident scenarios. In this paper, HPR1000 SBO (station blackout) accident is taken as the research object. Based on the theory of RISMC, dynamic characteristics analysis is carried out, the typical scenario of SBO accidents with the failure of auxiliary feed water is selected for analysis. Combined with probabilistic safety analysis, deterministic safety analysis and engineering judgment, the key dynamic characteristic parameters of SBO accidents are analyzed. The research results in this paper can provide support for the typical case RISMC analysis for SBO accident.

articleTitle: Few shot fault diagnosis method of rolling bearing based on CSML
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: Currently, neural network models have seen widespread adoption in the sphere of fault diagnosis. In the training process of the model there are still problems such as high demand for training data and insufficient generalisation of the model under different working conditions. In order to solve the above problems, in this paper, an algorithm named Cosine Annealing-Sgd-Meta-Learning (CSML) is proposed, which combines the cosine annealing method with the principles of stochastic gradient descent meta-learning. The method uses the cosine annealing algorithm to adjust the learning rate in the outer loop so as to better help the meta-learning task to find the initialisation parameters. In the inner loop, the learning rate is updated using the SGD optimisation algorithm and a wide convolutional network is used to improve the model's ability to extract fault information from the meta-task under known operating conditions, and then the basic learner is updated. High diagnostic accuracy was obtained on the Western Reserve University bearing dataset, which verified its feasibility and effectiveness.

articleTitle: Test methods for reliability evaluation based on environmental factors
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: Reliability tests are typically conducted in a single environment. However, when products operate in different environments, the original reliability test methods become inadequate. This paper studies reliability evaluation test methods under two different environments based on the reliability characteristic quantities required by the reliability evaluation test. It provides calculation methods for the initial failure period and service life concerning environmental factors, as well as the principles for reducing reliability information across different environments. Using a specific product as an example, a feasible reliability evaluation test scheme based on the environmental factor reliability evaluation test method is proposed.

articleTitle: Optimization of preventive and opportunistic maintenance strategies for wind turbines
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: Traditional preventive maintenance strategies are increasingly insufficient to address the diverse maintenance demands of win d turbines. This paper explores a comprehensive approach to optimize preventive maintenance tasks for wind turbine systems, developing a corresponding strategy optimization model. This model incorporates the age reduction factor and the failure rate increasing factor into the degradation process of component maintenance, constructing a failure rate function for components under imperfect maintenance conditions. Building upon this, the concept of opportunistic maintenance is introduced, which considers the structural and temporal characteristics of the maintenance tasks. The opportunistic maintenance coefficient of components is used as the optimization variable in the target model, creating maintenance optimization models that aim to minimize maintenance costs while maximizing system availability. A multi-objective optimization model for wind turbine maintenance strategies is formulated through a comprehensive assessment of maintenance costs and availability indicators, employing the objective weighting method. The results demonstrate that the opportunistic maintenance strategy can significantly reduce the total maintenance costs during the effective operational period of the wind turbine and enhance syst em availability. The proposed maintenance model effectively meets the varied needs of decision-makers.

articleTitle: Level set method for structure topology optimization with asymmetrical microstructure model
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: Granular materials and structures, which are prevalent in nature and replicated in numerous engineering applications across various fields, display complex mechanical behaviors, notably asymmetry in tension and compression under external loading conditions. When designing structures utilizing these materials, addressing only material anisotropy is inadequate from a macroscopic viewpoint. Existing methods for the topology optimization of granular materials often do not yield smooth boundaries, which can create challenges in practical engineering applications, especially during the post-processing of jagged edges. This work offers a parametric level set topology optimization methodology for granular material structures to handle zig-zagged borders. The stiffness matrix for each element is derived using the granular micromechanics methodology, which links micro-scale interactions to macro-scale phenomena to define material constitutive relationships. Furthermore, this constitutive relationship is integrated into the radial basis function framework for the level set topology optimization method. Benchmark issues are addressed using the provided mathematical approach, resulting in topologies with smooth borders. In the resulting optimal topologies, areas experiencing tension and compression are distinctly marked in red and blue, respectively. These results illustrate the dependability and accuracy of the presented mathematical model for topology optimization.

articleTitle: Explosion hazard analysis of LNG tank trucks passing through cross sea bridges after unloading
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: A small amount of liquefied natural gas (LNG) often remains inside tank trucks after unloading. This paper investigates the safety of LNG tank trucks traversing cross-sea bridges post-unloading. Using the process hazard analysis software tool PHAST, the study calculates methane leakage and dispersion from holes in pipelines connected to LNG tanks, as well as the explosion consequences of methane-air mixtures. An explosion overpressure value of 0.10 MPa is used as the hazard evaluation criterion. The results indicate that even with only 0.10% to 0.50% of the rated filling capacity of the LNG tanks remaining after unloading, if the leakage breach diameters exceed 25 mm, the resulting maximum explosion overpressure may surpass 0.10 MPa. This level of overpressure could cause permanent damage to the reinforced concrete structures of cross-sea bridges. Therefore, to ensure the safety of cross-sea bridges, it is not advisable to allow unloaded LNG tank trucks to pass through these structures.

articleTitle: Optimization of reliability evaluation method based on fault correction test
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: The occurrence of product failure during the aviation equipment test directly affects the reliability level. Whether the failure is corrected and the correction strength will also directly affect the reliability evaluation method and results. The situation encountered in the equipment test stage is complex and diverse, which poses a great challenge to reliability evaluation. In this paper, aiming at the problems of limited reliability growth assessment and difficult engineering application caused by the diversity of fault correction timing in the process of field test, the methods of non-correction test, immediate correction test, early correction test, delayed correction test, partial immediate correction test, single equipment complex correction test a nd multi-equipment complex correction test are studied step by step. The corresponding reliability evaluation model is put forward and applied to engineering practice, which improves the accuracy of equipment reliability evaluation results in fligh t test stage.

articleTitle: Research on performance degradation assessment of rolling bearings
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: The performance degradation assessment (PDA) in rolling bearings through vibration signals is crucial for the successful implementation of preventive maintenance strategies. However, traditional indicators in existing methodologies often fail to effectively characterize the degradation trend, and feature extraction is heavily reliant on specific experience and operational parameters. Addressing these limitations, this paper introduces a novel PDA method. Initially, the selected features under normal operating conditions are selected based on the correlation coefficient method. Subsequently, the dimensionality of the feature space is then reduced using the Kernel Principal Component Analysis (KPCA) algorithm. The refined comprehensive feature set is then input into the degradation assessment model, employing the novel method Support Vector Data Description (SVDD) to integrate these features into a coherent degradation indicator (DI). To fine-tune the SVDD parameters, including the penalty parameter and kernel parameter, the Hippopotamus Optimization (HO) algorithm is incorporated into the optimization process. Experimental results validate the method in degradation detection and in accurately reflecting the overall performance degradation of the bearings, showcasing distinct advantages over other existing methods.

articleTitle: Residual life prediction of lithium battery based on improved multi-optimization algorithm and support vector regression
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: The lithium-ion battery is increasingly critical in the fields of electric vehicles and sustainable energy. Accurate prediction of the Remaining Useful Life (RUL) of lithium-ion batteries is essential to mitigate risks and minimize potential losses. This paper introduces a novel fusion algorithm, FPSOGWO, which combines Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Grey Wolf Optimization (GWO) with an enhanced Circle chaos strategy and a random adaptive weighting strategy. The FPSOGWO algorithm, integrated with Support Vector Regression (FPSOGWO-SVR), was utilized to predict the RUL of health factors in lithium batteries. Compared to other optimization algorithms, FPSOGWO exhibits superior optimization speed and value, effectively overcoming issues of local optimality. Specifically, when benchmarked against the Whale Optimization Algorithm-SVR (WOA-SVR), the R-Square values of FPSOGWO-SVR showed improvements of 15.62%, 1.28%, 5.67%, and 10.65% across four different types of batteries. Experimental results demonstrate that FPSOGWO-SVR provides more accurate RUL predictions for lithium batteries, highlighting its potential for broader application in battery health management systems.

articleTitle: Sensitivity analysis for optimizing magnetic bead recoveries in a flow-through fluorescence immunoassay analyser
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: The recovery rate of magnetic beads is a crucial factor in evaluating the performance of a flow fluorescence immunoassay analyzer. This paper proposes an optimal design method for an immunoassay analyzer using orthogonal testing and comprehensive sensitivity analysis. The orthogonal experimental design was employed to reduce the number of sensitivity analysis tests required for key design parameters of the flow fluorescence immunoassay analyzer. Through rigorous sensitivity analysis and comprehensive evaluation, the optimal combination of adsorption height, liquid volume, and adsorption time was determined. The experimental results demonstrate that this optimal combination design can significantly improve the recovery rate of magnetic beads. This method provides a novel approach to optimizing the performance of immunoassay analyzers.

articleTitle: Research on thermodynamic features of transients in the primary loop of nuclear power plant
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: The primary circuit transient of nuclear power plants serves as a crucial indicator for assessing the fatigue of primary circ uit materials. To facilitate the systematic management of transient data, an automatic classification tool was developed, designed to autonomously identify, classify, and manage the entire statistical process associated with these transients. The classification of transient data employs a variety of technical solutions, including thermodynamic feature rule classification, neural networks, and image recognition. The outcomes of this development reveal that by analyzing and extracting the thermodynamic characteristics of the primary loop's transients, a rule classification algorithm based on these thermo dynamic properties can be established. This algorithm can function as a foundational identification scheme and provide a reference for the results generated by intelligent algorithms.

articleTitle: Research on reliability analysis method of stiffened panel structure based on adaptive Kriging surrogate model
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: Stiffened panels are fundamental elements of deep-sea floating platforms and hull structures. Analysing these panels is essential for the reliability assessment of oceanic structures. However, existing reliability analysis methods for stiffened panels often struggle to balance computational efficiency with precision in assessment. The Kriging model, known for its error estimation capabilities, is increasingly used in structural reliability analysis. Within this context, the Confidence Interval Squeezing (CIS) method emerges as a novel adaptive reliability analysis technique that swiftly enhances the accuracy of failure probability estimates. This paper explores the reliability analysis of stiffened panel structures on an actual offshore platform utilizing the CIS method. Initially, the predominant loads and failure modes of stiffened panels are delineated. Subsequently, the paper discusses structural reliability analysis methods, including the CIS approach. The CIS method is then applied to the reliability analysis of stiffened panels via two numerical examples and is benchmarked against the AK-MCS method. The findings indicate that the CIS method not only accurately estimates the failure probability of stiffened panels but also delivers a quicker computational performance.

articleTitle: The application research of nuclear power mechanical equipment multi-fault feature extraction technologies based on material, energy and signal flow modeling
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: Due to the inherent complexities of nuclear power machinery equipment, which include intricate structures, numerous interfaces, and interconnected functions, failures within this equipment often exhibit dispersed, repetitive, and coupled characteristics . To address the challenges associated with extracting fault features and the subsequent difficulties in fault diagnosis and positioning in such mechanical systems, this paper introduces a multi-fault feature extraction method grounded in material, energy, and signal flow modeling. Utilizing condition monitoring data and expert insights, a sophisticated technique for multi-fault feature extraction is developed, incorporating function dependency modeling, fault parametric analysis, and the construction of a fault dependency matrix. This approach establishes a dependency matrix that correlates “multi-fault coupling failure modes and characteristic parameters” of typical mechanical equipment, enabling the systematic extraction and categorization of fault characteristic parameters. The efficacy and applicability of this key technology are validated, and recommendations for its optimization are proposed.

articleTitle: Rolling bearing fault diagnosis method based on symbiotic organisms search
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: Bearings frequently operate under extreme conditions such as high temperatures, high speeds, and heavy loads, which complicates the detection of their vibration signals. This complexity often undermines the precision and reliability of traditional fault diagnosis methods. While techniques such as Empirical Mode Decomposition (EMD) and Variational Mode Decomposition (VMD) have proven somewhat effective for analyzing non-stationary signals, they are impeded by issues like sensitivity to noise, mode mixing, and the necessity to set hyperparameters. In particular, VMD requires the pre-determination of two hyperparameters: the penalty factor and the number of modes, where finding optimal values typically involves laborious experimentation, thereby hindering the method’s efficiency. To address these challenges, this paper introduces an innovative approach that enhances the optimization of VMD parameters using a combination of the Genetic Algorithm (GA) and the Symbiotic Organisms Search (SOS) algorithm. This synergy aims to automate and optimize the extraction of bearing fault features efficiently. Subsequently, the features are classified using a Support Vector Machine (SVM), significantly improving the precision and efficiency of fault diagnosis.

articleTitle: Functional multi-response robust optimization for additive manufacturing process
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: In the context of the 3D printing process and product quality design, effectively addressing the modeling and parameter optimization problems of functional multi-response, particularly multiple profile responses, remains a significant challenge. Various methods have been developed to tackle these challenges, including functional data analysis and tensor regression. However, existing methods are inadequate for simultaneously handling the modeling and robust optimization problems of functional multi-response, especially when the functional multi-response is densely sampled. In light of the current research status, this study introduces a tensor regression method designed to address the sampling bias problem arising from a limited number of samples in functional multi-response. This method employs a robust optimization technique to determine the optimal process parameter settings. Initially, the high-dimensional parameter tensor in the tensor regression model is decomposed into low-rank components using the CP decomposition method. Subsequently, the parameters are jointly estimated using the Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM) and Block Coordinate Descent (BCD) methods. Finally, the Euclidean distance and tensor regression model are utilized to construct a robust optimization model, and a hybrid genetic algorithm is employed to obtain the optimal process parameter settings. Case studies on additive manufacturing validate the reliability an d robustness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A novel hybrid high-speed DC arc extinguishing circuit topology for the relay
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: Hybrid relays can effectively suppress arcing and enhance the electrical life and reliability of relays. However, existing hybrid relays require multiple commutations during the turn-off process, leaving room for improvement in turn-off speed. This paper proposes an improved topology, introducing a new fast DC hybrid relay that enhances switching speed by combining zero voltage switching (ZVS) and zero current switching (ZCS) technologies to achieve arc suppression. A transient model of the hybrid relay is established, and the key switching transient process is analyzed. A 28V/40A experimental prototype is built to verify the performance of the proposed circuit topology. Experimental results demonstrate that by simplifying the commutation process, the turn-off time of the hybrid relay is reduced to 17.4 μs . Additionally, the hybrid relay exhibits a minimum arc energy of 0.09 percent of that of the electromagnetic relay during the switching process. The arc suppression effect of the hybrid relay becomes more pronounced as the load current increases. The circuit topology proposed in this paper is universal and can be applied to hybrid switches of different voltage levels.

articleTitle: Research on quality assurance technology for electronic assembly process
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: Electronic equipment is advancing towards greater levels of intelligence, informatization, and digitization. As a result, electronic products are becoming increasingly complex, characterized by higher assembly density and significantly greater challenges in assembly. Consequently, the associated electronic assembly processes are fraught with escalating quality risks. This article, through research and consultations with major electronic equipment manufacturing enterprises in China, along with analysis and optimization solutions for numerous electronic product failures, identifies key factors contributing to these challenges. These include manufacturability design, material selection, and process assessment. The paper provides specific solutions for these three aspects to achieve a comprehensive improvement in the quality of electronic assembly processes.

articleTitle: An improved uncertainty calibration approach for reliable satellite temperature interval prediction
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: Accurate satellite temperature interval prediction is critical for satellite reliability analysis and health state evaluation. However, existing uncertainty quantification methods often yield imprecise uncertainty estimates for the complex task of predicting satellite temperatures. Therefore, enhancing the quality of uncertainty quantification by recalibrating uncertainty results is of paramount importance. This paper introduces an advanced model uncertainty calibration approach for satellite temperature interval prediction, leveraging the Monte Carlo Dropout and quantile calibration methods. Specifically, the Monte Carlo Dropout method is employed to quantify model uncertainty by generating output distribution samples. Concurrently, the uncertainty quality is enhanced by adjusting the quantile levels using the quantile calibration method, resulting in a more accurately calibrated prediction interval. The efficacy of the proposed method is validated through a simulation example and a real-world engineering case, demonstrating that the calibrated prediction interval coverage probability aligns more closely with the specified confidence levels, thereby rendering the predicted uncertainty interval more credible.

articleTitle: Diesel engine vibration signal decomposition method based on successive multivariate variational mode decomposition
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: To address the challenges of mode aliasing and endpoint effects inherent in current diesel engine vibration signal decomposition methods, and to enhance the reliability of subsequent anomaly detection and fault diagnosis, this paper proposes a novel approach by integrating successive variational mode decomposition (SVMD) with multivariate variational mode decomposition (MVMD), resulting in the Successive Multivariate Variational Mode Decomposition (SMVMD) method tailored for diesel engine vibration signals. The technical principles of SMVMD are elucidated, and its feasibility and effectiveness for processing diesel engine vibration signals are substantiated through both simulated signal analysis and real diesel engine condition monitoring data. Comparative analyses and example verifications demonstrate that SMVMD offers improved decomposition accuracy and computational efficiency relative to comparable methods, thereby presenting a significant advancement in the field of diesel engine diagnostics.

articleTitle: Equipment reliability modeling based on multi-dimensional time-varying universal generating functions
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: With the integration and diversification of equipment functions, the reliability of equipment makes it difficult to accurately characterize the integrated functional attributes of equipment. In this paper, we propose a reliability modeling and analysis method using a multidimensional time-varying general generating function, tailored to the multi-functional attributes of equipment. This approach involves decomposing the equipment’s multiple functional attributes, performing node analysis on each decomposed functional dimension, and discretizing the performance distribution of the equipment over time. Then, derive the universal generating function for each functional dimension using structural operators and establish a multi-dimensional time-varying universal function device reliability model by introducing superposition operators. Finally, a frequency-shifted track circuit transmitter within a rail transit signal system was used for numerical simulation as an example. The results demonstrated that the model in this paper can more comprehensively reflect the equipment’s reliability, verifying its innovation and effectiveness.

articleTitle: Analysis of wear failure mechanism and performance degradation prediction of aviation fuel gear pump
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: The gear pump is widely applied in aircraft fuel systems due to its reliable performance and low cost. It is one of the most critical components in the aircraft fuel control system. However, the failure mechanism of airborne gear pumps is complex due to the challenging operating conditions, including wide temperature ranges, varying load sequences, and strong vibrations. This paper focuses on the wear failure mechanism of the floating bearing in aviation fuel gear pumps and constructs its degradation process model. First, a dynamics model is established to demonstrate that floating bearings primarily experience two-body wear under airborne operating conditions. Next, the wear failure mechanism of the friction pair, composed of the fuel gear pump gear end face and the thrust bearing, is analyzed based on the two-body wear model, establishing the relationship between wear and leakage. Subsequently, the degradation process model is constructed based on the leakage model of the gear pump. Finally, the accuracy of the proposed model is verified using real test data.

articleTitle: Soil-structure reliability assessment of fixed monopile offshore wind turbine based on modified environmental contour method
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: This paper aims to develop a reliability assessment method for monopile offshore wind turbines, focusing on a serviceability limit state wherein the rotation of the pile head should not exceed a specified threshold. The modified environmental contour method is used to estimate the 50-year extreme distribution of the pile head forces. The finite element method is utilized to calculate the pile head rotation, taking into account the pile-soil interaction through the p-y curve method. Given the uncertainties associated with the extreme pile head forces and soil conditions, the First Order Reliability Method (FORM) is applied to evaluate the reliability of the monopile offshore wind turbine. The findings indicate that the short-term extreme pile head forces conform to the generalized extreme value distribution, and that the extreme bending moment and extreme shear force do not necessarily occur simultaneously. For a comprehensive reliability assessment, it is crucial to consider the 50-year extreme bending moment and the corresponding shear force that occur concurrently.

articleTitle: Fire risk analysis of offshore drilling operations based on Bayesian networks
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: Offshore oil and gas play a crucial role in meeting the energy demands of modern economies. However, the risks associated with offshore activities, such as fires and explosions, can lead to significant losses. Consequently, risk analysis of offshore operations is imperative. This paper introduces a Bayesian network approach to analyze the risks associated with offshore oil and gas activities. Initially, fuzzy set theory is employed to convert domain knowledge into quantitative prior probabilities. Insigh ts from industry experts and the literature then inform the development of a fault tree tailored to offshore operations. This fault t ree is integrated into a Bayesian network framework, enhancing the analysis of risk evolution mechanisms in detail. Subsequent ly, sensitivity analysis is conducted to identify and propose risk control measures. The applicability of the proposed method is demonstrated through a case study on offshore drilling operations, specifically analyzing fire risk. The results indicate tha t this method holds potential for application across various industrial systems.

articleTitle: Study of electrical contact performance of slotted contacts for electrical connectors under fretting wear conditions
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: Fretting wear is the predominant failure mechanism in electrical connectors during usage. This type of wear adversely affects the electrical contact performance of connectors, primarily by increasing the contact resistance. Once the contact resistance surpasses the failure threshold, the connector ceases to function effectively. This study initially examines the pattern of change in the electrical contact performance of slotted contacts in electrical connectors subjected to fretting wear. Subsequent stages involve selecting specific contact components for vibration testing to monitor and record shifts in contact resistance and to analyze the causative factors at each stage of wear. Finally, by varying the vibration conditions, further tests are conducted to elucidate the relationship between the electrical contact performance of slotted contacts and the applied vibration stress.

articleTitle: Fatigue life prediction of Dual Flat No-Lead packaging component solder joint
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: With the rapid development of electronic micro-assembly technology, the reliability of interconnected solder joints has become a crucial factor in determining overall equipment reliability. This paper focuses on a type of Dual Flat No-lead (DFN) packaging component that failed during actual service. Through temperature cycling life tests, a fatigue life prediction formula for this type of component was developed. The effectiveness of this formula was confirmed by comparing it with the fatigue life prediction results observed during actual service. This formula can also be used to predict the fatigue life of Square Flat No-lead (QFN) packaging component solder joints.

articleTitle: Vibration mode analysis of local resonance metamaterial with chiral spiral elastic beams
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: Local resonant metamaterials are highly effective for managing low-frequency vibrations in practical engineering applications. However, the focus of existing research on locally resonant metamaterials has predominantly been on their structural attributes, limiting the expansion of bandgaps that are generated through local resonance mechanisms. This study introduces a chiral spiral locally resonant metamaterial (CSLRM) designed to attenuate low-frequency vibrations. The proposed vibration damper, crafted from homogeneous materials, exhibits robust adaptability, high stability, and manufacturability, making it ideal for use in demanding engineering environments. The incorporation of resonators, consisting of chiral helical be ams and mass blocks, into the supporting structure facilitates vibration control within compact spaces. Additionally, a finite element model of th e CSLRM structure was developed, and its dispersion curves and vibration modes were analyzed to explore the bandgap formation mechanism and characterize the bandgap features of the CSLRM structure. This research advances the understanding of how to broaden and tune the bandgaps in locally resonant metamaterials.

articleTitle: Adaptive scheduling of predictive maintenance interval via the integration of multi-source information
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: As a pivotal technology in digital asset management, intelligent inspection and replacement play a crucial role in reducing operational costs, ensuring reliability, and enhancing the overall efficiency of various industrial plants. Traditionally, inspection and replacement intervals have been set based on a static reference cycle, which can often lead to either excessive or insufficient resource allocation. To overcome this issue, we propose an adaptive, predictive interval optimization approach that leverages multi-source health information. Specifically, we develop a data fusion method to track the dynamic degradation trend of assets, employing a Kalman Filter to facilitate the real-time updating of degradation rates and the distribution of remaining useful life. Subsequently, a dynamic interval management strategy is introduced, predicated on real-time state conditions. This strategy informs the optimization of a cost model to determine the optimal time for replacement. A case study is included to demonstrate the practicality and effectiveness of the proposed scheduling model.

articleTitle: Profit maximization and cost minimization considering total profit function, selling price, and warranty cost
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: This study evaluates the impact of warranty pricing on products characterized by increasing failure rates, focusing on strategies involving both replacement and repair. The main goal of this study is to determine an optimal strategy that balances the maximization of the profit function against the minimization of warranty costs during the warranty period. Recognizing the interplay between warranty durations and selling prices, a novel linear warranty period pricing model is introduced. This model aids industry professionals in effectively setting product prices and determining warranty length to enhance overall profitability. Additionally, the research offers managerial insights for developing competitive warranty policies and pricing strategies. The analysis demonstrates that under certain plausible conditions, this warranty-based pricing framework not only simplifies the pricing process with suitable warranty coverage but also achieves near-optimal profit levels and secures a larger market share for manufacturers. The practical applicability of the suggested methodology is presented through numerical examples.

articleTitle: Durability analysis of connecting rod mechanisms based on physics of failure
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: With the development of military technology, the mechanisms used in military equipment require higher reliability and longer lifespans. Addressing the challenge of ensuring the long lifespan of connecting rod mechanisms and the difficulty of conducting durability tests on each model, this paper analyzes the lifespan of connecting rod mechanisms under reciprocating operating conditions using fault physics and finite element methods. Additionally, the sensitivity of connecting rod mechanism parameters on lifespan is examined, providing valuable engineering references for the design of connecting rod mechanisms.

articleTitle: A multi-modal particle filtering method for fault detection and diagnosis of digital instrumentation and control systems
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel multi-modal Particle Filtering (PF)-based method, enhanced by integrating sliding window detection and a likelihood ratio test of time series observation data, for fault detection and diagnosis in digital instrumentation and control systems. The method is applied to a digital U-shaped Tube Steam Generator (UTSG) water level control system in pressurized water reactor nuclear power plants. The system simulation and testing incorporate eight fault modes affecting various digital components such as sensors, control valves, PI controllers, and CPU modules. Comparative analyses between the multi-modal PF-based method and the Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network are conducted using simulation data as both training and validation sets in real-time diagnostic applications. The results demonstrate that the multi-modal PF-based method, with its precise mathematical and simulation model integration, achieves robust diagnosis coverage of transient faults and their generation mechanisms. The diagnostic accuracy and timeliness provided by the sliding window particle filtering algorithm offer significant insights into the operational efficiency and safety enhancements of digital process control systems.

articleTitle: An enhanced VTS radar target tracking method addressing target splitting with integrated reasoning
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: The paper introduces a target-tracking technique designed to resolve the issue of target splitting in VTS radar imagery. The method consists of three parts: firstly, background subtraction is used for target detection in radar images, which results i n a large number of split targets affecting the tracking outcome; secondly, a target splitting reasoning mechanism based on the distance between targets and their orientation is designed to improve the detection results; finally, the optimized results a re tracked using Kalman filtering and the Hungarian algorithm. The experiments in the detection phase are divided into three groups: the first group does not use the reasoning mechanism and relies solely on background subtraction, the second group uses distance as the judgment factor, and the third group uses both distance and angle for judgment. The tracking phase is divided into two groups: the first tracks the detection results without the reasoning mechanism, and the second tracks the detection results using both distance and angle judgments. The experimental results show that the reasoning mechanism can significantly improve the effectiveness of target detection. Distance is the primary criterion for determining target splitti ng, whereas angle cannot be consistently relied upon as a basis for judgment. The effectiveness of this target tracking paradigm depends on the accuracy of detection, and the inclusion of the reasoning mechanism significantly enhances the final target tracking performance.

articleTitle: An improved generative adversarial network for fault detection of bearing
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: A method employing the Convolutional Wasserstein Conditional Generative Adversarial Network (CW-CGAN) is proposed to improve fault detection under imbalanced sample conditions. Real fault signal datasets are collected and pre-processed, utilizing the CWGAN-GP model to generate additional samples and expand the training set. A Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) is developed to facilitate automatic fault feature extraction and classification. Experimental results indicate that the augmented CNN model excels in validation and test sets, accurately classifying various fault types. The effectiveness of the model is further substantiated by the visualization of the confusion matrix. This method presents an effective solution for addresses data imbalance issues in fault detection, with future work aimed at optimizing model architecture and training algorithms to enhanced accuracy and real-time performance.

articleTitle: Numerical study of erosion wear in elbow under the action of gas-solid flow
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: In this paper, a comprehensive study of the hydrodynamics and erosion wear behavior is presented in CFD (Computational Fluid Dynamics) simulations for modeling elbow structures. Both the gas velocity and particle diameter characteristics are considered in this investigation, and a detailed comparison among various erosion models and experimental data is performed. A series of CFD numerical simulations have been conducted for the 90-degree elbow to facilitate a detailed analysis of hydrodynamics and erosion behavior, including static pressure, erosion area and erosion rate. The results indicate that the erosion rate at the elbow position is significantly influenced by different erosion models. Both gas velocity and particle diameter emerge as crucial parameters in capturing the hydrodynamic behavior and erosion wear phenomena. We suggest the erosion model could be refined by integrating the factory-site sensor monitoring data and machine learning method to achieve more precise and near-real-time simulation results, which could enhance the maintenance and support of the pipeline systems in industrial applications.

articleTitle: Study of product production quality risk identification based on fault data
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: In this paper, within the framework of intelligent transformation for product production quality risk control, a risk identification model based on fault data from the production link is developed. Drawing upon the analytical principles of Quality Function Deployment (QFD), the proposed method for identifying production quality risks using fault data is structured into three stages of knowledge extraction. The initial stage consolidates disparate raw data into semi-structured electronic document data. The subsequent stage generates fault abstraction data employing text structuring and regular expression techniques among other methods. The final stage leverages the Biterm Topic Model (BTM) and K-Means algorithm for extracting knowledge elements and conducting association clustering analysis. An empirical analysis is conducted using product data to perform association analysis of product faults and cluster analysis of quality management factors, thereby demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed model and methodology.

articleTitle: Research on bolt axial force measurement method based on the combination of ultrasonic longitudinal wave and trailing pulse
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: High-strength bolts are widely used in applications such as fans, sealed containers, and mechanical transmission devices, where ensuring the consistency of axial pre-tightening force is crucial for enhancing connection and seal reliability. Traditional torque methods for measuring bolt axial force often face challenges due to various industrial friction factors, resulting in significant measurement discrepancies. To overcome these limitations, this paper introduces an ultrasonic method to precisely measure bolt axial force, utilizing a novel approach that combines ultrasonic longitudinal waves with trailing pulses. This method notably simplifies the measurement process by eliminating the need to account for bolt length and reduces the complexity of transducer design, requiring only the design of a longitudinal wave transducer. The propagation characteristics of trailing pulses are analyzed using ray tracing techniques, and the study further explores the relationship between the travel time ratio of trailing pulses and longitudinal waves and the bolt axial force. The viability of this approach is validated th rough both simulation and experimental methods, revealing a linear correlation between ultrasonic time measurement (D) and bolt axial force (F), with a measurement error under 5%.

articleTitle: Multi-objectiveQ-learning approach of operation mode control and predictive maintenance for phased mission manufacturing systems
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: Phased Mission Manufacturing Systems (PMMSs) experience multiple operational phases throughout their lifecycle, each characterized by distinct mission profiles and production demands. In each phase, manufacturers typically prioritize different objectives when making Operation and Maintenance (O&M) decisions. However, existing O&M optimization methods generally focus on a single objective, such as minimizing makespan or maximizing remaining useful life, which does not fully address the varying demands of different phases. To bridge this gap, we propose a multi-objective optimization method for equipment Operation Mode Control (OMC) and Predictive Maintenance (PdM) in PMMSs that adapts to shifts in mission phases. Our main contributions include: 1) the development of an operation status index system for equipment within PMMSs that integrates optimization objectives of productivity, reliability, workpiece quality, and energy consumption, 2) the use of dynamic weight coefficients to identify and prioritize key objective functions in different phases and the application of the TOPSIS method to formulate the optimization objective based on these weighted indices, and 3) the implementation of a Q-Learning algorithm for mode control and PdM optimization. The effectiveness of the proposed method has been validated through an industrial case study involving a nuclear fuel rod shielding component manufacturing system.

articleTitle: Reliability evaluation of fuzz button contacts with random initial values
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: Fuzz button contacts are a novel type of electrical contact device, primarily used for connections between printed circuit boards within chassis or modules, as well as between printed circuits boards and chips. However, variability in the production process introduces significant variability in the initial values, which substantially influences their reliability assessment.At present, there are few studies on the reliability evaluation of fuzz button contacts in domestic and foreign literature. In this paper, the influence of high temperature environment on the properties of fuzz button contacts was studied by experiment. Afte r the experiment, the pressing force of fuzz button contacts decreased and the length became shorter. Based on this paper, a Wiener process model with random initial value is proposed, the nonlinear degradation data is linearly converted by using the time - scale transformation model, and the relation between sample lifetimes and high temperature is described by using Arrhenius model. With the maximum likelihood estimation (MLE) method, the model parameters are estimated by integral statistics of all performance degradation data, and the reliability of fuzz button contacts is predicted success.

articleTitle: A new part-oriented test equipment for evaluating the mechanical characteristics of copper alloy spring materials
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
