abstract: Copper alloy spring materials are widely used in electromechanical components for carrying mechanical load and current load. The mechanical characteristics of such materials are closely related to the reliability and serviceability of components used in harsh environment. In this paper, a new automated test equipment for evaluating the mechanical characteristics of real part within the component is developed. The stress relaxation test and mechanical fatigue test could be carried out individually. Furthermore, the effects of temperature and mechanical load on the degradation behavior was demonstrated, without the need for a whole component level testing.

articleTitle: Research on feedback and disposal mechanism of equipment quality problem
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: This paper examines the feedback and disposal mechanisms for equipment quality problem, with a detailed focus on the Problem Quality Defect Report and the Alert System. The organizational structure of the Problem Quality Defect Report, including the Originator, Originating Point, Screening Point, Action Point, and Support Point. Similarly, the Alert System is structured with a chair, vice chair, temporary participants, an alert focal point, and an alert coordinator. These mechanisms clearly delineate responsibilities to foster collaborative and highly integrated processes. To enhance the efficiency of these feedback and disposal mechanisms, the paper proposes several improvements: clarifying relevant regulations, establishing a structured screening process, and creating mechanisms for common problem alerts.

articleTitle: AC series arc fault detection device based on multiple metrics and Random Forest
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: AC series arc faults in power distribution systems present significant fire risks, necessitating the development of a device capable of precisely detecting such arcs to ensure equipment reliability. The primary challenge involves differentiating fault currents from normal operational currents due to similar amplitudes and diverse types of loads. This research tackles these challenges by initially developing an apparatus to capture arc characteristic parameters. Employing an ARM microcontroller and FPGA, this device samples arc currents and calculates their characteristics. These parameters are then used to train a Random Forest algorithm, which generates a model capable of accurately classifying arc fault types based on these characteristics. This model is subsequently implemented on an ARM microcontroller for experimental validation of the device's accuracy in detecting arc faults. Experimental results affirm that the device proficiently identifies arc fault currents under various load conditions promptly and provides a dependable fire warning mechanism.

articleTitle: An improved method for estimating bootstrap confidence interval of quantile function
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: This paper presents an improved method for estimating the bootstrap confidence interval of the quantile function, aimed at precisely assessing the distribution of product performance. The method begins by refining the quantile function estimation technique, integrating maximum entropy with fractional probability weighted moments, and developing a single-loop optimization method that is both efficient and robust for determining distribution parameters. This approach is then augmente d with an improved bootstrap sampling method to estimate the confidence interval of the quantile function. The proposed methodology capitalizes on the strengths of combining probability-weighted moments with maximum entropy and the bootstrap technique. It is characterized by its distribution type independence and not sensitive to outliers samples. Moreover, it effectively determines the confidence interval of the quantile function, even from very small samples. The superiority of thi s method is comprehensively validated through various test cases.

articleTitle: Design of reference architecture for testing and evaluation of communication equipment driven by digital twin
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: With its capabilities for virtual-real symbiosis, fusion, and interaction, digital twin (DT) technology has become a pivotal tool for the digital transformation of communication equipment testing and evaluation (T&E). Unlike typical mechanical equipment, the physical activities of communication equipment encompass the transmission and exchange of information and energy across physics, electromagnetism, and information domains. This paper explores the unique challenges encountered in the T&E of communication equipment and introduces the concept of communication network equipment T&E driven by digital twin technology. Building on this, a reference architecture based on the five-dimensional model of digital twin is proposed, providing a theoretical framework for applying digital twin technology in communication equipment T&E.

articleTitle: Complex product quality diagnosis framework based on association rule mining
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: Quality diagnosis serves as a critical tool in quality control, playing a pivotal role in identifying potential quality issues and thereby enhancing the overall quality management of enterprise products. However, conventional quality diagnosis methods often underutilize the valuable data relationships between process parameters and quality indicators, resulting in challenges in providing a clear diagnostic foundation for quality anomalies, thereby complicating quality control efforts. To address this issue within the context of modern manufacturing data characteristics, this study proposes a product quality diagnosis method based on association rule mining. The methodology begins with the application of the Partitioning Around Medoid (PAM) algorithm for data pre-processing, including clustering and discrete coding. Subsequently, the Frequent Pattern Growth (FP-Growth) algorithm is employed to mine rules from the discretely coded data. Finally, the Whale Optimization Algorithm (WOA) is leveraged to extract optimal rules and establish a comprehensive rule library for effectively tracing the root causes of anomalies, thereby enabling precise quality diagnosis of products.

articleTitle: Research of the differential power control method for novel wind turbine
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: The innovative wind turbine features a variable ratio transmission system, consists of a differential gear train alongside a speed-regulating motor. This system enables the turbine to adjust its output independently of wind speeds. Notably, the synchronous generator integrated within this setup directly connects to the power grid, eliminating the need for a frequency converter. This design ensures that while the wind rotor's speed fluctuates, the generator rotor maintains a steady speed, achieving a variable speed but constant frequency operation. This seamless integration enhances efficiency and stability in energy production. Research on the power control strategy for this type of wind turbine remains unexplored. So, the Differential Power Control (DPC) technique, a pivotal method in wind turbine management, has been meticulously analyzed across varying wind conditions, specifically focusing on speeds that diverge from the standard rated s peed. This examination utilizes the interrelated dynamics of the wind energy utilization rate (Cp), pitch angle (β), and tip speed ratio (λ) to opti mize power output. A detailed simulation was conducted using SIMULINK to construct a 1500 kW wind turbine model, which integrates differential speed regulation. Various wind speeds served as inputs to assess the model's responsiveness and efficiency under fluctuating environmental conditions. The effectiveness of the Differential Power Control (DPC) technique in managing grid-connected wind turbines with variable speed regulation is validated through a comparative analysis of simulation outputs against theoretical benchmarks of critical parameters.

articleTitle: Simulation study on dynamic mechanical performance of off-center pin and socket of high-speed backplane connector
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: High-speed electrical connectors are widely used in electronic, communication, and computer equipment, ideally requiring precise alignment of the pin and socket. However, achieving perfect alignment during practical use is often challenging because the centers of the pin and socket may not align during the insertion process. This misalignment can lead to issues such as contact failure and socket damage. Therefore, this study establishes an equivalent pin-and-socket connector model to investigate the contact mechanics between centered and off-center pin and socket during the insertion and extraction process. The results indicate that the off-center pin and socket make the insertion and extraction process more unstable than the centered pin and socket. Additionally, the forces required for insertion and extraction increase significantly for the off-center pin and socket.

articleTitle: Informer neural network-based prediction of degradation trajectory of energy meter clock battery life
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: Accurate prediction of the life degradation trajectory of the clock battery, a critical component of the power meter, is essential for assessing the reliability of the device. Addressing the computational inefficiency and limited generalization capabilitie s of traditional empirical recession models, this paper introduces a prediction model based on the Informer neural network. The battery degradation data are initially segmented and reassembled using a sliding window strategy. The encoder-decoder structure is then employed to achieve multilevel feature extraction from the input sequences. By setting various prediction starting points, the model demonstrates high sensitivity in predicting battery degradation under temperature conditions identical to those in the training set. Additionally, the model is capable of predicting the degradation trajectories of batteries under different temperature conditions, such as 60℃.

articleTitle: Research on simulation modeling of moling flow of phenolic thermal protection material RTM
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: This article develops a simulation model for the injection flow of phenolic thermal protection materials, employing a method that ensures mutual validation between experimental data and simulation results. Specifically, a molding experiment platform was established for the Resin Transfer Molding (RTM) process, suitable for conducting RTM filling experiments. During these experiments, parameters such as density, porosity, and volume fraction of the reinforcing fibers were measured, and filling experiments were conducted using anisotropic fibers. The simulation model was constructed using Fluent software, utilizing the Volume of Fluid (VOF) model to track the flow front. Material models were established, the mesh was divided, and the solver settings were configured to support the simulation process. Comparative analyses were conducted between the simulation results and both one-dimensional and two-dimensional experimental data, employing isotropic materials as controls.

articleTitle: Accelerated degradation modeling and transfer of multilayer ceramic capacitors
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: Multilayer ceramic capacitors (MLCCs) are extensively utilized across various industrial sectors, and their failure can result in significant losses. Thus, it is crucial to investigate the degradation of MLCCs under varying environmental stresses. In this study, multilayer ceramic capacitors produced with diverse parameters are examined. Environmental stresses, specifically different temperatures and voltages, are applied to conduct accelerated degradation tests on these capacitors. Through the fitting of degradation data, accelerated degradation models for the capacitors under different stresses are developed. Analysis of these models elucidates the degradation pattern of the capacitors, offering valuable insights for understanding capacitor failure. Moreover, by transferring MLCCs of different specifications but identical materials from the same manufacturer and production line, the relationship between manufacturing parameters and model coefficients can be inferred. This is significant for predicting the lifespan of MLCCs.

articleTitle: Reliability analysis of multi-state system considering interdependent performance conversion
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: Multi-state systems characterized by interdependent performance conversion represent a complex category where system components exist in multiple states, each with distinct performances that are interdependent. Significant research has focused on modeling and analyzing such systems, as their reliability analysis is vital for numerous practical applications. This paper introduces a system model for multi-state systems with interdependent performance conversion. Additionally, it expands the universal generating function (UGF) method to analyze the system reliability of the proposed model, encompassing both reliability probability and expected instantaneous performance deficiency (EIPD). To demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed model and method, two numerical examples are presented, one featuring linear interdependence and the other non-linear interdependence.

articleTitle: Bearing fault diagnosis based on wavelet packet energy spectrum with extreme learning machine (ELM)
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: Rolling bearings, as critical components of rotating machinery, support and reduce friction in mechanical systems. Failures in these bearings can not only disrupt project progress but also lead to substantial economic losses and potentially cause casualties. Consequently, research into rolling bearing fault diagnosis is of paramount importance. This paper addresses the problem of bearing failure by proposing a fault diagnosis method that combines wavelet packet energy spectrum analysis with an Extreme Learning Machine (ELM). To replicate real-world noisy operational environments, high-intensity noise is added to the collected signal samples. These samples undergo wavelet packet decomposition and reconstruction for energy feature extraction, with the band energy being selected via the wavelet packet energy spectrum. The extracted energy features are then used to construct a dataset that is input into the ELM model for multiple training iterations. The diagnostic accuracy of the model reached 95.1429±2.87%, demonstrating the method's effectiveness in bearing fault diagnosis and its ability to enhance the recognition and diagnosis capabilities of bearing fault signals.

articleTitle: Study on common cause failure in multiple redundant system
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: To enhance the safety of nuclear power plants, redundant designs are frequently implemented within safety systems. Probabilistic safety analysis further reveals that common cause failures (CCF) of redundant systems significantly contribute to risk. When a specific component fails, it not only impacts the redundant design but also affects the functioning of components that have not failed. This paper builds upon the common cause failure model widely utilized in probabilistic safety analysis. It explores and establishes an accurate quantitative method for assessing common cause failures in the context of component failure. This approach aims to provide a rational evaluation of the safety levels of nuclear power plants and support the risk assessment and management efforts. The efficacy of this method is demonstrated through a case study analysis of a multi-redundancy design.

articleTitle: Life prediction of O-ring with accelerated performance degradation equation
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: This article first conducts artificial accelerated aging tests on O-ring seals based on the principle of time-temperature equivalence, obtaining the compression permanent deformation rates of fluorine rubber, nitrile rubber, and ethylene propylene rubber O-rings under different experimental conditions. Subsequently, an aging kinetics equation is established to describe the relationship between aging parameters and aging time. This equation is used to determine the aging reaction rate at the corresponding accelerated aging temperature, to extrapolate the aging reaction rate at the actual usage or storage temperature, and to calculate the lifespan based on a given failure threshold. Finally, based on accelerated degradation data, a reliability evaluation method is used to describe the distribution pattern of the overall product life using statistical distribution.

articleTitle: A developed Plan-Do-Check-Act and contextual teaching and learning model
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: Despite some application of Contextual Teaching and Learning (CTL) theories in practice, their effectiveness has not been prominent, necessitating comprehensive optimization. To enhance the quality and the success of typical processes like education activities, this study integrates CTL with Deming's PDCA (Plan-Do-Check-Act) cycle theory. Through the stages of planning, implementation, and evaluation, the CTL model has been significantly improved. Methodologically, the study employs an inductive approach and experimental methods for data analysis. Results show significant improvements in the mentioned activities and enhances of performance and satisfaction of stakeholders like the population involved with the optimized PDCA & CTL model. The results of this paper also confirmed the efficacy of the proposed method in process quality improvement .

articleTitle: Integrated optimization model of economic manufacturing quantity and hybrid condition-based maintenance for continuous-production systems
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: Continuous production line degeneration is commonly observed in complex manufacturing systems, potentially leading to substantial financial losses and safety risks. In this paper, we propose a model that integrates Economic Manufacturing Quantity (EMQ) optimization with hybrid maintenance scheduling. This model leverages the health information of the production machine extracted through condition monitoring (CM) and employs stochastic processes to describe manufacturing deterioration. The maintenance strategy in this hybrid approach encompasses three components: (a) age-dependent preventive maintenance; (b) CM-dependent condition-based maintenance (CBM); and (c) reactive corrective maintenance. Preventive maintenance is scheduled at production halt points within each production lot, preceded by limited CMs. At each CM, the control limit for CBM is dynamically adjusted based on the amount of CM and defined by a reliability criterion. This study aims to jointly optimize the production lot size and reliability criteria to minimize the expected cost per production cycle. A case study on the converter system in a steel plant demonstrates the applicability of the proposed joint strategy.

articleTitle: Research on intelligent alarm analysis of nuclear power plant secondary loop system based on multi-level flow model
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: Due to the intricate and interrelated nature of nuclear power plant systems, any anomaly can trigger a casc ade of alarms. Operators must skillfully assess the system's status amidst this deluge of alarm information and promptly implement appropriate mitigation measures. To address these challenges, an intelligent alarm analysis method based on a Multi-Level Flow Model (MFM) is employed, facilitating the analysis of causal relationships between alarms. Utilizing the secondary loop system and the Low-Pressure Feedwater Heater System (ABP) of a Pressurized Water Reactor (PWR) nuclear power plant as research subjects, a multi-layer flow model for the ABP system was constructed. This model, based on the steady-state operation at full power of the nuclear power plant, clarifies the causal relationships between functions and targets. The mul tilayer flow model was validated using an alarm scenario triggered by an insertion fault superimposed under steady-state operating conditions. The results indicate that the system can filter information, identify root causes, and provide operator s with effective comprehensive diagnostic information. This reduces the impact of a large volume of information on diagnostic tasks and enhances the safety and reliability of nuclear power plant operations.

articleTitle: Residual life prediction method for rolling bearings considering random shock effect
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: This study introduces a bearing residual life prediction method that accounts for the influence of random shocks, acknowledging the potential safety implications arising from the neglect of such factors. Firstly, the degradation process of the bearing is characterized using a nonlinear Wiener process, while the shock process is modeled by a Poisson process. Subsequently, leveraging the established degradation model and the concept of the first attainment time, the residual life probability density function and its approximate analytical solution are derived. Finally, the proposed method's effectiveness and practicality are validated using a bearing dataset.

articleTitle: Simulation and analysis of sliding bearing durability of marine gear pump
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: In this paper, durability simulation analysis is conducted for marine gear pump plain bearings, with the oil film pressure simulated under varying coaxial speeds and lubrication conditions. The ICEM mesh division module under ANSYS software and the FLUENT fluid simulation module are utilized to simulate the two-phase flow problem under actual working conditions using the Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) method. Subsequently, the bearing static characteristic parameters under variable load and dual working conditions are solved to provide the key parameters required for subsequent life prediction. Through CAE simulation analysis, as outlined in the plain bearing design manual, the simulation results under different lubrication conditions at various speeds are determined, and life prediction is conducted using a strain-fatigue life prediction curve. The findings from the simulation analysis and life prediction reveal that, as the sliding bearing is a component withi n a system designed for one-time, short-term use, it meets the design life requirements. Under maintenance conditions that involve cleaning and replacing lubricating oil post-completion of equipment tasks, the sliding bearing can maintain normal operation without experiencing fatigue failure, assuming no other components or system elements fail.

articleTitle: A high-dimensional reliability analysis method via subspace updating and Gaussian process
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: The subspace-based surrogate modeling method has become increasingly popular in high-dimensional reliability analysis due to its effectiveness in mitigating the “curse of dimensionality.” Establishing an accurate subspace through dimensionality reduction is crucial for ensuring reliable outcomes in these methodologies. However, traditional approaches often perform dimensionality reduction solely based on sample responses and gradients, which can compromise subspace accuracy. To address this issue, this paper presents a novel high-dimensional reliability analysis method that integrates manifold optimization with Gaussian process (GP). Initially, the slice inverse regression technique is used to determine the parameter s of the initial projection matrix, and an initial GP model is constructed within the projected subspace. To enhance the precision of dimensionality reduction, the projection matrix is evaluated using responses from the GP model within the subspace, followed by calibration through manifold optimization techniques. Finally, Monte Carlo simulation is performed using the subspace GP model to estimate the failure probability. The proposed method’s effectiveness is validated through two high -dimensional case studies.

articleTitle: Research on improving the reliability of aerospace components based on PSO-VMD-FFT dense modal frequency identification method
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: This article focuses on aerospace engine components and proposes the PSO-VMD-FFT method for identifying dense modal frequencies, addressing the challenge of difficult identification of dense modal frequencies in structures. The method utilizes the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) algorithm to find the optimal combination of the decomposition level K and penalty factor α , thereby enhancing the decomposition accuracy of VMD. Subsequently, experiments were conducted on a scaled-down model of a rocket engine component using the LMS Testlab experimental platform. The PSO-VMD-FFT method was applied to analyze the measured acceleration response curves, extract modal frequencies, and compare the results with those from LMS software analysis. The relative error was within 3%, meeting the accuracy requirements and enhancing the reliability of structural design and improvement of aerospace products.

articleTitle: Reliability analysis of ultimate strength of FPSO based on maximum entropy method
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: Due to prolonged offshore production, the structural reliability of floating production storage and offloading (FPSO) units is continually challenged. This study evaluates the structural reliability of FPSOs over their design life, taking into account uncertainties in material properties, plate thickness, and load. The ultimate strength of the FPSO hull girder is determined using a direct calculation method based on an assumed section stress distribution, and the probability distribution of the limit state function is established using the maximum entropy method (MEM). The failure probability of the FPSO during its design life is ascertained through direct integration of the probability distribution function. This failure probability is subsequently compared with results obtained using direct Monte Carlo simulation. The findings indicate that the MEM, as introduced in this study, can rapidly and accurately determine the ultimate strength reliability of FPSO hull girders, providing a crucial reference for the structural safety assessment of FPSOs.

articleTitle: Experimental study on the effect of load on the residual fatigue life of 7050-T7451 aluminum alloy structures containing crack damage
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: Fatigue tests were conducted on 7050-T7451 aluminum alloy, a commonly used material in aircraft, under various stress levels utilizing a random load spectrum. The crack extension data were statistically analyzed to determine the mean remaining fatigue life and the dispersion coefficient for structures with different crack damage sizes. The analysis reveals that the mean remaining fatigue life of structures decreases as the crack damage size increases. At the same crack damage size, higher stress levels result in a shorter remaining fatigue life. Furthermore, as the damage size increases, the difference in the effect of varying stress levels on the remaining fatigue life diminishes. The dispersion coefficient of the remaining fatigue life also increases with the crack damage size. Under the same crack damage conditions, higher stress levels correspond to larger dispersion coefficient values, and the difference in dispersion of the remaining fatigue life between different stress levels increases with larger damage sizes. Considering the dispersion factor, the remaining fatigue life decreases with increasing damage size, with the dispersion coefficient rising sharply beyond a certain damage size. Specifically, the remaining fatigue life of a test specimen with a 5 mm crack damage size decreases to 2.8% of that of a specimen with a 0.5 mm damage size at a medium stress level. A critical crack size of 5 mm is identified, which is less than 50% of the critical size designed for conventional fracture control.

articleTitle: Weapon system of systems mission reliability allocation method based on RBD model and dynamic programming
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: In the design of systems of systems, it is crucial to effectively manage equipment reliability through precise reliability allocation. However, existing research on reliability allocation methods tailored specifically for systems of systems remains sparse. Standard practices often apply allocation methods such as equal allocation, AGREE allocation, AHP allocation, and score allocation, which are typically unconstrained and do not account for the redundancy relationships among units, thus imposing unrealistically high-reliability demands on individual units. Among constrained methods, the direct search method only considers parallel relationships, limiting its applicability. In contrast, dynamic programming accommodates various constraints, rendering it mo re appropriate for systems of systems. This paper introduces a mission reliability allocation method for systems of systems, leveraging the Reliability Block Diagram (RBD) model and dynamic programming. This approach integrates redundancy relationships and additional constraints into the allocation process. An objective function aimed at maximizing basic reliability is established, incorporating constraints derived from mission reliability requirements and expert evaluations to formulate a comprehensive mission reliability allocation model. A novel algorithm is then proposed to determine the optimal allocation, which is validated through a case study and comparative analysis. The findings demonstrate that this method effectively lower s the reliability demands on individual components while ensuring the overall mission reliability meets established standards.

articleTitle: Fault risk assessment of railway turnout ballast clearing machine based on AHP-fuzzy comprehensive evaluation method
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: To evaluate the fault risk of a small railway turnout ballast clearing machine, this paper employs the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) to assess reliability based on subjective experience. Additionally, the fuzzy comprehensive evaluation method is utilized to quantify the risk. This combined approach facilitates the construction of an objective and rational risk assessment system for the ballast-clearing machine. The four main fault factors, which include rake claw fault, bearing fault, chain fault, and sprocket fault, are analysed using the Analytic Hierarchy Process, and the weight value for each type of fault is determined. A fuzzy relationship matrix is then established using the fuzzy comprehensive evaluation method, and a comprehensive evaluation of each fault factor is conducted to obtain the probability of various faults occurring in the ballast-clearing machine. Based on the results, the fault grade of the ballast clearing machine is assessed to be of medium risk.

articleTitle: Modified information criterion for change-point gamma process model
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: In practical scenarios, the degradation process of components like often exhibits multi-stage characteristics due to internal degradation mechanisms and external environmental factors. For precise analysis of the reliability characteristics of these components, identifying the change-point location is essential. It enables researchers and engineers to select or develop a change-point model that accurately depicts these behaviors. Traditional methods to detect change points are time-consuming; therefore, employing a modified information criterion method to detect the existence and estimate the change-point location presents a viable alternative. The efficacy of this method is evaluated through several numerical simulations. Subsequently, this approach is applied to metal oxide semiconductor field-effect transistor data to demonstrate its practical application.

articleTitle: A pattern recognition method using big data for device behaviour with linear features
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: In recent years, big data technology has rapidly developed, yet research on device behavior recognition based on big data monitoring remains relatively scarce. To address this gap, a big data-based pattern recognition method for device behavior with linear characteristics is proposed. This research aims to identify the behavior and activities of devices through big data-based pattern recognition algorithms to ensure their normal operation. Initially, the required sequence data, window data, and corresponding formal structural expressions are constructed from the raw data. Following preprocessing, the big data is cleaned, and rules and calculation methods for handling abnormal data, such as mutations and losses, are formulated. The device behavior identification method classifies data into three basic states based on the changing characteristics of the data. The logical relationship between device behavior and data state changes is studied, revealing that the change in data state flow is crucial for accurately judging or determining device behavior. A graphical simulation of big data on device behavior is provided, and the simulation experiment visually displays the data changes associated with device behavior activities. The results effectively verify the proposed method's effectiveness.

articleTitle: Study on the dynamic response of multi-physics field coupling in AC contactor electromagnetic mechanism
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: For an in-depth analysis of the dynamic response of the contactor's electromagnetic system, this paper initially calculates the mechanical movement and temperature field distribution of the electromagnetic mechanism by evaluating the coupling between the magnetic field and the circuit. It implements multi-physics coupling of mechanical, electrical, magnetic, and thermal fields in an indirectly coupled manner, and establishes a digital prototype model of a commercial contactor. Subsequently, the dynamic response of the AC contactor at room temperature and after multiple operations was calculated. A comparison with experimental results validated the precision of the prototype model in forecasting the dynamic behavior of AC contactors. This paper can serve as a reference for studying the dynamic response of similar contactors and provide the basis for evaluating the reliability a nd optimizing the design of AC contactors.

articleTitle: Lithium-ion battery RUL prediction based on multi-modal historical data
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: A comprehensive assessment of satellite lithium-ion batteries is essential for ensuring the operational reliability of in-orbit satellite platforms. The modeling of newly developed satellite lithium-ion battery models often encounters challenges due to limited historical data, which complicates rapid assessment necessary for minimizing battery testing costs and shortening the installation interval before deployment. This paper introduces a novel approach utilizing multi-modal historical data for predicting the remaining useful life (RUL) of new satellite lithium-ion battery models. The proposed method comprises three main stages: Initially, a Transformer network-based model is trained using data from older models to establish a base model that captures the general degradation trajectory. Subsequently, a transfer learning model is developed by fine-tuning the base model with data from the new models and aligning the model parameters with the unique degradation characteristics of the new batteries. Lastly, this transfer learning model is applied to provide accurate RUL predictions for new lithium-ion battery models. Experimental validation on two distinct datasets demonstrates that the proposed method significantly enhances the accuracy of RUL predictions, achieving minimal max percentage error and mean absolute error of 4.63% and 10.7, respectively, with limited historical training data.

articleTitle: Composite layer evaluation based on multi-scale finite element analysis
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: FRP (fiber-reinforced plastics) composite materials are extensively utilized across various sectors, including aviation and navigation, making the study of their layers significantly valuable from an engineering perspective. This research evaluates twenty different types of FRP laminates subjected to low-speed impacts. A multi-scale model for various FRP laminates was developed, and simulations of low-speed impacts were conducted. The gray correlation evaluation method was employed to assess the impact performance of different fiberglass plates. The results reveal that the outcomes from multi-scale finite element analysis are in close agreement with experimental data, confirming its effectiveness in evaluating the layers of FRP composites. The impact performance of the FRP composites varied, with the maximum R-value recorded at 0.7490 and the lowest at 0.3934. These findings are instrumental in assessing the impact properties of FRP composite materials.

articleTitle: Method for reliability analysis based on RBF surrogate model and evidence theory
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: This paper introduces a research method that assesses the reliability of evidential theory through the application of Radial Basis Function (RBF) agent models. This approach combines the function learning capabilities of RBF agent models with the uncertainty processing strengths of evidential theory to model and predict reliability issues effectively. Initially, RBF agent models are utilized to simulate historical data, creating functional models that form the basis for further analysis. Subsequently, evidential theory is applied to perform a reliability analysis on the predictive results generated by these models. The efficacy and feasibility of this method have been substantiated through real-world case studies, demonstrating its practical application in reliability assessment.

articleTitle: Modal analysis of propellant casing for solid rocket engines based on CEEMDAN
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: The structural design and manufacturing of spacecraft require meticulous attention to lightweight characteristics, rigidity, and stability, which are fundamental for the success of space missions. As a result, designs must be subjected to rigorous analys is, testing, and validation to ensure structural reliability and safety. However, the use of Empirical Mode Decomposition (EMD) methods for identifying dense modes presents challenges due to endpoint effects, which can compromise the accuracy of modal parameter identification. This study evaluates the performance of EMD and its enhanced variant, Complete Ensemble Empirical Mode Decomposition with Adaptive Noise (CEEMDAN), in identifying complex signals with closely spaced frequencies. The analysis reveals that CEEMDAN significantly outperforms EMD by effectively mitigating the endpoint effect through the application of Autoregressive (AR) extension techniques. Simulation experiments conducted on the propellant casing of solid rocket engines using ANSYS software demonstrate that CEEMDAN is particularly effective in handling low-frequency and widely dispersed signals, although it shows only moderate performance in decomposing high-frequency and concentrated signals. These findings offer crucial insights for spacecraft structural design and manufacturing, especially in addressing c omplex signal challenges and improving decomposition accuracy.

articleTitle: Ductile domain of aluminium-silicon glass in high-speed milling
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: The ductile glass-cutting method not only enhances processing efficiency and reduces costs but also yields smoother surfaces compared to grinding. The transformation of material toughness during the cutting process is crucial for improving the surface integrity of the machined product, enhancing efficiency, and extending the lifespan of the product. Experimental observations using Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM) revealed that the cross-section of the brittle material, aluminosilicate glass, exhibits ductile domain characteristics during ultra-high-speed micro-milling with a multi-faceted (30-edge) tool. These findings provide valuable insights for adjusting optimization parameters in future extreme milling experiments and aligning with actual production demands.

articleTitle: Fault correlation analysis of the spindle system subsystem of a heavy-duty CNC boring and milling machine
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: Due to the coupling fault between complex system structures and subsystems, it is difficult to determine the fault location and fault source location, and it is proposed to construct a directed diagram of fault transmission of the spindle system based on the fault data of the spindle system. With the help of the theory of node importance solving in the PageRank algorithm, the fault-related influence degree and fault-related influence degree of the spindle subsystem are calculated, and the obtained affected degree value table can quickly locate the fault location of the spindle system. The derived impact value table can serve as a foundation for diagnosing the fault source, thereby facilitating the formulation of maintenance plans. This is important for improving the reliability of machine tools.

articleTitle: Fatigue characteristics analysis of carbon fiber laminates with multiple initial cracks
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: Carbon fiber laminates are composite materials renowned for their high specific strength, high modulus ratio, and lightweight properties, making them widely utilized for their exceptional performance. However, these laminates often face cyclic loading conditions, leading to fatigue issues exacerbated by inherent manufacturing defects. This study specifically examines carbon fiber laminates with initial cracks, conducting static and fatigue tests on multiple cracks while varying crack length, inter-crack angle, and distance. Fatigue simulations based on Paris' law are performed for laminates with prefabricated cracks. The research investigates the load-bearing characteristics and intrinsic relationships of cracks within carbon fiber laminates under varying parameters, explores the crack propagation process, and conducts life analysis under fatigue loads.

articleTitle: A general framework for optimal discrete-time preventive replacement models
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: Maintenance optimization enhances the procedures and strategies for maintaining assets, equipment, or systems, thereby improving performance, reliability, and cost-effectiveness. This paper proposes a general framework for optimizing maintenance replacement strategies in a discrete-time setting. To address multiple replacement options occurring as simultaneous events, we define the profound concept of priority for more replacement option. Initially, the analysis focuses on optimal preventive replacement policies that minimize expected costs in each model by prioritizing replacements. Subsequently, the discussion expands to a comprehensive framework that includes age replacement models, minimal repair models, and block replacement models.

articleTitle: Equipment general quality characteristics evaluation: planning of questionnaire content for qualitative subjective data collection
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: As the emphasis on enhancing user experience grows in the design and production of equipment, rigorous research on users' subjective perceptions of general quality characteristics become increasingly important. However, there remains a shortage of tools for collecting subjective data on these characteristics. This article analyzes the internal relationships between general quality characteristics through structural equation modeling and constructs a comprehensive questionnaire addressing five dimensions: equipment suitability and usability, task execution difficulty, workload, supportability element supply efficacy, and human-system interaction experience. The questionnaire items have been meticulously crafted to closely align with the typical manner of describing user experiences. Additionally, empirical questionnaires are available for consultation, facilitating th e swift development of a valid and reliable questionnaire. The article also presents the mapping relationship between the constructed questionnaire items and the general quality characteristics, obtaining the weights of each item through expert scoring. Reliability and validity tests confirm that the questionnaire possesses good reliability and validity, making it a useful tool for collecting subjective data on the general quality characteristics of equipment.

articleTitle: Early prediction of cycle life of supercapacitors based on GA-LSTM
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: Supercapacitors are increasingly utilized in the new energy automotive industry, favored for their long cycle life, high power density, and environmental sustainability. Accurately predicting the Remaining Useful Life (RUL) of supercapacitors is crucial for timely replacement and avoiding losses associated with unexpected failures. This paper introduces a novel cycle life prediction method for supercapacitors, employing a Genetic Algorithm-Long Short-Term Memory (GA-LSTM) approach. Initially, a Moving Average Filter (MAF) is applied to the degradation data of 20 different supercapacitors for noise reduction. Subsequently, a multi-task learning strategy is implemented, training the LSTM model multiple times to enhance its predictive accuracy. The Genetic Algorithm is then utilized to optimize the LSTM's hyperparameters, significantly refining the prediction model. By inputting only 10% of the test data, the trained model successfully predicts the supercapacitor’s RUL. To validate the method's efficacy, performance tests on eight diverse datasets were conducted. The results indicate that the Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) and Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of this method are maintained within 0.0041 and 0.0032, respectively, showcasing a more precise RUL prediction for supercapacitors compared to traditional LSTM approaches and those without noise reduction.

articleTitle: Load-sharing and maintenance policy for two-unit systems under dependent bivariate degradation processes
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: Given that workload allocation can significantly impact the deterioration rate of units, decision-making regarding load-sharing and maintenance must consider the complex and dynamic interactions between unit deterioration and the allocated workload. This research focuses on condition-based maintenance for a system comprising two units with mutually dependent deterioration processes. A joint optimal load-sharing and maintenance policy with flexible load-sharing is proposed for two-unit deteriorating systems under a constant total workload. The underlying deterioration process of the system, which depends on the workload allocation, is modeled using a bivariate gamma degradation process. Based on the system's deterioration state, the decision - maker determines whether to continue operating the system for an additional period with a specific load allocation ratio or to initiate maintenance on any unit. The optimization problem is formulated as a Markov decision process that minimizes the total expected cost over an infinite horizon. The properties of the proposed optimal decision policies are investigated through simulation results, and the performance of the proposed policy is evaluated by comparing it to a policy with equal workload distribution. Additionally, a sensitivity analysis is conducted to illustrate the effects of economic and deterioration dependencies on load-sharing.

articleTitle: Research on the reasoning algorithm for intelligent alarm analysis in nuclear power plants based on multi-level flow model
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: With the increasing complexity of nuclear power plant systems, traditional alarm systems struggle to provide effective early warning and response across multiple operating states and potential faults. In response, this paper proposes an intelligent alarm algorithm based on a multi-level flow model, aimed at significantly enhancing the safety and operational efficiency of nuclear power plants. Initially, the paper underscores the necessity of integrating intelligent alarm systems into the safety management of nuclear power plants. It then introduces the theoretical framework of the multilayer flow model, followed by a detailed exposition of the steps involved in designing and implementing the intelligent alarm algorithm based on this model. The adaptive capabilities and accuracy of the alarm system are also validated. In the application section, the effectiveness of t he intelligent alarm algorithm is demonstrated through a case study of an actual nuclear power plant system, verifying its superiority in fault detection and resolution. This study endeavors to develop an effective intelligent alarm solution for th e nuclear power industry, providing a theoretical foundation and practical support for the safety management and operational optimization of nuclear power plants.

articleTitle: Research on design and selection method of helical gear meshing stiffness considering tooth lead modification
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: Meshing stiffness is a crucial parameter that affects gear transmission characteristics. Accurately calculating the meshing stiffness of gears and comprehensively analyzing the influence of various factors on it are essential for providing reference and guidance for design selection. In this paper, the finite element method is employed to calculate the meshing stiffness of helical gears. Subsequently, axial modification is introduced to estimate the gear meshing stiffness after shape modification. Finally, gear meshing stiffness parameters are analyzed using numerical examples, and a gear design selection principle based on meshing stiffness is derived.

articleTitle: Period oriented weighting sparse denoising for compound faults of rolling bearing
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: Compound faults (CFs) present substantial challenges in the fault diagnosis of rolling bearings. This study introduces a novel methodology, termed Period Oriented Weighting Sparse Denoising (POWSD), designed specifically to diagnose and differentiate CFs in rolling bearings. Initially, the type of faults is determined based on the outcomes of sparse denoising. Subsequently, POWSD employs the fault periods identified for each type, calculating a new metric, FPER, which leverages the multiscale features and periodic relationships within sparse coefficients. These relationships are weighted differently at various levels, aiding in the targeted denoising of sparse coefficients during the POWSD process. Through the implementation of POWSD, repetitive impulses associated with CFs are effectively extracted and isolated. Both simulation experiments and practical tests conducted on a specialized bench confirm the efficacy of POWSD, showcasing its superior performance in denoising and separating CFs in comparison to existing methods.

articleTitle: Reliability assessment of dented pipelines transporting hydrogen by artificial neural network
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: The transportation of hydrogen energy through existing aged pipelines is a global concern, yet research on reliability assessment is limited. This work utilizes theoretical analysis, finite element (FE) simulation and an Artificial Neural Network (ANN) model to establish an assessment framework for the reliability of X52 dented pipelines transporting gaseous hydrogen. The degradation of the fracture toughness related to the hydrogen concentration was considered as the failure pattern of the pipeline. Denting and hydrogen diffusion processes were simulated using FE method. With the increasing indentation displacement, the simulation results indicated that the maximum hydrogen concentration shifted circumferentially away from the dent center of the pipelines. Using FE data from this study and the literature, an optimizable ANN model was trained through hyperparameter optimization. This led to the establishment of a reliability assessment framework for dented pipelines degraded by hydrogen, through the determinations of failure probabilities.

articleTitle: Safety analysis for deformable IoT system: a case study of wearable ECG monitoring system
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: In the field of health monitoring, the Internet of Things (IoT) is extensively utilized and is progressively advancing towards more critical applications, such as wearable electrocardiogram (ECG) monitoring systems. Despite its potential, IoT faces substantial challenges in this domain, including the need for safety analysis of IoT as deformable systems and the requirement to balance cost with safety performance. This study proposes a scenario-based approach, leveraging the innovative use of the AltaRica language for system modelling and reliability experiments. Our findings suggest that the proposed scenario-based method is broadly applicable for analysing deformable IoT systems. Using a wearable ECG monitoring system as a case study, we identify the optimal range for minimizing the failure rate of key system components. Additionally, it is noted that the impact of the repair time attributes of repairable components on overall system reliability exhibits a non-linear trend.

articleTitle: Multi-objective optimization algorithm based on electromagnetic relay parameters
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: Electromagnetic relays perform critical functions such as control, circuit switching, and safety grounding within power equipment and systems, fulfilling roles that cannot be replaced by semiconductor switches. This paper addresses the issue of low qualification rates caused by the two-step absorption and release processes in balanced force electromagnetic relays. A multi-objective optimization study is conducted on these relays, focusing on the structural parameters of the electromagnetic system. The Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm III (NSGA-III) is employed to solve the Pareto frontier solution of multi-objective higher-order functions due to its high convergence speed, search efficiency, robustness, and portability . This paper proposes a novel multi-objective optimization algorithm based on NSGA-III, utilizing Isolation Forest (iForest) and Support Vector Regression (SVR) for the structural parameter optimization of electromagnetic systems in balanced force relays. Firstly, the original data are processed using the iForest method to detect and eliminate outliers. Secondly, given the small sample s ize of the electromagnetic suction force dataset for balanced force relays, the SVR model is used to predict and expand th e dataset, thereby providing a solid data foundation for subsequent structural parameter optimization. Thirdly, constraint and objective functions are constructed, and the NSGA-III algorithm is used to predict the electromagnetic suction force through the SVR model, optimizing the structural parameters. The NSGA-III algorithm refines the structural parameters of the electromagnetic relay using data generated by the SVR model to obtain the optimal parameters. Finally, finite element simulation software verifies the results, demonstrating that the proposed method effectively identifies the optimal parameters of the electromagnetic rela y and enhances optimization efficiency.

articleTitle: An attempt to utilize functional modeling for enhanced application code analysis
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: Due to the complex and highly interdependent relationships among parameters in system programs, anomalies can lead to abnormal propagation, thereby degrading system performance and potentially inducing measurement or execution errors within the control system. Such errors can adversely affect the stability and safety of a nuclear reactor. To address this issue, this study introduces a function modeling-based analysis method for data anomaly traceback and parameter tuning assistance. This method enables root cause inference of anomalies when program outputs significantly deviate from expected values, facilitating further investigation. For parameter tuning, the method simplifies the direct model of the program through functional combinations, elucidating the data flow of critical parameters. This enhances and accelerates parameter-tuning efforts. Using a radiation dose calculation program as a case study, this paper demonstrates that the proposed method effectively identifies potential root causes of anomalies, simplifies the direct model, clarifies the interrelations among critical parameters, facilitates parameter tuning, and reduces risks associated with human error.

articleTitle: Time-space-dependent kinematic reliability of planar mechanism considering joint clearance
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: In practical engineering, failure modes exhibiting spatiotemporal variability are inherent to the complexities of mechanical systems. However, contemporary analyses of kinematic reliability often overlook the simultaneous impact of spatial parameters, such as input angles, and temporal parameters, such as motion cycles, on the performance of mechanisms. Specifically, motion cycles influence the mechanism's output at various cycles due to joint wear, while input angles affect the output at different positions within each cycle. To address these challenges, this study employs the space-time-dependent outcrossing rate (STOR) method for conducting a space-time-dependent kinematic reliability analysis of motion mechanisms. Initially, a decoupling approach is proposed to isolate motion errors attributable to input angle and wear factors. Subsequently, the STOR method is enhanced to estimate the maximum failure probability, significantly reducing computational demands. Building on this, the Armijo-based adaptive stability transformation method (AASTM) is refined to augment the efficacy of the Hasofer-Lind-Rackwitz-Fiessler (HL-RF) method in identifying the most probable point (MPP). Upon establishing the outcrossing rates, the upper bound of failure probability is efficiently computed through the application of the Gauss-Legendre (GL) quadrature. The precision and effectiveness of the proposed methodology are validated through comparative analysis with the Monte Carlo simulation (MCS) method.

articleTitle: Review on potential application of IoT technologies in transporting radioactive packages
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: The accumulation of spent nuclear fuel has led to an increased demand for the safe transportation of radioactive waste. Howev er, transporting these materials poses unique challenges related to safety and security. The integration of Internet of Things (IoT) technologies shows promise in enhancing the monitoring, tracking, and management of radioactive packages during transit. Despite this potential, there is currently limited explicit mention of IoT technologies specifically applied to the transportation of radioactive packages. This study investigates the potential uses of IoT in the transportation of radioactive packages, with a specific emphasis on real-time monitoring of environmental conditions, radiation levels, and package status. It explores the benefits of IoT-enabled sensors, data analytics, and communication systems in improving safety, efficiency, and regulatory compliance during transportation. The study also addresses challenges such as data security, interoperability, and regulatory frameworks that need to be addressed for effective implementation. By adopting IoT technologies, personnel can effectively mitigate risks, streamline logistics, and ensure the secure transport of radioactive packages.

articleTitle: Failure mode analysis and health management research of helicopter teletype flight control system
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: In order to improve the safety and reliability of the helicopter fly-by-wire system and guarantee flight safety, a helicopter fly- by-wire system health management program is proposed by systematically combing and categorizing typical helicopter failures during the service period, and by studying the causes of the failures in depth. Based on FMEA failure mode analysis, this pap er researches the maintenance strategy, and studies the optimization method of helicopter health management system by analyzing the typical failures, so as to provide theoretical reference and technical support for the safety and reliability o f helicopter fly-by-wire system.

articleTitle: Maintenance decision-making for a two-component buffered serial production system
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: This paper presents a maintenance decision-making model for a two-component serial production system. The Gamma process describes the deterioration process of the component. When the component deteriorates to a preventive maintenance (PM) threshold, the component is restored by PM. When the upstream component is in the PM state, and the downstream component deteriorates to the opportunistic maintenance (OM) threshold, the downstream component is restored by OM. The optimal PM threshold and OM threshold are derived by minimizing the long-run average cost of the system. Finally, a case study and a parameter sensitivity analysis are provided to demonstrate the applicability of the presented model.

articleTitle: Fault diagnosis method of planetary gearbox based on acoustic signal IACCUGRAM-AMSESHIRD
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: To overcome the difficulties in extracting fault features from acoustic signals of planetary gearboxes, this paper introduces a novel fault diagnosis method combining Improved ACCUGRAM (IACCUGRAM) and Adaptive Modified Square Envelope Spectrum Harmonic Interference Ratio Deconvolution (AMSESHIRD). Initially, the feature extraction process in the ACCUGRAM algorithm is refined using an enhanced Gini index. Given the challenge of deconvolution as a non-convex optimization problem prone to local optima, a tailored filter specific to the fault characteristic band identified by IACCUGRAM is developed to initiate the deconvolution process, thus improving efficiency and accuracy in signal interpretation. Additionally, the harmonic interference ratio of the square envelope spectrum is weighted and pre-processed, with the fault period and filter length optimized using a fitness function formulated from a modified smoothness index and a fault characteristic index, optimized through the African Vulture Optimization Algorithm. Deconvolution is then executed using the custom initial filter, pre-optimized criteria, and optimal parameters determined. The final stage involves fault diagnosis of the planetary gearbox through envelope spectrum analysis of the acoustic signal. The effectiveness and superiority of this method are validated through both simulated and experimental signals, with results demonstrating significant improvements over conventional methodologies.

articleTitle: A population-based worst-case localized disruption scenario identification method of interdependent infrastructure systems
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: Infrastructure systems are indispensable to modern societies, underpinning vital services that sustain everyday life. Nevertheless, these systems are intricately interdependent and frequently vulnerable to various hazards, often manifesting as localized disruptions. This study eschews hazard-specific modeling in favor of a worst-case scenario approach to identify the potential for the most severe damage scenario that could precipitate the greatest loss of performance across these interconnected systems. Traditional identification methods primarily assess post-disaster performance based on the operational states of individual components. However, many authoritative reports emphasize the affected population as a significant consequence of such hazards. Addressing this discrepancy, this study proposes a population-based method to identify critical areas whose component disruptions could impact the largest number of people. This model also facilitates the exploration of new types of logical interdependencies, captured through a population-based objective function, thus providing a complementary tool for the disaster management of urban areas. Applied to Tianjin Eco City, the results demonstrate the dynamic nature of disaster consequences, varying with the intensity of disruptions. The study further elucidates the implications of considering interdependencies within road transport systems and offers a comparative analysis of different modeling approaches for attackers and operators.

articleTitle: A weighted multi-scale L1/L2 deconvolution method and its application for bearing fault diagnosis
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: Incipient weak fault diagnosis is is of paramount importance for the secure functioning of rotating equipment. Detecting masked weak fault impulses is challenging due to significant background noise and various interferences. Visual deblurring (BD) stands out as a proficient approach for extracting repetitive transients, but the performance of conventional BD methods is often compromised by strong interferences, such as pronounced harmonics and random impulses. This paper proposes a weighted multi-scale L1/L2 deconvolution (WMSD) method to address these challenges. The WMSD method utilizes the adjustable Q-factor wavelet transform to construct a multi-scale space. In this space, the weights of all scales are determined by power spectrum kurtosis (PSK) to retain the fault characteristic energy, forming the weighted multi-scale space. The scale containing abundant fault characteristic information is identified based on the combined amplitude-weighted PSK. The frequency band of this scale is then used to initialize the L1/L2 deconvolution filter, allowing the deconvolution model to focus on fault characteristic information. The weighted reconstructed signal is subsequently processed using the initialized deconvolution model, and the fault is diagnosed using the envelope spectrum. The resilience and efficiency of the WMSD technique are confirmed by its adept handling of fault signals that exhibit intense harmonic content and considerable erratic impulses.

articleTitle: Research on software task profile modeling technology
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: Research on software task profile modeling technology is conducted from three perspectives. First, the event characteristics of the software task profile are analyzed to identify entry events, exit events, and various intermediate events. Second, the data characteristics of the software are examined to clarify the inputs, outputs, and intermediate variables involved in the task. Third, the event sequence characteristics of the software task profile are analyzed to determine the preconditions, action operations, postconditions, and transfer probabilities of each event sequence. Based on these three aspects of task feature information, a comprehensive software task profile model is constructed.

articleTitle: A parametric approach of computing Taguchi signal-to-noise ratio from incomplete life data
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: The Taguchi method for experimental design is widely utilized to improve product reliability through the systematic arrangement of multiple runs or treatments, each representing a unique combination of factor levels. In such experiments, lifetime data o f sample units are gathered via life tests, which are typically monitored periodically and terminated at a pre-determined endpoint. The resultant data, characterized by small sample sizes, high censorship, and heterogeneity, preclude direct computation of t he Taguchi signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), a crucial measure of robustness used to evaluate the performance of a run. This paper addresses this issue by introducing a parametric approach that begins by constructing a life distribution model for each run through a three-step parameter estimation procedure. It then calculates the SNR from the fitted distribution using SNR expressions derived from typical life distributions discussed herein. The effectiveness and superiority of the proposed method are demonstrated through two real-world examples, underscoring its applicability and potential benefits in enhancing the reliability analysis of complex products.

articleTitle: Multisource dual unsupervised domain adaptation method for remaining life prediction under multiple operating conditions
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: Aero engines, with their complex structures and intricate gas paths, are a crucial component of the aviation system. Traditional machine learning-based methods for predicting the remaining useful life (RUL) of rolling bearings often struggle to provide adequate feature representation and adaptive extraction due to complex operating conditions and challenges in obtaining degradation data. Given that traditional machine learning methods require substantial amounts of labeled data, they frequently fail to yield satisfactory RUL prediction results. To overcome these limitations, domain adaptation methods have been employed, facilitating the transfer of knowledge from a well-labeled source domain to an unlabeled target domain. Additionally, to augment the available data, a multisource domain transfer approach is proposed, which transfers data from multiple source domains to the target domain intended for prediction. To enhance the effectiveness of this multisource domain transfer method, a dual alignment strategy is introduced for aligning features at both the feature and semantic levels, thereby improving predictive performance. The model incorporates a convolutional neural network (CNN) and long short-term memory (LSTM) as its backbone, leveraging CNN's robust feature extraction capabilities combined with LSTM’s proficiency in processing time-dependent data. Experiments conducted on the CMAPSS dataset, along with comparisons and ablation studies against current popular multisource domain adaptation methods, demonstrate the superiority of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Reliability-based multidisciplinary design optimization method under original probability model for wind turbine structure
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: As an optimization strategy considering both uncertainty and discipline coupling, Reliability based Multidisciplinary Design Optimization (RBMDO) has been widely studied. While RBMDO is utilized across various fields, its application and overarching frameworks are scant in the context of wind turbine structures. This study introduces an RBMDO approach tailored for wind turbine structures. The method incorporates a strategy for resolving the Most Probable Point (MPP) issue based on the original probability model, which is particularly useful for addressing challenges encountered when RBMDO relies on the First Order Reliability Method that may result in multiple MPPs. To alleviate the computational demands of RBMDO, collaborative optimization, sequential optimization and reliability analysis are integrated into the methodology. The effectiveness of this approach is demonstrated through the design optimization of a 3 MW onshore wind turbine tower, considering the uncertainties in material properties, load conditions and design variables.

articleTitle: Experimental research on the vibration of aviation elbow tube by 21~35 MPa fluid pressure pulsation
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: The experimental study investigates the vibration responses of aviation elbow tubes under various pressure pulsations, with a focus on different tube layouts. Three sets of tube specimens were designed, each varying in bending position, radius, and angle. Pressure pulsation excitations, characterized by different working pressure levels, amplitudes, and frequencies, were applied to these specimens. The layout parameters were found to affect the stiffness of the tubes both on the Elbow-tube Plane and the Normal Plane. It was observed that the resonance acceleration amplitude is approximately 4 to 8 times greater than that in the non-resonant state, while the resonance stress is about 6 to 14 times higher than in the non-resonant state. Additionally, stress increases by 30% to 70% when the working pressure level in the tube rises from 21 MPa to 35 MPa. An increase in the amplitude of pulsation excitation from 5% to 10% results in acceleration and strain response amplitudes escalating from 55% to 2 times. Notably, when the bending position is centered and the radius is fourtimes the tube's outer diameter, the elbow tube exhibits the largest acceleration and strain responses. Positioning the bending point close to the constrained end and employing alarger bending angle can effectively reduce tube vibration. This research provides valuable insights into the dynamic design of high-pressure aircraft pipeline structures.

articleTitle: Research on integrity management system and key evaluation technology of power station boiler
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
