abstract: The safety of power station boilers, critical thermal components in power generation, has attracted considerable attention due to the harsh operational conditions they endure. This paper introduces integrity management, a prevalent approach in the management of pressure equipment, to enhance the safety management of power station boilers and explores key evaluation technologies pertinent to these boilers. Considering the distinctive characteristics of power station boilers, the integrity management system is structured around four primary facets: organizational structure, documentation system, implementation procedure, and technical system. This study also identifies four principal damage modes that impact seven major pressure - bearing components of utility boilers and proposes qualitative and semi-quantitative risk assessment techniques for these components, based on risk-based inspection (RBI). Moreover, the paper describes an integrity evaluation method that amalgamates testing methodologies with assessments of remaining life. For instance, parameters input for a main steam pipeline made from 12Cr1MoV material indicate a maximum equivalent stress of 57.76 MPa and an estimated residual life of 21.75 years. This research offers substantial insights into enhancing risk prevention and control strategies in power station boilers and encourages further exploration of innovative approaches in safety management.

articleTitle: A novel probabilistic risk analysis approach for engine bird strike issue applied on the airworthiness regulations
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: Bird strikes on aero-engines are a significant factor contributing to aircraft accidents. Airworthiness regulations in various countries impose specific requirements on engine resistance to bird strikes. Currently, the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO), the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) of the United States, and the Civil Aviation Administration of China (CAAC) categorize the severity levels of bird species that pose threats to flight safety based on their weight within the relevant regions. Consequently, this thesis introduces a probabilistic risk assessment method based on bird strike severity levels. Utilizing bird strike data from U.S. civil aviation engines as an example, this study assesses the risk posed by birds of different severity levels in U.S. civil aviation. Through this method, the bird strike risk associated with each weight range specified in FAR 33.76 was quantitatively evaluated. This evaluation confirmed that the risk predictions for large birds in current airworthiness regulations align with the intended safety objectives.

articleTitle: A reliability analysis method based on signed directed graph
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: The Signed Directed Graph (SDG) is a qualitative fault diagnosis method grounded in graph theory, effectively illustrating the relationships between variables in complex systems and elucidating the propagation paths of potential hazards and faults. Renowned for its simplicity in modeling and comprehensive coverage, SDG has been extensively utilized in safety evaluation and fault diagnosis across various fields. Despite its widespread application, the limitations of SDG, particularly its lack of quantitative analysis and the unwieldy size of its models, have become increasingly apparent. To address these challenges, this paper introduces a reliability analysis method that leverages SDG. Initially, a hierarchical approach predicated on accessibi lity is employed to streamline the system's SDG model. Subsequently, quantitative dimensions, including system failure probability and component importance, are integrated into the hierarchical SDG model. The method's feasibility and validity are demonstrated through a case study involving the Safety Injection System (SIS) of a pressurized water reactor nuclear power plant, where a hierarchical SDG model of the SIS is developed and used to conduct a quantitative reliability analysis.

articleTitle: An approach for analyzing IC quality of wafer level based on its circuit probe data set
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: Circuit probe (CP) test data for a wafer encapsulates the comprehensive electrical characteristics of each integrated circuit (IC) chip, making the accurate analysis of this data set crucial for quality control within the semiconductor industry. This paper introduces a novel methodology for analyzing the quality of IC dies based on their CP data set. Initially, a three-dimensional quality matrix, termed wafer_Q_set, is constructed by extracting quality information from the CP test data set. Subsequently, this three-dimensional wafer_Q_set is reduced to two dimensions utilizing fractal theory and transformed into a Comprehensive Quality Spectrum (CQS) through the application of the quality spectrum method. The CQS visually represents the overall quality information of the CP test data set, facilitating qualitative analysis. Finally, the quality information within the CQS is examined quantitatively, enabling a comprehensive analysis of the entire batch of chips and the exploration of potential fault correlations within the data. The effectiveness, accuracy, and efficiency of the proposed approach are validated using a CP data set from an actual IC chip foundry.

articleTitle: Optimal condition-based maintenance decisions for group-replacement multi-component repairable system
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: Multi-component replacement repairable systems refer to systems wherein all critical components are replaced in batches after a given production cycle, while defective parts are taken offline for maintenance before being reused as the system continues to operate. This paper focuses on multi-component replacement repairable systems composed of multiple identical components, defining a grouped replacement and offline condition-based maintenance strategy. The concept of maintenance degree is introduced to indicate the extent of maintenance on a component, and a model is constructed where maintenance effects, costs, and durations are determined by this degree of maintenance. By analyzing the state transition characteristics of the system operating under alternating conditions of operational and replacement components, a steady-state probability model of system degradation is derived. Considering factors such as maintenance time, cost, and effectiveness, an average cost rate model within a finite time frame is established to determine the optimal system replacement period, preventive maintenance thresholds, and degree of maintenance. The correctness and effectiveness of the strategy and model are verified using a seven-roll continuous hot-rolling system as a case study, along with an analysis of parameter sensitivity.

articleTitle: Time-dependent strength reliability analysis of four-link mechanisms based on extreme moment method
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: Strength is crucial in the design of structural and mechanical systems. Although current research predominantly focuses on the structural strength reliability, there is a marked scarcity of studies addressing the strength reliability of mechanical mechanisms. Unlike static structures, the dynamic properties of mechanical systems often evolve over time, complicating the assessment of their strength reliability. Mechanical operations may indeed entail the risk of strength failure. Consequently, this article explores the time-dependent strength reliability of four-link mechanisms. Initially, a finite element model of the four-link mechanism is developed, incorporating the effects of material properties and applied loads on the dynamic behaviour of the mechanism. Subsequently, a time-dependent reliability method predicated on extreme moments is introduced to calculate the strength reliability of four-link mechanisms. This involves evaluating the fractional moments of stress extremes using the rotational quasi-symmetric point method (RQ-SPM) and determining extreme responses from quasi-symmetric points via Kriging. Furthermore, employing the maximum entropy method (MEM), constrained by fractional moments and extreme responses, the probability density function (PDF) of stress extremum is derived, allowing for the calculation of strength reliability through PDF integration. The efficacy and precision of this approach are corroborated by the Monte Carlo method and a double-loop Kriging surrogate model method, confirming the method's high efficiency and accuracy.

articleTitle: Failure analysis and preventive maintenance of high-power flexible clutch systems
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: Clutches are essential components in automobiles and other power transmission systems. Flexible clutch systems, known for their superior qualities such as shock resistance, vibration resistance, and reliable operation under weightless conditions, are extensively utilized in various industries, including machinery, maritime, and oil extraction. This paper examines the component composition and working principles of each sub-system within the flexible clutch system. By analyzing fault information for the overall system and employing the fault tree analysis method, we identify the basic events leading to the failure of each sub-system and construct a fault tree model for the flexible clutch system. To address failures within the flexible clutch system, we develop a maintenance cost model based on component categories. By comparing the importance of preventive maintenance costs, we determine the optimal order for preventive maintenance of each system component. Finally, two strategies are employed to simulate the degree of importance, demonstrating the high flexibility of this measure.

articleTitle: Optimization of dynamic characteristics of a dual power split transmission system
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: The Runge-Kutta method was utilized to solve the load sharing coefficients and dynamic load coefficients of a coaxial twinrotor dual power split transmission system. Employing a multi-objective optimization method with a genetic algorithm, the optimal solution set and Pareto frontier diagram for each stage clearance combination was obtained, using the load sharing coefficient and dynamic load coefficient of each stage as optimization objectives. The research revealed that the scatter plot shows a spatial curve composed of the two objective functions, with a relatively uniform distribution of points. Consequently, the results of this optimal set encompass most of the optimal solutions, offering higher accuracy, a broad range of adaptability, and superior global performance.

articleTitle: Analysis of stress influencing factors in the spring tube screw connection assembly of electro-hydraulic servo valve
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: The armature assembly of the electro-hydraulic servo valve, featuring the spring tube as its core component, is essential for converting torque into displacement with high precision. During operation, the spring tube, in conjunction with the armature baffle assembly, undergoes micro-bending due to swinging motions, significantly affecting the mechanical properties and assembly quality, which in turn impacts the dynamic and static performance of electro-hydraulic servo valves. This paper investigates the evolution of stress and strain in the spring tube screw connection assembly under various operational conditions. The study begins with a simulation of the assembly process of the spring tube to determine the stress distribution patterns under different preload conditions. Concurrently, a comprehensive analysis of the stress relaxation characteristics of the spring t ube material is performed, along with an evaluation of the reliability of the predicted performance indicators for the spring tub e screw connection assembly under room temperature storage conditions.

articleTitle: A feature extraction enhancing-based LSTM integrated deep learning model for remaining useful life prediction
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: The prediction of Remaining Useful Life (RUL) for complex engineering systems is crucial for maintaining their safety and reliability. To address the issue of limited RUL prediction accuracy due to inadequate extraction of degradation features in these systems, this paper presents an innovative RUL prediction method that integrates residual dilated causal convolution and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks. This approach employs residual connections to stack multiple dilated causal convolutions, facilitating the deep extraction of degradation features and enhancing the feature learning process. Additionally, it incorporates LSTM structures to forge a linkage between the degradation features and RUL, thereby enabling accurate RUL prediction for complex engineering systems. To validate the efficacy of the proffered method, experimental validation was conducted using the NASA public dataset C-MAPSS, and a comparative analysis was performed against the results of existing mainstream methods. The experimental results demonstrate that the suggested approach significantly enhances the precision of RUL estimation for complex engineering systems.

articleTitle: Remaining useful life prediction of high voltage relays based on performance degradation information
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: Considering the challenges associated with limited performance degradation data and low prediction accuracy for high-voltage relays in new energy vehicles, this paper proposes a residual life prediction method that incorporates data cleaning and the Wiener process. In this approach, the contact resistance measured during the on-off test of a high-voltage relay serves as the input variable. Standard deviation and mean filtering techniques are employed to identify and remove anomalous data. The independence and normality of the degradation increments are assessed using statistical tests, and the parameters of the Wiener process model are estimated through the maximum likelihood method. The point at which the contact resistance of the relay first reaches a predetermined threshold is considered the end of product life, and the remaining life is predicted based on this failure threshold. Utilizing the performance degradation data of a high-voltage relay and employing the mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) as a metric, the practicability and effectiveness of the proposed method are demonstrated.

articleTitle: A survey of automatic target recognition technology based on multi-source data fusion
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: With the rapid advancement of big data, the Internet of Things, and artificial intelligence, informatization, and intelligent warfare have become central themes in modern conflict. Warfare has evolved from traditional methods to unmanned and intelligent operations, such as swarming and wolf-pack tactics, presenting significant challenges for the development of new-era combat systems and intelligent unmanned platforms. Military ground unmanned platforms leverage their scalability to incorporate various measuring instruments and sensors, thereby broadening their application to meet diverse combat requirements. Currently, the most prevalent and significant application of these platforms is in the reconnaissance and identification of targets, systematic threat evaluation, casualty avoidance, and enhancement of combat personnel's battlefield survival rates. Consequently, both domestic and international scholars have increasingly focused on developing various Automatic Target Recognition (ATR) technologies, with extensive research dedicated to ATR based on multi-source data fusion. To elucidate the current state of research, this paper provides a detailed review of various multi-source data fusion algorithms and automatic target recognition algorithms, offering insights and future research directions.

articleTitle: Research on standardization of nuclear robots
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: With the burgeoning integration of robot technology into the nuclear industry, the standardization of nuclear robots has emerged as a pivotal issue. The standardization is critical for ensuring the safety, efficiency, and sustainable development of nuclear energy. This paper presents a systematic analysis of the classification, functionality, and evolutionary landscape of nuclear robots globally. An in-depth discourse on the specific demand for standardization within the nuclear sector is provided, elucidating the structural framework of standard system and levels of standards. Furthermore, the paper puts forward implementation strategies and suggestions for standardization construction of nuclear robots. This study provides theoretical support and practical guidance for the standardization construction of nuclear robots, which is of great significance to promote the healthy development of nuclear robots and improve the safety level and operational efficiency of the nuclear industry.

articleTitle: Optimal burn-in and warranty design for heterogeneous population subject to stochastic degradation
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: In practice, product heterogeneity is commonplace. Burn-in processes are extensively utilized to screen out weak products from heterogeneous batches before delivery to customers, proving to be an effective strategy for enhancing product reliabilit y and reducing warranty costs. This study introduces a model that integrates burn-in procedures with warranty policies for a heterogeneous product population, where the degradation processes are modeled using a general degradation path. We propose utilizing shock as a method of burn-in and offer a renewable warranty for products that survive this process upon delivery to customers. Initially, a novel shock-based burn-in model is developed, and the effects of shock are analyzed concerning population characteristics. Subsequently, a cost model is formulated to determine the optimal magnitude of shock that minimizes the total expected cost. The optimal sale price, warranty period, shock magnitude, and replacement threshold level are calculated to maximize expected profit. An illustrative example is provided to demonstrate the application of the model.

articleTitle: T-S fuzzy dynamic fault tree analysis based on expert comprehensive assessment
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: The T-S dynamic fault tree (DFT) effectively models the dynamic failure behaviour of systems through the application of the T-S dynamic gate rule. However, obtaining failure data for components within high-reliability systems often presents a significant challenge. To enhance the T-S DFT's capability to address uncertain events, this paper introduces the T-S fuzzy dynamic fault tree (FDFT) analysis method, grounded in comprehensive expert assessments. This approach aggregates the evaluations from various experts regarding the likelihood of each fault event within the system and converts these assessments into quantitative interval fuzzy data. Subsequently, these interval fuzzy numbers are incorporated into the T-S dynamic gate input and output rule algorithm of the T-S DFT. This integration facilitates the determination of the system’s failure occurrence probability over time, as well as the probabilistic importance and critical importance of each failure cause. The feasibility of this method is demonstrated through a case study involving the bogie-bearing system of a moving train set. This method provides a robust foundation for fault analysis and maintenance of high-reliability systems where fault data are scarce.

articleTitle: Autonomous underwater vehicles hull shape resistance prediction and multi-objective optimization using CFD
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: The development of Autonomous Underwater Vehicles (AUVs) has become a priority for numerous countries. Achieving low drag and high efficiency in these vehicles is essential for enhancing their endurance. To effectively reduce energy consumption and improve navigation durability, a parametric Myring shape model was established, and the Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) method was employed to predict flight resistance at cruising speed. The accuracy and reliability of the CFD method were subsequently verified. A surrogate model was then constructed to optimize hydrodynamic performance, with optimal space filling applied for sample sampling to generate a nonparametric regression response surface. This surface was optimized using a multi-objective optimization algorithm, resulting in a 9.5% reduction in drag while maintaining sufficient volume, given constant overall length and diameter.

articleTitle: Buckling reliability and sensitivity analysis of a composite stiffened panel with high-dimensional uncertainties
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: This paper presents an uncertainty analysis of composite stiffened panels with high-dimensional input parameters, encompassing reliability assessment and sensitivity analysis. Initially, a finite element model is developed. Subsequently, the uncertain parameters influencing the mechanical properties of the stiffened panels are identified, and finite element simulations are conducted. Following the simulation, various surrogate models are established and compared for accuracy, with results indicating that the high-dimensional surrogate model KDIC exhibits superior fitting accuracy. Finally, the probability of failure is computed, and a local sensitivity analysis (LSA) is performed to evaluate the influence of the input parameters.

articleTitle: Robust parameter design of latent variable Gaussian process model based on mixed input variables
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: As for the problem of robust parameter design with qualitative and quantitative mixed input variables in the additive manufacturing process, a new optimization scheme is proposed based on the latent variable Gaussian process model. Firstly, the experimental data of mixed input variables are generated by maximum projection design. The part entities are obtained by 3D printing experiments. The response values of the target quality characteristics are collected by experiments. Then, each qualitative factor is mapped to potential numerical variables, and a Gaussian process model of mixed input latent variables i s constructed. Finally, considering the uncertainty of response, an optimization model is established, and the differential evolution algorithm is used to find the best factor design in the parameter space. The paper show that the method can scientifically express the relationship between qualitative factors. At the same time, it can effectively deal with the problems of meta-modeling and robust parameter design with mixed input variables.

articleTitle: A review of order-ratio-based fault feature extraction techniques for planetary gearboxes
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: The vibration signals of planetary gearboxes are non-smooth, presenting challenges for signal processing methods that have made significant progress in analyzing smooth vibration signals. However, methods based on order-ratio analysis excel in processing non-smooth vibration signals. This paper evaluates the advantages and disadvantages of signal processing methods based on order-ratio analysis. Firstly, the basic principles of order-ratio analysis and its current development trends are summarized. Secondly, the paper reviews the advancements of order-ratio analysis methods in vibration signal analysis. Finally, the study discusses future developments and challenges in the field of fault diagnosis for planetary gearboxes.

articleTitle: Ship collision situation assessment based on GA-BP and HMM
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: To proactively identify collision risks in ship navigation and enhance maritime traffic safety, a novel method for evaluating ship collision risk status using GA-BP and HMM algorithms is introduced. Initially, an analytic hierarchy process is employed to develop a ship collision risk assessment model. Subsequently, historical trajectory data of ships along with pertinent environmental information are leveraged to train the BP and its optimization algorithm, enhancing the prediction accuracy for potential ship collisions. Furthermore, the HMM model is utilized to evaluate ship encounter situations. The results demonstrate that this approach significantly improves the accuracy and reliability of ship collision risk assessments, providing critical decision-making support to shipping companies and crew members in scenarios of collision risk.

articleTitle: Multi-objective optimization design for step-stress accelerated degradation testing based on Wiener process
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: This paper presents a multi-objective optimization approach for step-stress accelerated degradation testing (SSADT), overcoming the constraints associated with single-objective optimization in practical scenarios. Initially, the degradation path of a product is modeled using a Wiener process. A multi-objective optimization model is then developed, which simultaneously considers three objectives while adhering to a predefined total experimental budget. The particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm is utilized to identify the optimal test plan within this framework. The efficacy of the propose d approach is validated through a series of experiments using LED lamps as examples.

articleTitle: A novel method for rolling bearing fault diagnosis based on multi-domain feature extraction and particle swarm algorithm optimised support vector machine (PSO-SVM)
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: As a vital component of rotating machinery, the accurate fault diagnosis of rolling bearings is crucial to maintaining project continuity, minimizing economic losses, and ensuring safety. This document introduces an innovative method for diagnosing faults in rolling bearings, utilizing a blend of multi-domain feature extraction and PSO Support Vector Machine (PSO-SVM).This method integrates the time domain, frequency domain, and wavelet packet energy features of vibration signals to construct a comprehensive feature library that enhances sensitivity and classification accuracy. The PSO-SVM model classifies these fault features, with the particle swarm algorithm optimizing the parameters automatically and the support vector machine providing robust interpretability. To validate the effectiveness of the proposed method, tests were conducted using both open-source and laboratory data. Gaussian noise was introduced to the vibration signals to replicate complex operational conditions. The diagnostic accuracy of this model was then benchmarked against traditional SVM and Genetic Algorithm-Back Propagation (GA-BP) models. Evidence shows the technique's high accuracy, sturdiness, sturdiness, and resilience, making it suitable for diagnosing faults in rolling bearings.

articleTitle: Structure eigenfrequency adjusting using topology optimization with granular material model
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: Topology optimization has emerged as a significant focus in structural design, renowned for its capacity to meet the demands for high strength, increased stiffness, and minimized weight. The structure of granular materials often displays tension and compression asymmetry similar to biological structures, providing a compelling explanation for the mechanical properties observed in certain biological systems. Optimizing the micro-scale constitutive structure through topology optimization facilitates the attainment of structures exhibiting biological anisotropy. This paper employs the parametric level set method to refine the eigenfrequencies and specific gaps between eigenfrequencies of granular material stru ctures, thereby eliminating the issue of zigzag boundaries in final topologies and ensuring the creation of optimal structures with smooth boundaries. The constitutive relationship of granular materials is formulated by correlating the forces and displacements among spherical granules. A mathematical framework for topology optimization is developed using radial basis function-based parametric level sets. The robustness of this method is substantiated through benchmark problems in topology optimization, exam ining the influence of the tension-compression asymmetry factor on eigenfrequency adjustments. Analysis of the final topologies confirms the reliability and s of the mathematical approach for topology optimization.

articleTitle: An adaptive sampling method for generating boundary scenarios of UAV swarms based on Gaussian process regression
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: In the field of autonomous system testing, the dynamic and interactive nature of multi-agent systems, such as UAV swarms, poses substantial challenges for effective testing and validation. Traditional boundary scenario generation techniques struggle to comprehensively identify boundary scenarios in UAV swarm testing, primarily due to the sparsity and complexity inherent in high-dimensional scenario spaces. To overcome these limitations, this paper proposes an adaptive sampling process that is guided by a Gaussian Process Regression (GPR) surrogate model. This method leverages predictive insights from the surrogate model to dynamically adjust the balance between exploring and exploiting the scenario space, aiming to identify critical transition areas in UAV swarm performance. By focusing on distinguishing boundary scenarios that demarcate distinct performance modes, this approach optimises testing efficiency and deepens the understanding of UAV swarm behavior under varied operational conditions. The efficacy of this novel method in testing complex autonomous unmanned systems is validated through a series of simulation experiments involving UAV swarm search tasks.

articleTitle: A review of state assessment and RUL prediction methods for equipment based on acoustic signal
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: This paper explores the integration of acoustic signals within the field of Prognostics and Health Management (PHM), particularly focusing on the evaluation of equipment states and the prediction of their remaining useful life. Acoustic signals offer the benefits of non-contact data acquisition and provide comprehensive information, making them increasingly relevant in PHM research. By conducting an extensive review of the literature, this study presents a systematic overview of methodologies related to acoustic fault diagnosis, health state assessment, and remaining life prediction. Furthermore, it highlights the current challenges and outlines prospective research avenues. This review aims to serve as a valuable resource for both researchers and practitioners aiming to enhance the application of acoustic signals in PHM.

articleTitle: Research on the reliability modeling and assessment method of solar unmanned aerial vehicle power system considering balancing requirements
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: The power system of a solar-powered Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) is a critical component that necessitates extremely high reliability. Traditionally, reliability in such systems is ensured by incorporating redundancy units to meet performance requirements. The conventional approach for evaluating reliability employs the K/N system model. However, this model only accounts for the number of units and neglects the impact of spatial distribution and balancing requirements, leading to inaccuracies. In this study, we introduce a balanced system model which has multi states to evaluate the reliability of a solar-powered UAV. Based on the operational principles of the power system and integrating two different load-sharing principles, we propose three system re-balancing mechanisms and establish a power system reliability model that considers balancing requirements. Finally, we evaluated the reliability of the power system using finite Markov chain approach (FMCA), which significantly enhances the accuracy of the evaluation.

articleTitle: Transfer fault prognosis of bearing across different machines with the application of negative transfer mitigation
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: Accurately predicting the remaining useful life (RUL) of rolling element bearings is essential for maintaining the reliable operation of mechanical assets. Many existing research endeavours focus on utilizing domain adaptation (DA) techniques to predict RUL across variable operating conditions within the identical machine fleets. However, this oversimplified approach may limit the applicability and prediction accuracy in real industrial settings. While DA can address domain shifts between different machines or conditions, it also has the risk of the negative transfer, which can significantly compromise the effectiveness of transfer learning (TL)-based prognostic methodology. A dual network comprising a deep convolutional neural network (DCNN) and a multi-layer perceptron (MLP) is proposed for a more challenging and realistic scenario, i.e., transfer RUL prediction between the heterogeneous rolling bearings. Additionally, a negative transfer mitigation (NTM) scheme is integrated within the DA module for mitigating negative transfer. Finally, experiments conducted on two publicly available bearing datasets highlight the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed model.

articleTitle: Research on thermal characteristics diagnosis method of aviation hydraulic pump
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: The safety and reliability of hydraulic systems are critical to the overall flight safety of aircraft. Fault diagnosis technology for hydraulic pumps plays a vital role in ensuring their operational safety. Traditionally, the maintenance of aviation hydraulic pumps has relied on hydraulic oil testing and temperature monitoring. However, these methods often suffer from poor diagnostic accuracy and a lack of timeliness. This study introduces an infrared technology diagnostic approach to detect fault characteristics in aviation hydraulic pumps. By utilizing the thermal characteristics of aviation hydraulic pumps for infrared diagnosis, this method collects temperature field data to establish status labels and incorporates neural networks to facilitate intelligent diagnosis. The study utilizes infrared data from the casing of a hydraulic pump belonging to a specific airline to construct and validate an intelligent diagnosis model through case studies. The findings indicate that this method achieves a diagnostic accuracy of up to 95%, providing valuable insights for enhancing existing diagnostic strategies and offering technical support and a theoretical foundation for improving the reliability of hydraulic pumps and ensuring flight safety.

articleTitle: A bibliometric analysis and hotspot discussion of container multimodal transport in China based on CiteSpace
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: Since the mid-20th century, with the vigorous development of globalization and the continuous improvement of the international trade system, container multimodal transport has gradually become the mainstream mode of international cargo transportation. This paper aims to provide a comprehensive overview of the current research status of container multimodal transport in China by examining publications from the China National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI) spanning from January 1, 2000, to April 1, 2024. Utilizing CiteSpace software, a visual analysis of the annual publication volume and key terms was conducted, highlighting the research hotspots and developmental trends in this domain. The findings suggest that the study of container multimodal transport has increasingly gained popularity within China in recent years. Based on these insights, the paper identifies three future research directions: the iterative upgrading of optimization algorithms under multi-objective and multi-scenario conditions of the entire process, the development of intelligent container multimodal transport systems, and the exploration of multimodal transport from the perspective of green logistics. This analysis aims to chart the developmental trajectory and current status of container multimodal transport, providing valuable guidance for future academi c research and robust theoretical support for industry practice.

articleTitle: Reliability-based design optimization of offshore wind turbine support structure considering pile-soil coupling effect
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: The significant portion of the overall capital costs of wind turbine projects attributed to the tower and support structure necessitates that the wind power industry implements optimization strategies that ensure reliability while minimizing costs. This paper presents a reliability design optimization method for offshore wind turbine support structures that incorporates the impact of pile-soil coupling. The method begins with parametric finite element modeling of monopile support structures and foundations for offshore wind turbines, considering both pile-soil coupling and the combined effects of wind and wave forces. Subsequently, the constraints in the optimization design for reliability are represented through a surrogate model that corre lates the full parameters of the finite element model with the structural response. These constraints encompass modal frequency, stress, strain, buckling, variable range, and the reliability index. Ultimately, a lightweight design is realized by harmoniz ing these multiple constraints, thus meeting the reliability standards prescribed by turbine design criteria.

articleTitle: Defect size estimation of rolling bearing life cycle based on envelope analysis and BPNN
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: A life cycle defect size estimation method for rolling bearings based on envelope analysis and a BPNN is presented to accurately evaluate the degree of bearing damage. The method begins with pre-whitening, band-pass filtering, and Hilbert transform applied to the original vibration signal, which allows for precise identification of the rolling element's entry and exit from the defect area, followed by defect size estimation. Subsequently, the RMS value of the bearing vibration signal is extracted and used as the input for training the BP neural network, with the estimated defect size as the output. This process establishes a mapping relationship between the RMS value and the defect size. Finally, the trained neural network predicts the defect size for the enti re lifecycle of the bearing. This approach not only improves the accuracy of defect size estimation but also offers a new perspective for analyzing defect evolution and predicting the lifespan of bearings.

articleTitle: Finishing milling parameter optimization based on Isight
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: The surface quality of products, such as the servo power supply bracket from solid rocket engines machined by integral milling, often exhibits instability, necessitating the optimization of milling finishing parameters. To tackle this issue, th is research utilizes the optimal Latin hypercube sampling method within the multidisciplinary optimization software, Isight. Initially, finite element simulation experiments are conducted to ascertain the coefficient of variation (CV) of the milling force of the tool and the surface roughness (Ra) of the material under various milling parameter combinations. Subsequently, radial basis function neural network (RBF) and Kriging methods are employed to construct surrogate models for the milling parameters, as well as for the milling force CV and material surface roughness Ra. Finally, the study utilizes the archival micro-genetic algorithm (AMGA) for multi-objective optimization of the surrogate models, facilitating the iterative calculation and identification of optimal milling finishing parameters.

articleTitle: Modeling and wear analysis of aircraft flap self-lubricating bearing
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: Wear of self-lubricating bearings in aircraft flaps is a significant contributor to bearing failure. Despite this, research into the wear characteristics of these bearings under real-world mechanical conditions is scant. This study introduces a wear analysis method for aircraft flap self-lubricating bearings that accounts for actual coupled variable load conditions. Initially, a contact stress distribution model based on conformal contact theory is developed for self-lubricating gaskets. This model incorporates both axial and radial coupling loads affecting the bearings. The contact stress on the self-lubricating gasket is then determined using finite element simulation, and the accuracy of this model is validated under pure radial load conditions. Subsequently, the wear quantity of the self-lubricating bearing is calculated employing the modified Archard model, based on the specific wear form observed. From this analysis, a life prediction model for the aircraft flap self-lubricating bearing is constructed. Furthermore, the study includes an examination of a self-lubricating bearing that has undergone 50,000 aircraft take-offs and landings using a Scanning Electron Microscope (SEM). This research provides a solid theoretical foundation for predicting the service life of aircraft flap self-lubricating bearings and for a detailed analysis of their wear characteristics.

articleTitle: AI-driven optimization in nuclear reactor core operations: advances in prediction, management, and fault diagnosis for enhanced safety
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: The application of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in nuclear reactor core management offers significant enhancements in efficiency, safety, and performance. AI-driven methods, including Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs), Genetic Algorithms (GA), and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), optimize fuel loading patterns, power distribution, and core parameters, addressing complex optimization challenges. This paper reviews advancements in AI applications within reactor core management, highlighting successes in automating and refining processes traditionally dependent on manual calculations. Implementations of AI optimize fuel reload patterns, enhance safety margins, and more effectively manage the nuclear fuel lifecycle, thereby contributing to operational efficiency and sustainability. Future directions for AI integration focus on predictive maintenance, advanced modeling, and next-generation reactor design optimization.

articleTitle: A reliability optimization method of motion mechanism based on multi-source cost factors
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: Addressing the overlooked aspect of reliability costs in optimizing motion mechanisms, this paper introduces a multidimensional reliability cost coefficient evaluation system that encompasses machining cost, assembly difficulty, operational load characteristics, and working environment. Utilizing this framework, a comprehensive assessment function for meta-analysis under multiple cost factors is constructed, accompanied by a reliability optimization model. The process begins with the employment of Low-Rank Approximate sensitivity analysis to allocate reliability to specific motion mechanisms. This model is then used to optimize the results of reliability allocation. The findings reveal that the proposed method markedly reduces reliability costs while satisfying the design reliability requirements.

articleTitle: Quality evaluation for wind turbine design by an uncertain HoQ
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: This research evaluates the quality of a wind turbine design project using a House of Quality (HoQ) with uncertainties. The Verification and Validation (V&V) model encompasses the entire design trajectory, facilitating the structuring of the HoQ. It elucidates aspects of blade and generator design, manufacturing procedures, and laboratory tests. This paper explores a scenario where the Quality Features (QFs) within the HoQ follow a Gaussian distribution. Analytical solutions for adjusted relative weights of Engineering Characteristics (ECs) are obtained through traditional and calibrated Delta methods. Monte Carlo (MC) simulations demonstrate that this scenario results in normally distributed weights for the ECs. When compared to the traditional Delta method, the analytical solution obtained using the calibrated method aligns more closely with numerical solutions. Furthermore, mean value analyses from the HoQ advocate for prioritising enhancements in generator design to reach optimal design quality. This investigation expands upon the conventional HoQ by incorporating uncertainties, thereby significantly enriching the quality quantification framework for wind turbine design.

articleTitle: Remaining life prediction of automotive high voltage relay based on LSTM
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: As an essential component of new energy vehicles, the lifespan of automotive high-voltage relays directly impacts the reliability and driving safety of automotive electrical and electronic products. This paper presents a methodology for predicting the lifespan of automotive high-voltage relays. To address the significant noise issues, present in the measured high-voltage relay parameters from experimental data, this study proposes the use of a wavelet analysis algorithm for parameter pre-processing. A standard one-dimensional convolutional neural network (CNN) algorithm is initially employed to conduct lifespan prediction experiments for high-voltage relays. Additionally, considering the temporal characteristics of the actual degradation data, a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network algorithm is utilized to extract these temporal features for more accurate lifespan prediction. To fully verify the performance of these two algorithms in predicting the lifespan of high-voltage relays, comparative experiments and analyses were conducted using root-mean-square and other errors as evaluation metrics. The results demonstrate that the LSTM network significantly outperforms the CNN in this application.

articleTitle: Research on automatic fault tree construction for nuclear power plants
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: The PSA model is a crucial industry tool for understanding and evaluating the safety of nuclear power plants. Given the complexity of nuclear systems, the development and maintenance of such models are highly time-consuming and labor-intensive tasks. This paper proposed a fault tree generation method tailored to the nuclear power plants. Utilizing P&IDs and FMEA as inputs, the method applied a tracing algorithm to automatically construct fault trees. Additionally, for special cases in nuclear power plants, such as reverse flow tracing, branch isolation failure handling, and common cause failure group generation, specific solutions were provided. In the final section, we introduced an automatic fault tree modeling tool, AutoFAT, which is characterized by its user-friendly interface and high level of automation. We imported the automatically constructed fault trees into the reliability analysis software RiskSpectrum PSA and compared them to manual modeling results, which showed a time savings of over 70% for modeling individual top events and a translation accuracy of over 90%. Specifically, accuracy was evaluated by comparing basic events, CCF events, calculated top event unavailability, and the minimal cut sets. It is believed that the application of AutoFAT will facilitate PSA modeling, model maintenance and model review.

articleTitle: A novel Modelica-based reliability modelling approach for electric propulsion systems
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: The electric propulsion system of a ship represents a quintessential electromechanical system, the reliability of which is crucial to assess. This paper introduces a novel approach for modeling the reliability of electric propulsion systems using the Modelica language, designed to overcome the shortcomings of traditional reliability modeling methods that often fail to account for the heterogeneity, dynamicity, and interactivity inherent in electric propulsion systems. This approach utilizes multi-domain modeling to address system heterogeneity, employs parametric modeling to capture environmental dynamics, and facilitates device interactions through the connectors provided by the Modelica language. Additionally, modeling efficiency is enhanced through the reuse of the device model packages. An electric propulsion system from a specific vessel is used as a case study to demonstrate the modeling process and simulation results, validating the effectiveness and adaptability of the proposed method. This approach introduces a novel tool for the reliability modeling of complex electromechanical systems, thereby enhancing the precision and efficiency of system reliability assessments.

articleTitle: Analysis of key dynamic parameters for typical scenarios of sloca based on RISMC method
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: Given the inherent uncertainties in the design of nuclear power plants (NPPs), it is essential to incorporate an appro priate safety margin. The Risk-Informed Safety Margin Characterization (RISMC) method integrates both deterministic and probabilistic approaches to identify typical sequences through dynamic characteristic analysis. Key dynamic parameters are determined based on a combination of probabilistic safety analysis, deterministic safety analysis, engineering judgment, and an evaluation of the design characteristics of nuclear power plants, with their uncertainty distributions calculated to support the RISMC coupling model. Utilizing the HPR1000 NPP as a case study, this paper examines and identifies typical sequences that exhibit a higher risk of Small Loss of Coolant Accidents (SLOCA). These sequences are analyzed to ascertain the key dynamic parameters within the RISMC analysis method. The findings provide a reference for determining essential dynamic parameters in future applications of the RISMC method.

articleTitle: Reliability modelling and confidence limit estimation of electric multiple unit incorporating mixed distributed likelihood ratio
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: The Electric Multiple Unit (EMU) is a sophisticated asset renowned for its high reliability. The implementation of advanced health management technology can enhance the operational reliability and safety of EMUs. Preventive replacement interval planning, a key aspect of EMU lifetime management, requires significant investment in funds, manpower, and resources. However, it has the potential to substantially reduce maintenance management expenses and improve the profitability of EMU operations. This paper introduces a method for estimating reliability confidence limits for EMUs under multi-stage maintenance scheduling to extend replacement maintenance cycles. By employing the mixed distribution model as a two-level foundational framework, the point estimates of the fundamental model are determined using the EM algorithm, and the confidence intervals of the mixed distribution model are assessed through likelihood ratio statistics. A practical case study utilizing actual EMU data demonstrates the feasibility of extending preventive replacement cycles and validates the rationality of the model.

articleTitle: Improved combinatorial optimization model for vessel scheduling in constrained channel ports
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: Vessel scheduling, which assigns time and space resources to vessels, is crucial for the safety of waterborne transportation and directly influences the efficiency of waterborne logistics systems. This paper proposes a systematic solution to the Multiple Legs and Multiple Navigation Modes Vessel Scheduling Problem (ML&MM-VSP) in the port region. First, a generalized framework for ML&MM-VSP is proposed, adaptable to different port layouts. Secondly, the original VSP model is simplified, and the constraint conditions are refined. The model sets total scheduling time and vessel delay time as two objectives while considering the characteristics of the waterway and vessel attributes as constraints. Thirdly, a Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II) is employed to solve the problem, aiming to identify optimal vessel scheduling strategies. Lastly, empirical analysis is conducted to verify the rationality and effectiveness of both the proposed model and the adopted algorithm, and comparative experiments are carried out to test ML&MM-VSP with different layouts. The results show that the proposed model performs better than the original models and can provide more effective guidance for ML&MM-VSP practice.

articleTitle: Competing failure modeling and analysis of phased-mission unmanned aerial vehicles
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) can be outfitted with ground sensors to offer substantial benefits across a range of applications. Nonetheless, ensuring their reliability in delivering services throughout the designated mission time remains crucial. UAV integrated systems are typically phased-mission systems, which undergo multiple, consecutive, non-overlapping operational phases, each with unique system configurations and component behaviors due to changing tasks and environmental conditions. Components within UAV-integrated systems exhibit statistical dependencies across phases. Furthermore, UAV-integrated systems usually employ relayed communications, where some UAVs (dependent components) rely on other UAVs (relays) to communicate with the base station. If the relay fails, dependent components may increase transmission power to establish a direct link with the base station, but only for a limited and uncertain duration until their power is depleted below the necessary threshold. The competition between isolation and propagated failures is also considered. This paper proposes a combinatorial reliability modeling methodology for phased-mission UAVs subject to competition and random isolation time. The methodology applies to arbitrary types of time-to-failure and time-to-isolation distributions for components. A detailed case study demonstrates the approach. The correctness of the proposed method is verified through Monte Carlo simulations.

articleTitle: Holo-balancing method of flexible rotors based on multi-objective differential search algorithm
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: The rotor is a critical component of rotating machinery, often experiencing high amplitude vibrations caused by unbalance. Therefore, achieving efficient and accurate dynamic balancing of rotors is essential for effective monitoring and maintenance . Traditional optimization algorithms for dynamic balancing have several limitations. For instance, the vibration data obtained from a single sensor cannot adequately represent the overall vibration of the system, and the balancing objectives are often too narrow. This paper addresses the dynamic balancing of flexible rotors using multi-objective intelligent optimization. Leveraging the comprehensive information extraction capabilities of the holospectrum, three metrics are selected to evaluate the balancing state of the rotor: the average value, the maximum value, and the extreme difference of residual vibration. An optimal evaluation function for multiple targets is introduced to resolve the coordination issues among these three metrics. To enhance the efficiency and accuracy of dynamic balancing, an improved differential search algorithm, E2-S-DSA, is proposed. Balancing experiments demonstrate that this method achieves a vibration reduction ratio of 85.3%, further verifying the reliability and practical value of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Research on high-low cycle fatigue damage of aircraft engine blades based on numerical simulation
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: In response to the complex alternating loads that aircraft engine blades endure and their vulnerability to fatigue damage, a study was undertaken to investigate high-low cycle composite fatigue damage through numerical simulation. The initial phase of the research involved analyzing the characteristics of high-low cycle composite fatigue loading, which encompassed uncertainties, load histories, and variations in geometric parameters. This analysis aimed to elucidate the behaviors and damage mechanisms of the blades. Subsequently, the study applied continuum damage mechanics to explore the interplay between high-cycle fatigue and low-cycle fatigue, including their combined effects. This theoretical exploration resulted in the development of a constitutive equation specifically for high-low cycle composite fatigue damage in engine blades. Additionally, a finite element model for aircraft engine blades was constructed, facilitating both static and dynamic analyse s through finite element analysis software. This model allowed for the assessment of stress field distribution and vibration characteristics under various operational conditions. These insights offer critical theoretical support and methodological guidance for enhancing the design and extending the lifespan of aircraft engine blades, thereby improving engine safety and reliability.

articleTitle: An intelligent cloud monitoring system for multiple 3D printers based on IoT
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: In the Industry 4.0 era, 3D printing has become a cornerstone of intelligent manufacturing, necessitating precise real-time monitoring and control to ensure efficiency and quality. This research developed an IoT-based cloud monitoring system for 3D printers to enhance remote monitoring and control capabilities. The system collects real-time sensor data on parameters such as temperature and humidity, along with live video feeds. These multimodal data are pre-processed at the edge and further analyzed in the cloud. Users can monitor the 3D printing status via a custom visual interface and adjust parameters based on data analysis to optimize printing quality. To evaluate the system's effectiveness, experiments were conducted to explore the relationship between process parameters and surface roughness and to optimize the printing process and quality using the Taguchi design of experiments. Five factors were considered: nozzle temperature, bed temperature, printing speed, layer height, and ambient temperature. The significant printing process factors were identified, and optimal factor levels were determined to enhance print quality. The experimental results demonstrated that the system can significantly improve the quality and response speed of 3D printing process monitoring. Additionally, it enhances the reliability and user experience of 3D printing.

articleTitle: Fault diagnosis of multi-sensor oil system of road header based on convolution neural network
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: To address the limitations of single-sensor data in providing comprehensive and multidimensional insights into the oil systems of tunneling machines during long-term operations, we propose a fault diagnosis method based on convolutional neural networks (CNNs). Firstly, oil monitoring methods assess the performance and condition of the oil by analysing its physical an d chemical properties, as well as the information carried by wear particles. This approach is unaffected by environmental noise and directly extracts optimal features from the oil data without the need for preliminary data conversion or manual feature extraction. Subsequently, the data collected from multiple sensors are utilized as input to the CNN, enabling the diagnosis o f faults in the oil system. Finally, we compare the fault state classification accuracy of our method with that of other machin e learning methods. The experimental results demonstrate that the diagnostic accuracy of our proposed method surpasses that of competing methods, thereby achieving efficient diagnostic performance.

articleTitle: Prostate cancer diagnosis using resampling technology and extra trees
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: Prostate cancer represents a significant health concern for middle-aged and elderly men in China, where both incidence rates are climbing and detection and treatment methodologies trail behind those of Western countries. This study aims to enhance the diagnostic and treatment processes for prostate cancer through the application of machine learning techniques. The research concentrates on enriching and equilibrating medical datasets using the Extra Trees prediction model. A comparative analysis confirms the effectiveness of this model in developing a robust diagnostic model for prostate cancer, thus supporting clinical decision-making. The study is divided into three main areas: first, machine learning techniques are applied to address missing values in prostate cancer datasets, with various approaches including Extra Trees and optimized ensemble algorithms assessed for effectiveness. Secondly, a strategy to balance datasets with mixed features is explored, particularly focusing on correcting imbalances in diagnostic outcomes, with random oversampling noted to enhance diagnostic precision. Finally, a diagnostic model based on the Extra Trees classifier is constructed and benchmarked against alternative algorithms and pertinent studies, establishing its suitability for prostate cancer diagnosis.

articleTitle: Reliability assessment of unmanned aircraft combat effectiveness based on improved ADC analysis method
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: To evaluate the effectiveness and reliability of ground attack missions of combat UAVs, this paper ad opts an improved ADC method, distinct from the traditional ADC approach that relies on a vague and complex capability index C. The innovation in this study involves method enhancement and model reconstruction, resulting in a redefined capability matrix C. To validate the feasibility of the improved model, three typical combat UAVs—MQ-9B, XQ-5, and XQ-58—are selected for assessment. By integrating the combat process and analyzing evaluation indices, the effectiveness evaluation index system and corresponding capability expression formula are established. Employing the hierarchical analysis method, weight coefficients are assigned t o each capability indicator, and the effectiveness assessment results of each UAV are synthesized to verify the method's feasibility. The assessment reveals that the X-47B exhibits high operational effectiveness reliability in ground attack missions (0.7194), whereas the MQ-9 (0.6351) and XQ-58 (0.5174) demonstrate areas for improvement in electronic countermeasures and ground attack capabilities. The improved ADC model presented in this paper can be utilized for the effectiveness evaluation and index analysis of various combat UAVs, providing theoretical support for the research, development, and enhancement of UAV equipment. Furthermore, the method of constructing corresponding expressions for each capability index C can be applied to the effectiveness evaluation of other weapons, enabling a more comprehensive parameter of weapon effectiveness to be obtained .

articleTitle: Radar software reliability test case intelligent generation based on domain knowledges
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: Due to a lack of expertise in the radar field and intelligent technology, testers typically rely on their personal experience and knowledge to generate reliable test cases. This approach is highly subjective and lacks objectivity, leading to a substantial workload and low efficiency in software reliability testing. Additionally, the absence of a test profile construction method oriented towards task reliability makes it difficult to fully identify weak links that affect the completion of system tasks. To address this problem, this paper proposes a new approach for radar software reliability test profile construction using intelligent test-case generation technology. First, a test profile construction technology oriented towards task reliability is introduced. Next, a radar domain knowledge dictionary is constructed to facilitate text segmentation of test data based on domain knowledge. Then, leveraging the LDA (Latent Dirichlet Allocation) topic model, a deep learning algorithm, and cosine distance, the intelligent reuse and generation of radar software reliability test cases based on semantic similarity is achieved. Finally, case studies of radar data processing software and radar control software are conducted. The results demonstrate that the proposed approach outperforms three classic intelligent algorithms in terms of the reliability test case reuse accuracy rate (P) and recall rate (R), with the accuracy rate (P) increased by at least 10.04% and the recall rate (R) increased by at least 14.94%.

articleTitle: A multi-source information fusion method for multi-level performance index evaluation
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: Maintaining equipment performance at specified levels is crucial for optimizing operational effectiveness, necessitating mult-level performance index evaluations. Currently, performance evaluations often confront challenges related to data insufficiency, necessitating the comprehensive utilization of multi-source data and consequently leading to issues in multi-source information fusion for performance assessment. This paper addresses these challenges by analyzing perf ormance index systems and proposing a multi-source information fusion framework, which encompasses four stages: data collection, quantification, assessment, and fusion. Utilizing a cognitive cross-entropy approach, the paper determines data value weights, setting forth multi-level evaluation criteria and a quantitative reference for the long-term performance of stored equipment. Additionally, it introduces the minimum cross-entropy solution method and the statistical characteristic parameter method for scenarios characterized by sufficient and insufficient data, respectively, based on these data value weights. To demonstrate and validate the feasibility of this approach, a case study involving bolt torque reduction is presented.

articleTitle: Incremental learning based intelligent fault diagnosis of rolling bearings
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: Deep Learning (DL) algorithms excel in identifying bearing failures, but their dependence on large amounts of high-quality data renders them unsuitable for many real-world industrial applications. Additionally, as data is continuously obtained, it can change or new failure types can emerge over time. Consequently, models capable of Incremental Learning (IL) are required to adapt to evolving industrial settings. To address these challenges, this paper integrates Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) with Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) for Intelligent Failure Diagnosis (IFD) of bearings. Furthermore, an IL method is incorporated to mitigate the issue of catastrophic forgetting in streaming data scenarios. The IFD model lever ages PSO to optimize the CNN structure rather than obtaining optimal weights, thereby achieving superior performance in fault recognition. The integrated IL method employs knowledge distillation and replay techniques to minimize forgetting as data gradually includes new failure classes. Various IL algorithms are evaluated under simulated real-world conditions, demonstrating a reduction in catastrophic forgetting. The proposed method proves to efficiently adapt to changes and learn new failure modes, outperforming existing methodologies while reducing computational time.

articleTitle: Risk-informed time margin analysis for operators in main control room of nuclear power plant
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: Nuclear reactor safety is crucial for the sustainable development of nuclear energy and the utilization of clean energy. This paper proposed a comprehensive framework for analyzing nuclear power plant accidents by integrating Risk-Informed Safety Margin Characterization (RISMC) with Human Reliability Analysis (HRA). It dynamically assessed Human Error Probability(HEP) by considering the continuous distribution of factors such as required time and available time for tasks. Unlike the static appr oach of the Standardized Plant Analysis Risk-Human Reliability Analysis (SPAR-H), this study introduced the concept of time margin to replace available time and established a distribution function for time margin-PSF. The integrated approach of coupling HRA with the RISMC method was applied to analyze Medium Break Loss of Coolant Accident (MLOCA). It utilized RELAP5 program for system simulation and risk analysis of key parameters within discrete intervals, combined with HEP, to evaluate Probability Safety Margin (PSM).The results indicated that, compared to existing safety analysis methods, the approach proposed in this paper adequately characterizes the distribution characteristics of available time for personnel actions and the time req uired for these actions. The probability of accident sequences, risk levels, and sequence consequences will significantly change with time margin, thereby affecting probabilistic safety margin. By incorporating human factor uncertainties into the PSM value, it is possible to reduce the reliance on expert judgment and conduct risk analysis from a more realistic perspective.

articleTitle: Characteristics exploration of human and organizational factors in maritime traffic accidents
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: This paper introduces a reliable analytical methodology designed to delve into the characteristics of human-organizational factors (HOFs) in maritime traffic accidents along China's coastal waters and uncover the causal chains of critical accident HOFs. By collecting 811 relevant accident reports from the China Maritime Safety Administration (CMSA) database, the frequency of HOFs occurrence across different accident reports was statistically analyzed. Employing co-word clustering analysis, a co-occurrence relationship map was constructed, and cluster analysis and visualization analysis of HOFs were performed. Subsequently, the Human Factors Analysis and Classification System (HFACS) model was applied to analyze the accident causes, extracting the salient features of maritime traffic accidents and HOFs. Furthermore, complex network theory was utilized to explore the interconnected pathways within the HOFs network of maritime traffic accidents by analyzing the key nodes and edges of the network. The analysis results indicate that the primary HOFs contributing to maritime vessel traffic accidents are negligent lookout, poor safety awareness, and failure to implement safety management responsibilities. Based on the HFACS model, 235 HOFs and 3 causal pathways were identified, with "ineffective education and training - failure to implement safety management responsibilities - failure to use safe speed - poor safety awareness" being the most critical causal pathway for HOFs-related accidents. These findings can serve as a reference for relevant authorities to formulate targeted measures to prevent maritime traffic accidents along China's coastal waters and enhance maritime safety management.

articleTitle: An elevator trapping fault warning method based on self-attention-LSTM
publicationTitle: 14th International Conference on Quality, Reliability, Risk, Maintenance, and Safety Engineering (QR2MSE 2024)
abstract: Due to the complexity of elevator structures and the numerous components involved, prolonged operation often leads to entrapment faults. However, current handling methods predominantly rely on post-incident rescue efforts and lack proactive preventive measures. To achieve autonomous and accurate predictions of elevator entrapment faults, we propose a predictive model integrating a Long Short-Term Memory Neural Network (LSTM), a Self-Attention Mechanism, and the Adaptive Moment Estimation Algorithm (Adam). This model leverages extensive IoT and historical data from elevators. Initially, we conduct thorough data analysis, followed by data cleaning and normalization, ensuring a robust foundation through weig hted screening. Subsequently, we construct an LSTM-based model, enhanced by a self-attention mechanism layer to improve performance. The model is then optimized using the Adam algorithm. Ultimately, this approach enables precise early warnings for elevator entrapment faults. Experimental results indicate that, with a learning rate of 0.001, the model achieves optimal training results, reducing the model loss rate to 0.125%, and achieving better parameter fitting. The warning model demonstrates a considerable accuracy rate in predicting elevator entrapment scenarios.
